title.en: Volume 71: Pei Shuye, Xiahou Daoqian, Li Yuanhu, Xi Fayou, Wang Shibi, Jiang Yuezhi, Chun Yudan, Li Miao
title.raw: 卷71 裴叔業 夏侯道遷 李元護 席法友 王世弼 江悦之 淳于誕 李苗 Volume 71: Pei Shuye, Xiahou Daoqian, Li Yuanhu, Xi Fayou, Wang Shibi, Jiang Yuezhi, Chun Yudan, Li Miao

sentences.zh: 裴叔業 夏侯道遷 李元護 席法友 王世弼 江悅之 淳于誕 李苗

translations.literal: Pei Shuye, Xiahou Daoqian, Li Yuanhu, Xi Fayou, Wang Shibi, Jiang Yuezhi, Chunyu Yan, Li Miao
translations.idiomatic: Biographies of Pei Shuye, Xiahou Daoqian, Li Yuanhu, Xi Fayou, Wang Shibi, Jiang Yuezhi, Chunyu Yan, and Li Miao

sentences.zh: 裴叔業，河東聞喜人也。

translations.literal: Pei Shuye was a man of Wenxi in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Shuye was from Wenxi in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 魏冀州刺史徽之後也。

translations.literal: He was a descendant of Hui-zhi, Governor of Ji Province in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He traced his line to Pei Hui-zhi, who had served as Governor of Ji Province under Wei.

sentences.zh: 五代祖苞，晉秦州刺史。

translations.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor Bao was Governor of Qin Province under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Five generations back, his ancestor Bao had been Governor of Qin Province in the Jin dynasty.

sentences.zh: 祖邕，自河東居于襄陽。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yong moved from Hedong to settle in Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yong had left Hedong and made his home in Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 父順宗、兄叔寶仕蕭道成，並有名位。

translations.literal: His father Shunzong and elder brother Shubao served Xiao Daocheng, and both attained fame and rank.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shunzong and elder brother Shubao had served under Xiao Daocheng and both won distinction and office.

sentences.zh: 叔業少有氣幹，頗以將略自許。

translations.literal: Shuye in youth had spirit and capacity, and rather prided himself on military stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Shuye showed force of character and considered himself something of a strategist.

sentences.zh: 仕蕭賾，歷右軍將軍、東中郎將諮議參軍。

translations.literal: He served Xiao Ze, passing through the posts of General of the Right Army and Staff Adviser to the General Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xiao Ze he rose through the ranks to General of the Right Army and staff adviser to the General Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 蕭鸞見叔業而奇之，謂之曰：「卿有如是志相，何慮不大富貴。

translations.literal: Xiao Luan saw Shuye and marveled at him, saying to him: "You have such a countenance of ambition—why worry that you will not attain great wealth and honor?"
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Luan met Shuye he was struck by the man and told him, "With a bearing like yours, what could keep you from the highest honors?"

sentences.zh: 深宜勉之。

translations.literal: You should strive deeply for it.
translations.idiomatic: You ought to press on with all your might.

sentences.zh: 」鸞為豫州，引為司馬，帶陳留太守。

translations.literal: When Luan was in Yuzhou, he brought him in as Marshal and concurrently made him Administrator of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: When Luan took charge of Yuzhou he appointed Shuye marshal and let him hold the concurrent post of Administrator of Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 鸞輔政，叔業常伏壯士數百人於建業。

translations.literal: When Luan held the regency, Shuye regularly kept several hundred stalwart men hidden in Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: While Luan acted as regent, Shuye kept several hundred armed men concealed in Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 及鸞廢昭文，叔業率眾赴之。

translations.literal: When Luan deposed Zhaowen, Shuye led his followers to join him.
translations.idiomatic: When Luan deposed Emperor Zhaowen, Shuye marched his men to his support.

sentences.zh: 鸞之自立也，以叔業為給事黃門侍郎，封武昌縣開國伯，食邑五百戶。

translations.literal: When Luan established himself, he made Shuye Attendant-in-Ordinary at the Yellow Gate, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Wuchang with an estate of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Once Luan had seized the throne he named Shuye Attendant-in-Ordinary at the Yellow Gate, created him Marquis of Wuchang, and granted him an estate of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 高祖南巡，車駕次鍾離。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu made a southern tour, and the imperial carriage halted at Zhongli.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen toured the south, the court encamped at Zhongli.

sentences.zh: 鸞拜叔業持節、冠軍將軍、徐州刺史，以水軍入淮。

translations.literal: Luan appointed Shuye Bearer of the Staff, General Who Establishes Valor, and Governor of Xuzhou, and sent him with a river fleet into the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Luan commissioned Shuye as Bearer of the Staff, General Who Establishes Valor, and Governor of Xuzhou, and ordered his naval force into the Huai.

sentences.zh: 去王師數十里，高祖令尚書郎中裴聿往與之語。

translations.literal: Several tens of li from the royal army, Gaozu ordered Master of Writing Pei Yu to go and speak with him.
translations.idiomatic: When he was still several tens of li from the imperial army, Emperor Xiaowen sent Master of Writing Pei Yu to parley with him.

sentences.zh: 叔業盛飾左右服玩以夸聿曰：「我在南富貴正如此，豈若卿彼之儉陋也。

translations.literal: Shuye richly adorned the attire and trinkets of those about him to boast to Yu, saying: "My wealth and honor in the south are just like this—how could they compare with your plainness over there?"
translations.idiomatic: Shuye dressed his attendants in lavish finery to impress Yu and said, "This is how prosperous I am in the south—nothing like your shabby northern court."

sentences.zh: 」聿云：「伯父儀服誠為美麗，但恨不晝遊耳。

translations.literal: Yu said: "Uncle, your ceremonial dress is indeed beautiful, but it is a pity you cannot parade by day."
translations.idiomatic: Yu replied, "Your robes are splendid, Uncle—but what a pity you may only wear them at night."

sentences.zh: 」徙輔國將軍、豫州刺史，屯壽陽。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General Who Assists the State and Governor of Yuzhou, and garrisoned Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was then moved to General Who Assists the State and Governor of Yuzhou, with his headquarters at Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 鸞死，子寶卷自立，遷叔業本將軍、南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: When Luan died, his son Baojuan established himself, and Shuye was moved to his former generalship and made Governor of Southern Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Luan's death his son Baojuan seized power and transferred Shuye to his old rank as general and to the governorship of Southern Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 會陳顯達圍建鄴，叔業遣司馬李元護率軍赴寶卷，其實應顯達也。

translations.literal: When Chen Xianda besieged Jiankang, Shuye sent his marshal Li Yuanhu to lead troops to Baojuan, but in truth to aid Xianda.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Xianda laid siege to Jiankang, Shuye sent his marshal Li Yuanhu with troops nominally to rescue Baojuan but in fact to side with Xianda.

sentences.zh: 顯達敗而還。

translations.literal: Xianda was defeated and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Xianda was defeated and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 叔業慮內難未已，不願為南兗，以其去建鄴近，受制於人。

translations.literal: Shuye feared that internal troubles were not ended and did not wish to hold Southern Yanzhou, because it was near Jiankang and he would be subject to others' control.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye worried that civil strife was not over and did not want Southern Yanzhou, since its proximity to Jiankang would leave him at the court's mercy.

sentences.zh: 寶卷嬖人茹法珍、王咺之等疑其有異，去來者並云叔業北入。

translations.literal: Baojuan's favorites Ru Fazhen, Wang Xuanzhi, and others suspected he had other intentions; travelers all said Shuye was going north to enter Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Baojuan's favorites Ru Fazhen and Wang Xuanzhi grew suspicious, and everyone coming and going reported that Shuye meant to defect north to Wei.

sentences.zh: 叔業兄子植、颺、粲等，棄母奔壽陽。

translations.literal: Shuye's brother's sons Zhi, Yang, and Can and others abandoned their mother and fled to Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: His nephews Zhi, Yang, and Can left their mother behind and fled to join him at Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 法珍等以其既在疆埸，急則引魏，力不能制，且欲羈縻之，白寶卷遣中書舍人裴長穆慰誘之，許不復回換。

translations.literal: Fazhen and the others, because he was already on the frontier and in urgency would summon Wei and they lacked strength to control him, yet wished to restrain him, told Baojuan to send Palace Attendant Pei Changmu to comfort and entice him, promising no further transfer.
translations.idiomatic: Fazhen and his circle, unable to rein him in on the border where he might call in Wei at any crisis, persuaded Baojuan to send Pei Changmu to soothe him with a pledge that his post would not be changed again.

sentences.zh: 叔業雖云得停，而憂懼不已，遣親人馬文範以自安之計訪之於寶卷雍州刺史蕭衍曰：「天下之事，大勢可知，恐無復自立理。

translations.literal: Although Shuye was said to have been allowed to remain, his worry and fear did not cease; he sent his kinsman Ma Wenfan to inquire of Baojuan's Governor of Yongzhou Xiao Yan about a plan for his own security, saying: "Affairs under Heaven—the great trend can be known; I fear there is no longer any prospect of standing on our own."
translations.idiomatic: Though officially allowed to keep his command, Shuye's anxiety never lifted. He sent his kinsman Ma Wenfan to ask Xiao Yan, Governor of Yongzhou, how he might secure himself: "The tide of events is clear—the south can hardly stand alone any longer."

sentences.zh: 雍州若能堅據襄陽，輒當勠力自保；

translations.literal: If Yongzhou can firmly hold Xiangyang, I will at once join forces to preserve ourselves;
translations.idiomatic: If you can hold Xiangyang firmly, I will join you in defending ourselves;

sentences.zh: 若不爾，回面向北，不失作河南公。

translations.literal: if not, turning to face north, I would not fail to become Duke of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: otherwise, by turning north I can still hope to become Duke of Henan."

sentences.zh: 」衍遣文範報曰：「羣小用事，豈能及遠。

translations.literal: Yan sent Wenfan to reply: "Petty men hold power—how can they reach far?"
translations.idiomatic: Yan sent Wenfan back with this answer: "Petty courtiers are in charge—they cannot see beyond their noses."

sentences.zh: 多遣人相代，力所不辦；

translations.literal: If they send many men to replace you, your strength cannot manage it;
translations.idiomatic: Send too many replacements and you cannot resist them;

sentences.zh: 少遣人，又於事不足。

translations.literal: if they send few, that too is insufficient for the affair.
translations.idiomatic: send too few and you lack the force you need.

sentences.zh: 意計回惑，自無所成。

translations.literal: Their schemes are confused and will accomplish nothing on their own.
translations.idiomatic: Their plans are muddled—they will achieve nothing by themselves.

sentences.zh: 唯應送家還都以安慰之，自然無患。

translations.literal: You should only send your family back to the capital to reassure them, and naturally there will be no trouble.
translations.idiomatic: You should send your family back to the capital to reassure the court, and you will have no trouble.

sentences.zh: 若意外相逼，當勒馬步二萬直出橫江，以斷其後，則天下之事一舉可定也。

translations.literal: If unexpectedly pressed, you should muster twenty thousand horse and foot to strike straight out at Hengjiang and cut off their rear—then affairs under Heaven can be settled in one move.
translations.idiomatic: If they force your hand, march twenty thousand horse and foot straight to Hengjiang and cut them off from behind—the realm could be decided in a single stroke.

sentences.zh: 若欲北向，彼必遣人相代，以河北一地相處，河南公寧復可得？

translations.literal: If you wish to turn north, they will surely send men to replace you and allot you one place north of the river—how could Duke of Henan still be obtained?
translations.idiomatic: If you turn north they will replace you and park you with some petty fief north of the river—do you really think you would still be made Duke of Henan?

sentences.zh: 如此，則南歸之望絕矣。

translations.literal: Thus the hope of returning south would be cut off.
translations.idiomatic: That would end any hope of your returning to the south."

sentences.zh: 」叔業沉疑未決，遣信詣豫州刺史薛真度，具訪入國可否之宜。

translations.literal: Shuye, sunk in doubt and undecided, sent a messenger to Governor of Yuzhou Xue Zhendu to inquire fully whether entering Wei was feasible.
translations.idiomatic: Still unable to decide, Shuye sent to Xue Zhendu, Governor of Yuzhou on the Wei side, to ask whether defecting to Wei was the right course.

sentences.zh: 真度答書，盛陳朝廷風化惟新之美，知卿非無款心，自不能早決捨南耳。

translations.literal: Zhendu answered in a letter, lavishly setting forth the court's renewed civilizing beauty, knowing you are not without sincere intent, only that you could not early decide to abandon the south.
translations.idiomatic: Zhendu wrote back praising the court's renewal and assuring him that his goodwill was understood—only that he had not yet been able to break with the south in time.

sentences.zh: 但恐臨迫而來，便不獲多賞。

translations.literal: But I fear if you come only when pressed, you will not obtain great reward.
translations.idiomatic: But if you wait until you are driven to it, you may not win such generous rewards."

sentences.zh: 叔業遲遲數反，真度亦遣使與相報復。

translations.literal: Shuye delayed and wavered several times; Zhendu also sent envoys to exchange messages with him.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye hesitated and changed his mind repeatedly while Zhendu kept sending messengers back and forth.

sentences.zh: 乃遣子芬之及兄女夫韋伯昕奉表內附。

translations.literal: Then he sent his son Fenzhi and his elder brother's daughter's husband Wei Boxin to present a memorial submitting to inner allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: At last he sent his son Fenzhi and his brother's son-in-law Wei Boxin with a memorial offering submission to Wei.

sentences.zh: 景明元年正月，世宗詔曰：「叔業明敏秀發，英款早悟，馳表送誠，忠高振古，宜加褒授，以彰先覺。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Jingming, Emperor Shizong decreed: "Shuye is bright, keen, and outstanding; his heroic sincerity was early awakened; he rushed a memorial to offer loyalty—his devotion towers above antiquity. He should receive enhanced reward to manifest his foresight."
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Jingming year 1, Emperor Xuanwu decreed: "Shuye is brilliant and far-sighted; he saw early where loyalty lay and sent his pledge of allegiance—devotion that puts the ancients to shame. Let us reward him fittingly and honor one who chose wisely in advance."

sentences.zh: 可使持節、散騎常侍、都督豫雍兗徐司五州諸軍事、征南將軍、豫州刺史，封蘭陵郡開國公，食邑三千戶。

translations.literal: He may be made Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant at the Leisurely Riders, Commander-in-Chief of military affairs of the five provinces Yu, Yong, Yan, Xu, and Si, General Who Conquers the South, and Governor of Yuzhou; enfeoffed as Duke of Lanling with an estate of three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant at the Leisurely Riders, commander of armies in Yu, Yong, Yan, Xu, and Si, General Who Conquers the South, and Governor of Yuzhou, and created Duke of Lanling with an estate of three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 」又賜叔業璽書曰：「前後使返，有敕，想卿具一二。

translations.literal: He also bestowed on Shuye an imperial letter saying: "Envoys have come and gone; there were orders—I trust you know them in detail."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also sent Shuye a sealed letter: "Our envoys have shuttled back and forth with my orders—you know the gist of them."

sentences.zh: 寶卷昏狂，日月滋甚，虐遍宰輔，暴加戚屬，淫刑既逞，朝無孑遺，國有瓦解之形，家無自安之計。

translations.literal: Baojuan is benighted and mad, day by day growing worse; cruelty reaches all ministers, violence falls on kin; licentious punishments have run their course, the court has not a survivor, the state has the form of disintegration, families have no plan for their own safety.
translations.idiomatic: Baojuan grows more deranged by the day—he tortures his ministers, brutalizes his kin, and lets lawless punishments run wild until no one in court is left standing; the state is coming apart and no household can feel safe.

sentences.zh: 卿兼茲智勇，深具禍萌，翻然高舉，去彼危亂。

translations.literal: You combine wisdom and courage, deeply perceive the sprout of disaster, and loftily turned away from that peril and chaos.
translations.idiomatic: You saw the danger with both wisdom and courage and boldly turned from that sinking realm.

sentences.zh: 朕興居在念，深嘉乃勳。

translations.literal: In rising and resting I keep you in mind and deeply commend your merit.
translations.idiomatic: You are in my thoughts waking and sleeping, and I deeply honor what you have done.

sentences.zh: 前即敕豫州緣邊諸鎮兵馬，行往赴援。

translations.literal: Earlier I already ordered the garrison troops of the border posts of Yuzhou to march to your aid.
translations.idiomatic: I have already ordered the border garrisons of Yuzhou to march to your relief.

sentences.zh: 楊大眼、奚康生鐵騎五千，星言即路；

translations.literal: Yang Dayan and Xi Kangsheng with five thousand iron cavalry set out as if by starlight;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Dayan and Xi Kangsheng are already on the road with five thousand armored horsemen;

sentences.zh: 彭城王勰、尚書令肅精卒十萬，絡繹繼發。

translations.literal: Prince of Pengcheng Xie and Chief Minister Xiao Su with a hundred thousand picked troops follow in continuous streams.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xie of Pengcheng and Chief Minister Xiao Su follow with a hundred thousand elite troops in an unbroken stream.

sentences.zh: 將以長驅淮海，電擊衡巫。

translations.literal: They will long-drive through Huaihai and strike Heng and Wu like lightning.
translations.idiomatic: They will sweep the Huaihai in a long drive and strike like lightning at the Yangzi barrier.

sentences.zh: 卿其并心勠力，同斯大舉。

translations.literal: You should join hearts and combine strength in this great undertaking.
translations.idiomatic: Join your strength to ours in this great campaign.

sentences.zh: 殊勳茂績，職爾之由，崇名厚秩，非卿孰賞？

translations.literal: Extraordinary merit and lush achievement will be yours to claim; lofty name and thick rank—if not you, whom shall we reward?
translations.idiomatic: Outstanding deeds will be yours to claim, and lofty rank—who else deserves such reward?

sentences.zh: 并有敕與州佐吏及彼土人士，其有微功片效，必加褒異。」

translations.literal: There are also orders to your provincial aides and the gentlemen of that land: whoever has the slightest merit will surely receive special praise."
translations.idiomatic: I have also commanded that your staff and the local gentry receive honors for even the smallest service."

sentences.zh: 軍未渡淮，叔業病卒，年六十三。

translations.literal: The army had not yet crossed the Huai when Shuye died of illness, aged sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Before the army could cross the Huai, Shuye died of illness at the age of sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 李元護、席法友等推叔業兄子植監州事。

translations.literal: Li Yuanhu, Xi Fayou, and others pushed Shuye's brother's son Zhi to oversee provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuanhu, Xi Fayou, and the others installed Shuye's nephew Zhi to govern the province.

sentences.zh: 乃贈開府儀同三司，餘如故。

translations.literal: He was then posthumously given the title of Grand Master with Golden Seal and Triple Staff; the rest remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Master with Golden Seal and Triple Staff; his other honors stood unchanged.

sentences.zh: 諡忠武公，給東園溫明祕器、朝服一襲、錢三十萬、絹一千匹、布五百匹、蠟三百斤。

translations.literal: He was given the posthumous title Duke of Loyal Valor, with the secret funerary vessels of the Eastern Garden, one set of court robes, three hundred thousand cash, a thousand bolts of silk, five hundred bolts of cloth, and three hundred jin of wax.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Duke of Loyal Valor and granted imperial funerary regalia, a set of court robes, three hundred thousand cash, a thousand bolts of silk, five hundred of cloth, and three hundred jin of wax.

sentences.zh: 子蒨之，字文聰。

translations.literal: His son Qianzhi, style Wencong.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qianzhi, courtesy name Wencong.

sentences.zh: 仕蕭鸞為隨郡王左常侍，先卒。

translations.literal: He served Xiao Luan as Left Regular Attendant to the Prince of Suizhou and died first.
translations.idiomatic: He had served Xiao Luan as Left Regular Attendant to the Prince of Suizhou and died before his father.

sentences.zh: 子譚紹封。

translations.literal: His son Tan inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tan inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 譚，粗險好殺，所乘牛馬為小驚逸，手自殺之。

translations.literal: Tan was coarse, fierce, and fond of killing; if the ox or horse he rode was slightly startled and bolted, he killed it with his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: Tan was brutal and bloodthirsty—if a mount shied even slightly, he killed it himself.

sentences.zh: 然孝事諸叔，盡於子道，國祿歲入，每以分贍，世以此稱之。

translations.literal: Yet he served his uncles filially to the full measure of a son's way; each year's income from the state stipend he divided to support them—the age praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he treated his uncles with filial devotion and shared his annual stipend among them, for which people praised him.

sentences.zh: 世宗以譚及高皇后弟貞、王肅子紹俱為太子洗馬。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong made Tan, the Empress Gao's brother Zhen, and Wang Suo's son Shao all Masters of Writing for the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu appointed Tan, Empress Gao's brother Zhen, and Wang Suo's son Shao as Masters of Writing for the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 肅宗踐祚，轉員外常侍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong ascended, he was transferred to Regular Attendant Outside the Sequence.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong came to the throne he was made Regular Attendant Outside the Sequence.

sentences.zh: 遷輔國將軍、中散大夫。

translations.literal: He was moved to General Who Assists the State and Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General Who Assists the State and Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈平南將軍、豫州刺史，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made General Who Pacifies the South and Governor of Yuzhou; posthumous name Jing.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the South and Governor of Yuzhou, with the posthumous name Jing (Reverent).

sentences.zh: 子測，字伯源，襲。

translations.literal: His son Ce, style Boyuan, inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ce, courtesy name Boyuan, inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 歷通直散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: He passed through the post of Regular Attendant at the Leisurely Riders Direct Communication.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Regular Attendant at the Leisurely Riders Direct Communication.

sentences.zh: 天平中，走於關西。

translations.literal: In the Tianping era he fled to Guanxi.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianping era he fled west of the passes.

sentences.zh: 蒨之弟芬之，字文馥。

translations.literal: Qianzhi's younger brother Fenzhi, style Wenfu.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhi's younger brother Fenzhi, courtesy name Wenfu.

sentences.zh: 長者，好施，篤愛諸弟。

translations.literal: A man of mature character, fond of giving, he deeply loved his younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: He was a man of steady character, generous by nature, and devoted to his brothers.

sentences.zh: 仕蕭鸞，歷位羽林監。

translations.literal: He served Xiao Luan, passing through the post of Supervisor of the Feathered Forest.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xiao Luan he rose to Supervisor of the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 入國，以父勳授通直散騎常侍，上蔡縣開國伯，食邑七百戶。

translations.literal: Upon entering Wei, by his father's merit he was given Regular Attendant at the Leisurely Riders Direct Communication, made Baron of Shangcai with an estate of seven hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: After defecting to Wei he was made Regular Attendant at the Leisurely Riders Direct Communication and Baron of Shangcai with seven hundred households, in recognition of his father's service.

sentences.zh: 除廣平內史，固辭不拜。

translations.literal: He was appointed Interior Minister of Guangping but firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was offered the post of Interior Minister of Guangping but firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 轉輔國將軍、東秦州刺史，在州有清靜之稱。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General Who Assists the State and Governor of Eastern Qinzhou; in the province he had the reputation of quiet purity.
translations.idiomatic: He was made General Who Assists the State and Governor of Eastern Qinzhou, where he won a reputation for clean and tranquil rule.

sentences.zh: 入為征虜將軍、太中大夫。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as General Who Captures Barbarians and Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court as General Who Captures Barbarians and Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 徙封山茌縣。

translations.literal: His enfeoffment was moved to Shanzhi county.
translations.idiomatic: His fief was transferred to Shanzhi county.

sentences.zh: 出為後將軍、岐州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as Rear General and Governor of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Rear General and Governor of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 正光末，元志西討隴賊，軍敗退守岐州，為賊所圍。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhengguang, Yuan Zhi campaigned west against the Long bandits; the army was defeated and retreated to hold Qizhou, and was besieged by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Zhengguang, Yuan Zhi marched west against the Long rebels, was defeated, and fell back to Qizhou, where the rebels besieged him.

sentences.zh: 城陷，志與芬之並為賊擒送於上邽，為莫折念生所害。

translations.literal: When the city fell, Zhi and Fenzhi were both seized by the bandits and sent to Shanggui, where they were killed by Mo Zhe Niansheng.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, Zhi and Fenzhi were captured and sent to Shanggui, where Mo Zhe Niansheng had them killed.

sentences.zh: 贈平東將軍、青州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously made General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 子涉，字仲昇，襲。

translations.literal: His son She, style Zhongsheng, inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son She, courtesy name Zhongsheng, inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子僑尼，襲。

translations.literal: His son Qiaoni inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qiaoni inherited.

sentences.zh: 武定中，員外羽林監。

translations.literal: In the Wuding era, Attendant Outside the Sequence in the Feathered Forest.
translations.idiomatic: During Wuding he served as Attendant Outside the Sequence in the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，爵例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, his rank was reduced by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi took the throne his title was reduced according to custom.

sentences.zh: 芬之弟簡之、英之，並早卒。

translations.literal: Fenzhi's younger brothers Jianzhi and Yingzhi both died early.
translations.idiomatic: Fenzhi's younger brothers Jianzhi and Yingzhi both died young.

sentences.zh: 英之弟藹之，字幼重。

translations.literal: Yingzhi's younger brother Aizhi, style Youzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhi's younger brother Aizhi, courtesy name Youzhong.

sentences.zh: 性輕率，好琴書。

translations.literal: By nature light and rash, he loved the zither and books.
translations.idiomatic: He was impulsive by nature and devoted to music and literature.

sentences.zh: 其內弟柳諧善鼓琴，藹之師諧而微不及也。

translations.literal: His wife's younger brother Liu Xie was skilled at playing the zither; Aizhi took Xie as teacher but fell slightly short.
translations.idiomatic: His brother-in-law Liu Xie was an accomplished lutenist; Aizhi studied under him but never quite matched him.

sentences.zh: 歷通直散騎侍郎，平東將軍，安廣、汝陽二郡太守。

translations.literal: He passed through Regular Attendant at the Leisurely Riders Direct Communication, General Who Pacifies the East, and Administrator of the two commanderies Anguang and Ruyang.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Regular Attendant at the Leisurely Riders Direct Communication, General Who Pacifies the East, and Administrator of Anguang and Ruyang.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 叔業長兄子彥先，少有志尚。

translations.literal: Shuye's elder brother's son Yanxian in youth had aspiration and principle.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye's nephew Yanxian showed ambition from youth.

sentences.zh: 叔業以壽春入國，彥先景明二年逃遁歸魏。

translations.literal: When Shuye entered Wei with Shouchun, Yanxian in the second year of Jingming fled and returned to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuye surrendered Shouchun to Wei, Yanxian fled south but returned to Wei in Jingming year 2.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉之，除通直散騎常侍，封雍丘縣開國子，食邑三百戶。

translations.literal: The court commended him and appointed him Regular Attendant at the Leisurely Riders Direct Communication, enfeoffed as Viscount of Yongqiu with an estate of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised his loyalty and made him Regular Attendant at the Leisurely Riders Direct Communication and Viscount of Yongqiu with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 出為趙郡太守，為政舉大綱而已。

translations.literal: He went out as Administrator of Zhao commandery; in government he set forth only the great outline.
translations.idiomatic: As Administrator of Zhao he governed by broad principles rather than petty detail.

sentences.zh: 正始中，轉勃海相。

translations.literal: In the Zhengshi era he was transferred to Chancellor of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhengshi he was transferred to Chancellor of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 屬元愉作逆，徵兵郡縣，彥先不從，為愉拘執，踰獄得免。

translations.literal: When Yuan Yu rebelled, troops were levied in the commanderies and counties; Yanxian refused and was seized by Yu, but escaped prison.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Yu rose in rebellion and the commanderies were ordered to raise troops, Yanxian refused; Yu had him arrested, but he broke out of prison.

sentences.zh: 仍為沙門，潛行至洛。

translations.literal: He then became a monk and secretly traveled to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He took monastic vows and made his way secretly to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 愉平，敕還郡。

translations.literal: When Yu was pacified, an edict ordered him back to his commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After Yu's defeat an edict recalled him to his post.

sentences.zh: 延昌中卒，時年六十一。

translations.literal: In the Yanchang era he died, aged sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died during Yanchang at the age of sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 熙平中，贈持節、左將軍、南青州刺史，諡曰惠恭。

translations.literal: In the Xiping era he was posthumously given Bearer of the Staff, General of the Left, and Governor of Southern Qingzhou, with posthumous name Huigong.
translations.idiomatic: During Xiping he was posthumously made Bearer of the Staff, General of the Left, and Governor of Southern Qingzhou, with the posthumous name Huigong (Gracious and Reverent).

sentences.zh: 子約，字元儉，性頗剛鯁。

translations.literal: His son Yue, style Yuanjian, was by nature rather stern and upright.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yue, courtesy name Yuanjian, was notably blunt and unyielding.

sentences.zh: 起家員外郎，轉給事中。

translations.literal: He began his career as Attendant Outside the Sequence and was transferred to Attendant Within.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as Attendant Outside the Sequence and was promoted to Attendant Within.

sentences.zh: 永平中，丹陽太守。

translations.literal: In the Yongping era he was Administrator of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongping he served as Administrator of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 後襲爵。

translations.literal: Later he inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: He later inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 冀州大乘賊起，敕為別將，行勃海郡事。

translations.literal: When the Mahayana bandits rose in Jizhou, he was ordered as Separate General to act in the affairs of Bohai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Mahayana rebels broke out in Jizhou he was commissioned as Separate General with authority over Bohai.

sentences.zh: 後州軍為賊所敗，遂圍郡城，城陷見害，年三十六。

translations.literal: Later the provincial army was defeated by the bandits, and they besieged the commandery city; when the city fell he was killed, aged thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial army was later routed, the rebels besieged the city, and when it fell he was killed at thirty-six.

sentences.zh: 神龜中，贈平原太守。

translations.literal: In the Shengui era he was posthumously made Administrator of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: During Shengui he was posthumously made Administrator of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 出帝時，復贈前將軍、揚州刺史。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Chu he was again posthumously made Forward General and Governor of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Chu he was again posthumously made Forward General and Governor of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 長子英起，武定末，洛州刺史。

translations.literal: His eldest son Yingqi, at the end of Wuding, was Governor of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Yingqi served as Governor of Luozhou at the end of Wuding.

sentences.zh: 英起弟威起，卒於齊王開府中兵參軍，年三十二。

translations.literal: Yingqi's younger brother Weiqi died as Staff Adviser to the Army in the Prince of Qi's staff office, aged thirty-two.
translations.idiomatic: Yingqi's younger brother Weiqi died while serving as staff adviser to the Prince of Qi's military staff at thirty-two.

sentences.zh: 贈鴻臚少卿。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Vice Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Vice Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 彥先弟絢，揚州治中。

translations.literal: Yanxian's younger brother Xuan was Chief Clerk of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxian's younger brother Xuan was Chief Clerk of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 時揚州霖雨，水入州城，刺史李崇居於城上，繫船憑焉。

translations.literal: At that time Yangzhou had continuous rain and water entered the walled city; Governor Li Chong lived atop the city wall, moored to boats for support.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rains flooded Yangzhou, and Governor Li Chong took refuge on the city wall, tethering his quarters to boats.

sentences.zh: 絢率城南民數千家汎舟南走，避水高原。

translations.literal: Xuan led several thousand households south of the city in boats to float south and escape the water to high ground.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan led several thousand families south of the city in boats to higher ground.

sentences.zh: 謂崇還北，遂與別駕鄭祖起等送子十四人於蕭衍，自號豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Believing Chong had gone north, he with Vice Administrator Zheng Zuqi and others sent fourteen sons to Xiao Yan and styled himself Governor of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Thinking Chong had fled north, he and Vice Administrator Zheng Zuqi sent fourteen sons to Xiao Yan and proclaimed himself Governor of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 衍將馬仙琕遣軍赴之。

translations.literal: Yan's general Ma Xiankou sent troops to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's general Ma Xiankou dispatched troops to his aid.

sentences.zh: 崇聞絢反，未測虛實，乃遣國侍郎韓方興單舸召之。

translations.literal: When Chong heard Xuan had rebelled and could not gauge the truth, he sent Palace Attendant Han Fangxing in a single boat to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the revolt but unsure of the facts, Chong sent Palace Attendant Han Fangxing alone by boat to call him in.

sentences.zh: 絢聞崇在，悵然驚恨。

translations.literal: When Xuan heard Chong was still there, he was dismayed and filled with regret.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Chong had not fled, Xuan was stricken with dismay and regret.

sentences.zh: 報崇曰：「比因大水，蹎䟺不免，羣情所逼，推為盟首。

translations.literal: He replied to Chong: "Lately because of the great flood I could not avoid stumbling; the crowd forced me and made me covenant leader."
translations.idiomatic: He wrote to Chong: "The flood left me no choice—the people forced me to become their leader."

sentences.zh: 今大計已爾，勢不可追。

translations.literal: Now the great plan is already thus; the momentum cannot be reversed.
translations.idiomatic: The die is cast and cannot be undone.

sentences.zh: 恐民非公民，吏非公吏。

translations.literal: I fear the people are no longer your people, and the officials no longer your officials.
translations.idiomatic: Your people and your officials are mine now.

sentences.zh: 願早行，無犯將士。

translations.literal: I wish you would depart early and not harm the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Leave at once, and spare your troops."

sentences.zh: 」崇遣從弟寧朔將軍神、丹陽太守謝靈寶勒水軍討絢。

translations.literal: Chong sent his younger cousin Ningshuo General Shen and Administrator of Danyang Xie Lingbao to lead a river force against Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Chong sent his cousin General Shen, Ningshuo General, and Danyang Administrator Xie Lingbao with a naval force against Xuan.

sentences.zh: 絢率眾逆戰，神等大破之，斬其將帥十餘人。

translations.literal: Xuan led his followers to meet them in battle; Shen and the others routed them greatly and beheaded more than ten commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan met them in battle; Shen routed his army and killed more than ten of his commanders.

sentences.zh: 絢眾奔營，神乘勝克柵，眾皆潰散。

translations.literal: Xuan's troops fled to camp; Shen took advantage of victory to seize the palisade, and the host all scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's men fled to camp, but Shen stormed the stockade and the army collapsed.

sentences.zh: 絢匹馬單逃，為村民所獲。

translations.literal: Xuan fled alone on a single horse and was seized by villagers.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan fled alone on horseback until villagers captured him.

sentences.zh: 至尉升湖，絢曰：「吾為人吏，反而見擒，有何面目得視公也。

translations.literal: At Weisheng Lake Xuan said: "I was a servant of the state, yet turned rebel and am captured—what face have I to see you, sir?"
translations.idiomatic: At Weisheng Lake he said, "I served the state, then rebelled and was taken—how can I face you?"

sentences.zh: 」投水而死。

translations.literal: He threw himself into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: He drowned himself.

sentences.zh: 并鄭祖起等皆斬之。

translations.literal: Zheng Zuqi and the others were all beheaded as well.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zuqi and his fellows were executed with him.

sentences.zh: 植，字文遠，叔業兄叔寶子也。

translations.literal: Zhi, style Wenyuan, was the son of Shuye's elder brother Shubao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi, courtesy name Wenyuan, was the son of Shuye's elder brother Shubao.

sentences.zh: 少而好學，覽綜經史，尤長釋典，善談理義。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning, surveyed the classics and histories, and was especially versed in Buddhist scriptures, skilled in discussing principle and meaning.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved learning, mastered the classics and histories, excelled in Buddhist texts, and was skilled in philosophical debate.

sentences.zh: 仕蕭寶卷，以軍勳至長水校尉，隨叔業在壽春。

translations.literal: He served Xiao Baojuan, and by military merit reached Colonel of the Long River, following Shuye at Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: He served Xiao Baojuan, rose by military merit to Colonel of the Long River, and was with Shuye at Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 叔業卒，僚佐同謀者多推司馬李元護監州，一二日謀不決定，唯席法友、柳玄達、楊令寶等數人慮元護非其鄉曲，恐有異志，共舉植監州。

translations.literal: When Shuye died, many of the staff in joint counsel pushed Marshal Li Yuanhu to oversee the province; for a day or two the plan was undecided. Only Xi Fayou, Liu Xuanda, Yang Lingbao, and a few others, fearing Yuanhu was not of their native place and might have other intentions, together raised Zhi to oversee the province.
translations.idiomatic: After Shuye's death the staff first favored Marshal Li Yuanhu to govern, but after two days of indecision Xi Fayou, Liu Xuanda, Yang Lingbao, and others—distrusting Yuanhu as an outsider—installed Zhi instead.

sentences.zh: 祕叔業喪問，教命處分皆出於植。

translations.literal: They concealed inquiry into Shuye's mourning; all orders and dispositions came from Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: They kept Shuye's death secret; Zhi issued every order.

sentences.zh: 於是開門納國軍，城庫管籥悉付康生。

translations.literal: Then they opened the gates to admit the Wei army, and the city stores and keys were all handed to Kangsheng.
translations.idiomatic: They opened the gates to the Wei army and turned the city treasury and keys over to Xi Kangsheng.

sentences.zh: 詔以植為征虜將軍、兗州刺史、崇義縣開國侯，食邑千戶。

translations.literal: An edict made Zhi General Who Captures Barbarians, Governor of Yanzhou, and Marquis of Chongyi with an estate of a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General Who Captures Barbarians, Governor of Yanzhou, and Marquis of Chongyi with a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 尋進號平東將軍，入為大鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to General Who Pacifies the East and entered the capital as Grand Minister of State Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to General Who Pacifies the East and made Grand Minister of State Ceremonial at court.

sentences.zh: 後以長子昕南叛，有司處之大辟。

translations.literal: Later because his eldest son Xin defected south, the authorities sentenced him to death.
translations.idiomatic: When his eldest son Xin defected to the south, the authorities sought the death penalty.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「植闔門歸款，子昕愚昧，為人誘陷，雖刑書有常，理宜矜恤，可特恕其罪，以表勳誠。

translations.literal: The edict said: "Zhi brought his whole household to allegiance; Xin is foolish and was lured by others. Though the penal code has its rule, reason calls for compassion; his crime may be specially pardoned to manifest his meritorious sincerity."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor decreed: "Zhi surrendered his entire household; Xin was foolish and led astray. The law demands death, but mercy is fitting—let his crime be pardoned to honor the family's loyalty."

sentences.zh: 」尋除揚州大中正，出為安東將軍、瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Chief Arbiter of Yangzhou and sent out as General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Chief Arbiter of Yangzhou and sent out as General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 罷州，復除大鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: When he left the province he was again made Grand Minister of State Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled from Yingzhou, he was again made Grand Minister of State Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 遷度支尚書，加金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was moved to Minister of Revenue and given the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of Revenue with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 植性非柱石，所為無恒。

translations.literal: Zhi's nature was not that of a pillar; his conduct had no constancy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi lacked the steadiness of a pillar and was inconsistent in his conduct.

sentences.zh: 兗州還也，表請解官，隱於嵩山，世宗不許，深以為怪。

translations.literal: Returning from Yanzhou, he memorialized asking to resign and retire on Mount Song; Emperor Shizong did not permit it and was deeply puzzled.
translations.idiomatic: Returning from Yanzhou he asked to resign and live in seclusion on Mount Song; Emperor Xuanwu refused, much to his surprise.

sentences.zh: 然公私集論，自言人門不後王肅，怏怏朝廷處之不高。

translations.literal: Yet in public and private discussion he said his family standing was not behind Wang Suo's, and he was displeased that the court did not place him higher.
translations.idiomatic: In public and private he complained that his lineage was no less than Wang Suo's and resented the court's failure to honor him accordingly.

sentences.zh: 及為尚書，志意頗滿，欲以政事為己任，謂人曰：「非我須尚書，尚書亦須我。

translations.literal: When he became Minister, his ambition was quite satisfied; he wished to take government affairs as his charge and told people: "It is not that I need the Ministry—the Ministry also needs me."
translations.idiomatic: As Minister he felt his ambitions fulfilled and declared, "The Ministry does not merely need me—I need the Ministry."

sentences.zh: 」辭氣激揚，見於言色。

translations.literal: His tone was fierce and lofty, visible in speech and expression.
translations.idiomatic: His words and bearing were fierce and arrogant.

sentences.zh: 入參議論，時對眾官面有譏毀。

translations.literal: Entering to join deliberation, he would face the assembled officials and openly mock them.
translations.idiomatic: In council he openly ridiculed his colleagues.

sentences.zh: 又表毀征南將軍田益宗，言華夷異類，不應在百世衣冠之上。

translations.literal: He also memorialized slandering General Who Conquers the South Tian Yizong, saying barbarian and Han are different kinds and should not stand above the hundred generations of eminent families.
translations.idiomatic: He also attacked General Who Conquers the South Tian Yizong, claiming that as a barbarian he should not rank above old noble houses.

sentences.zh: 率多侵侮，皆此類也。

translations.literal: He mostly acted with such insults.
translations.idiomatic: Insults of this sort were his habit.

sentences.zh: 侍中于忠、黃門元昭覽之切齒，寢而不奏。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-Ordinary Yu Zhong and Yellow Gate Yuan Zhao read it and ground their teeth, keeping it from presentation.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Yu Zhong and Yellow Gate Yuan Zhao read the memorial with fury and suppressed it.

sentences.zh: 會韋伯昕告植欲謀廢黜，尚書又奏：「羊祉告植姑子皇甫仲達，云受植旨，詐稱被詔，率合部曲，欲圖領軍于忠。

translations.literal: When Wei Boxin reported that Zhi wished to plot deposition, the Ministry again memorialized: "Yang Zhi reported Zhi's sister's son Huangfu Zhongda, saying he received Zhi's orders, falsely claiming an edict, gathering his followers, and intending to strike at Commander-in-Chief Yu Zhong."
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Boxin accused Zhi of plotting deposition, the Ministry reported: "Yang Zhi charged that Zhi's nephew Huangfu Zhongda, acting on Zhi's orders, had falsely claimed an imperial edict and gathered troops to attack Commander-in-Chief Yu Zhong."

sentences.zh: 臣等窮治，辭不伏引。

translations.literal: We interrogated to the limit, but he would not confess under torture.
translations.idiomatic: Under interrogation Zhongda would not confess.

sentences.zh: 然眾證明昞。

translations.literal: Yet the collective evidence was clear and bright.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the evidence against him was overwhelming.

sentences.zh: 案律，在邊合率部眾不滿百人以下，身猶尚斬，況仲達公然在京稱詔聚眾，諠惑都邑，駭動人情。

translations.literal: According to law, on the frontier gathering followers of fewer than a hundred still merits execution; how much more when Zhongda openly in the capital claimed an edict, gathered a host, disturbed the capital, and alarmed human hearts.
translations.idiomatic: By law even gathering fewer than a hundred men on the frontier warrants execution—how much more when Zhongda openly in the capital claimed an edict, raised troops, and threw the city into panic.

sentences.zh: 量其本意，不可測度。

translations.literal: Measuring his original intent, it cannot be fathomed.
translations.idiomatic: His ultimate aim could not be guessed.

sentences.zh: 按詐偽律：詐稱制者死。

translations.literal: According to the law on fraud: falsely claiming an imperial order is death.
translations.idiomatic: The law on fraud prescribes death for falsely claiming an imperial order.

sentences.zh: 今依眾證，處仲達入死。

translations.literal: Now according to collective evidence, Zhongda is sentenced to immediate death.
translations.idiomatic: On the evidence, Zhongda is sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 金紫光祿大夫、尚書、崇義縣開國侯裴植，身居納言之任，為禁司大臣，仲達又稱其姓名，募集人眾，雖名仲達切讓，[1]無忿懼之心。

translations.literal: Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon Minister, Marquis of Chongyi Pei Zhi held the office of remonstrance and was a minister of the prohibitory offices; Zhongda also spoke his name and surname, recruiting a host—though called Zhongda's urgent rebuke, [1] there was no anger or fear in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zhi, Minister with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon and Marquis of Chongyi, held a remonstrating office as a minister of the prohibitory courts; Zhongda also proclaimed his name and surname and recruited followers—though termed Zhongda's urgent rebuke, [1] he showed no anger or fear.

sentences.zh: 眾證雖不見植，皆言仲達為植所使。

translations.literal: Though collective evidence did not see Zhi, all said Zhongda was sent by Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: No witness saw Zhi directly, but all agreed Zhongda acted on his orders.

sentences.zh: 召仲達責問而不告列，推論情狀，不同之理不可分明。

translations.literal: Summoning Zhongda to question him, he would not inform; inferring the circumstances, the difference in reasoning cannot be made clear.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongda refused to implicate him when questioned, yet the circumstances pointed to Zhi—the case could not be reduced to an ordinary trial.

sentences.zh: 不得同之常獄，有所降減。

translations.literal: He cannot be treated like an ordinary prison case with reduction.
translations.idiomatic: No ordinary mitigation was possible.

sentences.zh: 計同仲達，處植死刑。

translations.literal: Calculating equal to Zhongda, Zhi is sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was sentenced to death on the same grounds as Zhongda.

sentences.zh: 又植親率城眾，附從王化，依律上議，唯恩裁處。

translations.literal: Moreover Zhi personally led the city populace to follow royal transformation; by law this should be submitted upward for deliberation, leaving only imperial grace to decide.
translations.idiomatic: They noted that Zhi had led the city to surrender—normally a matter for higher deliberation and imperial mercy.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「凶謀既爾，罪不合恕。

translations.literal: The edict said: "The wicked plot being thus, the crime does not admit pardon."
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "The plot is proved—there can be no pardon.

sentences.zh: 雖有歸化之誠，無容上議，亦不須待秋分也。

translations.literal: Although there was sincerity in turning to transformation, there is no room for upward deliberation, nor need to wait for the autumn equinox.
translations.idiomatic: His earlier surrender wins no deliberation, and he need not wait for the autumn executions."

sentences.zh: 」時于忠專擅朝權，既構成其禍，又矯為此詔，朝野怨之。

translations.literal: At that time Yu Zhong monopolized court power; having engineered this disaster, he also forged this edict, and court and countryside resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhong then dominated the court; having engineered Zhi's ruin, he forged the edict, to the outrage of all.

sentences.zh: 臨終，神志自若，遺令子弟命盡之後，翦落鬚髮，被以法服，以沙門禮葬于嵩高之陰。

translations.literal: At the end his spirit was as if normal; he left instructions to his sons that after life ended they should cut beard and hair, clothe him in monastic robes, and bury him by Buddhist rite on the northern slope of Song Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Facing death he remained composed, instructing his sons to shave his head and beard, dress him in monastic robes, and bury him on the northern slope of Mount Song by Buddhist rite.

sentences.zh: 年五十。

translations.literal: Aged fifty.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty.

sentences.zh: 初，植與僕射郭祚、都水使者韋儁等同時見害，於後祚儁事雪加贈，而植追復封爵而已。

translations.literal: Earlier Zhi, with Vice Minister Guo Zuo and Commissioner of Waterways Wei Jun, were killed at the same time; afterward Zuo and Jun had their cases cleared and received posthumous honors, while Zhi only had his enfeoffment restored.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi had died with Vice Minister Guo Zuo and Commissioner Wei Jun; later Zuo and Jun were exonerated and honored posthumously, while Zhi only had his title restored.

sentences.zh: 植故吏勃海刁沖上疏訟之，於是贈植征南將軍、尚書僕射、揚州刺史。

translations.literal: Zhi's former clerk Diao Chong of Bohai submitted a memorial of appeal; thereupon Zhi was posthumously made General Who Conquers the South, Vice Minister, and Governor of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His former clerk Diao Chong of Bohai appealed, and Zhi was posthumously made General Who Conquers the South, Vice Minister, and Governor of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 乃改葬。

translations.literal: Then his burial was changed.
translations.idiomatic: He was reburied with full honors.

sentences.zh: 植母，夏侯道遷之姊也，性甚剛峻，於諸子皆如嚴君。

translations.literal: Zhi's mother was the elder sister of Xiahou Daoqian; her nature was very stern and harsh, toward all her sons like a strict lord.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's mother was Xiahou Daoqian's elder sister—a stern woman who treated her sons like a lord treats subjects.

sentences.zh: 長成之後，非衣㡊不見，小有罪過，必束帶伏閣，經五三日乃引見之，督以嚴訓。

translations.literal: After they reached maturity, if not in formal dress she would not see them; for small faults she invariably made them bind their belts and kneel in the side chamber, only after five or three days summoning them to stern instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Once grown, they could not see her except in formal dress; for minor faults she made them kneel in the side chamber for days before calling them back for harsh discipline.

sentences.zh: 唯少子衍得以常服見之，旦夕溫凊。

translations.literal: Only the youngest son Yan could see her in ordinary dress, morning and evening asking after warmth and coolness.
translations.idiomatic: Only her youngest son Yan was allowed ordinary dress and daily visits.

sentences.zh: 植在瀛州也，其母年踰七十，以身為婢，自施三寶，布衣麻菲，手執箕箒，於沙門寺洒掃。

translations.literal: When Zhi was in Yingzhou his mother was over seventy; she made herself a maidservant, dedicated herself to the Three Treasures, wore hemp cloth, held dustpan and broom, and swept at a Buddhist temple.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhi governed Yingzhou his mother, past seventy, sold herself to a temple, wore hemp, and swept the floors as a servant of the Three Treasures.

sentences.zh: 植弟瑜、粲、衍並亦奴僕之服，泣涕而從，有感道俗。

translations.literal: Zhi's younger brothers Yu, Can, and Yan also wore servant dress, weeping as they followed, moving clergy and laity alike.
translations.idiomatic: His brothers Yu, Can, and Yan wore servants' clothes and followed weeping, moving monks and laypeople alike.

sentences.zh: 諸子各以布帛數百贖免其母。

translations.literal: The sons each used several hundred bolts of cloth to ransom their mother.
translations.idiomatic: The sons each paid hundreds of bolts of cloth to ransom her.

sentences.zh: 於是出家為比丘尼，入嵩高，積歲乃還家。

translations.literal: Then she left the household to become a bhikshuni, entered Mount Song, and after years returned home.
translations.idiomatic: She then became a nun on Mount Song and returned home only years later.

sentences.zh: 植雖自州送祿奉母及贍諸弟，而各別資財，同居異爨，一門數竈，蓋亦染江南之俗也。

translations.literal: Although Zhi from his province sent salary to support his mother and provide for his younger brothers, each had separate property; they lived together but cooked separately—several stoves in one household—probably also infected by Jiangnan custom.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi sent his salary to support his mother and brothers, yet each kept separate property—they shared a house but not a kitchen, a southern custom they had brought north.

sentences.zh: 植母既老，身又長嫡，其臨州也，妻子隨去，分違數歲。

translations.literal: Zhi's mother being old and he himself the eldest legitimate son, when he went to the province his wife and children went with him, separated for several years.
translations.idiomatic: Though his mother was elderly, Zhi as eldest son took wife and children with him to his post and left them apart for years.

sentences.zh: 論者譏焉。

translations.literal: Critics ridiculed this.
translations.idiomatic: Moralists condemned him for it.

sentences.zh: 子惔，字道則，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Tan, style Daozhe, inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tan, courtesy name Daozhe, inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 植弟颺，壯果有謀略。

translations.literal: Zhi's younger brother Yang was bold, resolute, and possessed of stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's younger brother Yang was bold, resolute, and resourceful.

sentences.zh: 常隨叔業征伐，以軍功為寶卷驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: He often followed Shuye on campaigns and by military merit became Baojuan's General of Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He often campaigned with Shuye and rose to General of Valiant Cavalry under Baojuan.

sentences.zh: 叔業之歸誠也，遣颺率軍於外，外以討蠻楚為名，內實備寶卷之眾。

translations.literal: When Shuye turned to sincerity, he sent Yang to lead troops outside—outwardly in the name of subduing Man and Chu, inwardly in truth to guard against Baojuan's host.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuye defected to Wei, he sent Yang with troops abroad—ostensibly to fight southern barbarians, in fact to hold Baojuan's forces in check.

sentences.zh: 景明初，以颺為輔國將軍、南司州刺史，擬戍義陽，封義安縣開國伯，邑千戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingming Yang was made General Who Assists the State and Governor of Southern Sizhou, slated to garrison Yiyang, enfeoffed Baron of Yi'an with a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingming year 1 Yang was appointed General Who Assists the State and Governor of Southern Sizhou to garrison Yiyang and created Baron of Yi'an with a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 詔命未至，為賊所殺。

translations.literal: The edict had not yet arrived when he was killed by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Before the commission arrived, bandits killed him.

sentences.zh: 贈冠軍將軍，進爵縣侯，餘如故。

translations.literal: Posthumously made General Who Establishes Valor, advanced in rank to Marquis of the county; the rest as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General Who Establishes Valor and advanced to Marquis of the county.

sentences.zh: 世宗以颺勳効未立而卒，其子烱不得襲封。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong, because Yang's merit was not yet established when he died, his son Jiong could not inherit the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu held that Yang had not lived to complete his service, so his son Jiong could not inherit.

sentences.zh: 肅宗初，烱行貨於執事，乃封城平縣開國伯，食邑八百戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Suzong, Jiong bribed those in power and was then enfeoffed Baron of Pingcheng with eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Suzong's reign Jiong bribed officials and was created Baron of Pingcheng with eight hundred households.

sentences.zh: 烱，字休光，小字黃頭。

translations.literal: Jiong, style Xiuguang, childhood name Huangtou.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong, courtesy name Xiuguang, childhood name Huangtou (Yellow Head).

sentences.zh: 頗有文學，善事權門。

translations.literal: He had considerable literary learning and was skilled at serving powerful families.
translations.idiomatic: He was literate and adept at courting the powerful.

sentences.zh: 領軍元叉納其金帛，除鎮遠將軍、散騎侍郎、揚州大中正，進伯為侯，改封高城縣，增邑一千戶。

translations.literal: Commander-in-Chief Yuan Cha accepted his gold and silk and made him General Who Pacifies the Distant, Regular Attendant at the Leisurely Riders, Chief Arbiter of Yangzhou, advanced from baron to marquis, changed enfeoffment to Gaocheng county, estate increased by a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Yuan Cha took his bribes and made him General Who Pacifies the Distant, Regular Attendant, Chief Arbiter of Yangzhou, and Marquis of Gaocheng with an added thousand households.

sentences.zh: 尋兼尚書右丞。

translations.literal: Soon he was concurrently Right Assistant Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He soon served concurrently as Right Assistant Minister.

sentences.zh: 出為東郡太守。

translations.literal: He went out as Administrator of Dong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Administrator of Dong commandery.

sentences.zh: 孝昌三年，為城民所害。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiaochang he was killed by the city populace.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaochang year 3 he was killed by townspeople.

sentences.zh: 贈散騎常侍、鎮東將軍、青州刺史，開國如故，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Regular Attendant at the Leisurely Riders, General Who Pacifies the East, and Governor of Qingzhou; his state enfeoffment remained as before; posthumous name Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Regular Attendant, General Who Pacifies the East, and Governor of Qingzhou, retaining his title, with the posthumous name Jian (Simple).

sentences.zh: 子斌，襲。

translations.literal: His son Bin inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bin inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 武定中，廣州長流參軍。

translations.literal: In the Wuding era, Long-Flow Staff Adviser of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During Wuding he served as Long-Flow Staff Adviser of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，爵例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, his rank was reduced by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi took the throne his title was reduced according to custom.

sentences.zh: 颺弟瑜，字文琬。

translations.literal: Yang's younger brother Yu, style Wenwan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang's younger brother Yu, courtesy name Wenwan.

sentences.zh: 初拜通直散騎常侍，封下密縣開國子，食邑三百戶。

translations.literal: At first appointed Regular Attendant at the Leisurely Riders Direct Communication, enfeoffed Viscount of Xiami with an estate of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was first made Regular Attendant Direct Communication and Viscount of Xiami with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 尋試守滎陽郡，坐虐暴殺人免官。

translations.literal: Soon tried as acting Administrator of Xingyang commandery; because of cruel violence and killing he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He briefly acted as Administrator of Xingyang but was dismissed for brutal murder.

sentences.zh: 後徙封灌津子。

translations.literal: Later his enfeoffment was moved to Viscount of Guanjin.
translations.idiomatic: His title was later changed to Viscount of Guanjin.

sentences.zh: 卒於勃海太守，年四十五。

translations.literal: He died as Administrator of Bohai, aged forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died as Administrator of Bohai at forty-five.

sentences.zh: 贈平南將軍、豫州刺史，諡曰定。

translations.literal: Posthumously made General Who Pacifies the South and Governor of Yuzhou; posthumous name Ding.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the South and Governor of Yuzhou, with the posthumous name Ding (Settled).

sentences.zh: 子堪，字靈淵，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Kan, style Lingyuan, inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kan, courtesy name Lingyuan, inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 歷尚書郎。

translations.literal: He passed through the post of Master of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Master of Writing.

sentences.zh: 興和中，坐事死，爵除。

translations.literal: In the Xinghe era he died because of an affair; the enfeoffment was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: During Xinghe he was executed for a crime and the title was revoked.

sentences.zh: 瑜弟粲，字文亮。

translations.literal: Yu's younger brother Can, style Wenliang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's younger brother Can, courtesy name Wenliang.

sentences.zh: 景明初，賜爵舒縣子。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingming he was granted the rank of Viscount of Shu county.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingming year 1 he was granted the rank of Viscount of Shu.

sentences.zh: 沉重，善風儀，頗以驕豪為失。

translations.literal: He was grave and dignified, skilled in bearing, but rather took pride and arrogance as faults.
translations.idiomatic: He was dignified and imposing but faulted for arrogance.

sentences.zh: 歷正平、恒農二郡太守。

translations.literal: He passed through the posts of Administrator of the two commanderies Zhengping and Hengnong.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Administrator of Zhengping and Hengnong.

sentences.zh: 高陽王雍曾以事屬粲，粲不從，雍甚為恨。

translations.literal: Prince of Gaoyang Yong once entrusted an affair to Can, but Can did not comply; Yong was deeply resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yong of Gaoyang once asked a favor of Can, who refused, and Yong bore a grudge.

sentences.zh: 後因九日馬射，敕畿內太守皆赴京師。

translations.literal: Later because of the Double Ninth horse archery, an edict ordered all administrators within the capital region to come to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the Double Ninth the emperor ordered all capital-region administrators to attend archery at court.

sentences.zh: 雍時為州牧，粲往修謁，雍含怒待之，粲神情閑邁，舉止抑揚，雍目之不覺解顏。

translations.literal: Yong was then Regional Governor; Can went to pay his respects. Yong received him with contained anger, but Can's spirit was leisurely and lofty, his bearing measured and expressive; Yong watched him and unawares his face relaxed.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was regional governor; Can paid a courtesy call. Yong greeted him coldly, but Can's easy grace softened Yong's expression.

sentences.zh: 及坐定，謂粲曰：「相愛舉動，可更為一行。

translations.literal: When seated, he said to Can: "Beloved, your movements—could you perform another round?"
translations.idiomatic: Once seated Yong said to Can, "Do that again for us."

sentences.zh: 」粲便下席為行，從容而出。

translations.literal: Can at once left his seat and performed the round, then withdrew with composure.
translations.idiomatic: Can rose, performed another round, and withdrew with perfect calm.

sentences.zh: 坐事免官。

translations.literal: Because of an affair he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 後世宗聞粲善自標置，欲觀其風度，忽令傳詔就家急召之，須臾之間，使者相屬，合家恇懼，不測所以，粲更恬然，神色不變。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Shizong heard that Can was skilled at self-presentation and wished to observe his bearing; suddenly he ordered edicts transmitted to summon him urgently at home. In the space of a moment envoys followed one another; the whole household was terrified, not knowing why—yet Can was all the more tranquil, his expression unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu, curious about Can's famous poise, suddenly sent repeated urgent summons to his home. The household panicked, but Can remained perfectly calm.

sentences.zh: 世宗歎異之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong marveled at this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was astonished.

sentences.zh: 時僕射高肇以外戚之貴，勢傾一時，朝士見者咸望塵拜謁，粲候肇，惟長揖而已。

translations.literal: At that time Vice Minister Gao Zhao, by the honor of his maternal kin, tilted power for a time; court gentlemen who saw him all bowed in the dust, but when Can waited on Zhao he only made a long bow.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhao dominated the court as imperial in-law; everyone groveled, but Can gave him only a formal bow.

sentences.zh: 及還，家人尤責之，粲曰：「何可自同凡俗也。

translations.literal: When he returned, his family reproached him especially; Can said: "How could one make oneself the same as the vulgar?"
translations.idiomatic: His family scolded him; Can replied, "Why should I act like everyone else?"

sentences.zh: 」又曾詣清河王懌，下車始進，便屬暴雨，粲容步舒雅，不以霑濡改節。

translations.literal: He also once visited Prince of Qinghe Yi; just as he dismounted and entered, a violent rain broke out. Can's step and bearing were graceful and easy; he did not change his demeanor because of being soaked.
translations.idiomatic: Visiting Prince Yi of Qinghe, he was caught in a downpour entering the gate yet walked on with unhurried grace.

sentences.zh: 懌乃令人持蓋覆之，歎謂左右曰：「何代無奇人！

translations.literal: Yi then had someone hold an umbrella over him and sighed to those about him: "What age lacks extraordinary men!"
translations.idiomatic: Yi ordered an umbrella held over him and exclaimed, "Every age has its marvels!"

sentences.zh: 」性好釋學，親升講座，雖持義未精，而風韻可重。

translations.literal: By nature he loved Buddhist learning and personally ascended the lecture seat; though his grasp of doctrine was not refined, his bearing was weighty.
translations.idiomatic: He loved Buddhism and lectured himself—doctrine aside, his presence commanded respect.

sentences.zh: 但不涉經史，終為知音所輕。

translations.literal: But because he did not involve himself in the classics and histories, in the end connoisseurs looked down on him.
translations.idiomatic: He neglected the classics, and men of taste looked down on him.

sentences.zh: 世宗末，除前將軍、太中大夫、揚州大中正，遷安南將軍、中書令。

translations.literal: At the end of Shizong's reign he was made Forward General, Grand Master of the Palace, and Chief Arbiter of Yangzhou, then moved to General Who Pacifies the South and Chief Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Xuanwu's reign he rose to Forward General, Grand Master of the Palace, Chief Arbiter of Yangzhou, then General Who Pacifies the South and Chief Secretary.

sentences.zh: 肅宗釋奠，以為侍講。

translations.literal: When Suzong performed the libation sacrifice, Can was made lecturer in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong performed the sacrifice to Confucius, Can was appointed court lecturer.

sentences.zh: 轉金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Master with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Master with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 後元顥入洛，以粲為西兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Later when Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Can was made Governor of Western Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao took Luoyang, Can was made Governor of Western Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋為濮陽太守崔巨倫所逐，棄州入嵩高山。

translations.literal: Soon he was driven out by Administrator of Puyang Cui Julun and abandoned the province to enter Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Puyang Administrator Cui Julun drove him out, and he fled to Mount Song.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝初，徵為驃騎將軍、左光祿大夫，復為中書令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Former Deposed Emperor he was summoned as General of Agile Cavalry and Left Grand Master of the Palace, and again made Chief Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Former Deposed Emperor he was recalled as General of Agile Cavalry, Left Grand Master, and again Chief Secretary.

sentences.zh: 後正月晦，帝出臨洛濱，粲起於御前再拜曰：「今年還節美，聖駕出遊，臣幸參陪從，豫奉醼樂，不勝忻戴，敢上壽酒。

translations.literal: Later on the last day of the first month the emperor went out to the Luo bank; Can rose before the imperial presence and bowed twice, saying: "This year's festival is fine; the sacred carriage goes out to tour. Your servant is fortunate to join in attendance and share in the feast and music—unable to bear joy and reverence, I dare offer wine of longevity."
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of the first month the emperor visited the Luo River; Can stepped forward and offered a toast: "What a splendid festival—how honored I am to attend and offer this cup of longevity."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「昔歲北海入朝，暫竊神器，具聞爾日卿戒之以酒，今欲使我飲，何異於往情？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Last year Beihai came to court and briefly usurped the sacred vessel; I have fully heard that on that day you admonished him with wine. Now you wish me to drink—how is this different from your former intent?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Last year you warned Beihai against wine when he seized power—why offer me drink now?"

sentences.zh: 」粲曰：「北海志在沉湎，故諫其所失。

translations.literal: Can said: "Beihai's intent lay in drowning himself in drink, so I admonished his fault."
translations.idiomatic: Can replied, "Beihai lived to drink—I warned him of that fault."

sentences.zh: 陛下齊聖溫克，臣敢獻微誠。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is equal in sageliness and gentle in restraint; your servant dares offer slight sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is sober and wise—I offer only sincere loyalty."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「實乃寡德，甚愧來譽。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "In truth I lack virtue and am very ashamed at this praise."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I am hardly worthy of such praise."

sentences.zh: 」仍為命酌。

translations.literal: He then ordered wine poured.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered wine poured.

sentences.zh: 出帝初，出為驃騎大將軍、膠州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Chu he went out as Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Governor of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Chu came to the throne Can was sent out as Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Governor of Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 屬時亢旱，士民勸令禱於海神。

translations.literal: At that time there was severe drought; gentry and commoners urged him to pray to the Sea God.
translations.idiomatic: A drought gripped the region and the people urged him to pray to the Sea God.

sentences.zh: 粲憚違眾心，乃為祈請，直據胡床，舉杯而言曰：「僕白君。

translations.literal: Can feared to go against the crowd's will and so made the prayer; leaning straight on a camp chair he raised his cup and said: "Your servant greets you, Lord."
translations.idiomatic: Reluctantly he prayed, lounging in a chair and saying, "I greet you, Lord."

sentences.zh: 」左右云，前後例皆拜謁。

translations.literal: Those about said that before and after the precedent was always to bow in audience.
translations.idiomatic: His attendants said precedent required a bow.

sentences.zh: 粲曰：「五嶽視三公，四瀆視諸侯，安有方伯而致禮海神也。

translations.literal: Can said: "The Five Peaks are regarded as equal to the Three Dukes, the Four Rivers as equal to the feudal lords—how could a regional governor perform ceremony to the Sea God?"
translations.idiomatic: Can said, "The Five Sacred Peaks rank with the Three Dukes and the Four Rivers with feudal lords—why should a governor bow to the Sea God?"

sentences.zh: 」卒不肯拜。

translations.literal: In the end he refused to bow.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to bow.

sentences.zh: 時青州叛賊耿翔受蕭衍假署，寇亂三齊。

translations.literal: At that time the rebel of Qingzhou Geng Xiang, receiving a provisional commission from Xiao Yan, raided and disturbed the Three Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhou rebel Geng Xiang, commissioned by Xiao Yan, ravaged the Three Qi region.

sentences.zh: 粲唯高談虛論，不事防禦之術。

translations.literal: Can only engaged in high talk and empty discourse, not attending to methods of defense.
translations.idiomatic: Can talked grandly but neglected defense.

sentences.zh: 翔乘其無備，掩襲州城。

translations.literal: Xiang took advantage of his lack of preparation and made a surprise attack on the walled city.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang surprised the undefended city.

sentences.zh: 左右白言賊至，粲云：「豈有此理！

translations.literal: Those about him reported that bandits had arrived; Can said: "How could there be such a thing!"
translations.idiomatic: When told the enemy had come, Can said, "Impossible!"

sentences.zh: 」左右又言已入州門，粲乃徐云：「耿王可引上廳事，自餘部眾且付城外。

translations.literal: Those about again said they had already entered the city gate; Can then said slowly: "Prince Geng may be brought up to the hall; as for the rest of his followers, hand them over outside the city."
translations.idiomatic: Told they were inside the gate, he said calmly, "Bring Prince Geng to the hall; leave his men outside."

sentences.zh: 」其不達時變如此。

translations.literal: His failure to grasp the changing times was like this.
translations.idiomatic: So blind was he to reality.

sentences.zh: 尋為翔所害，送首蕭衍，時年六十五。

translations.literal: Soon he was killed by Xiang; his head was sent to Xiao Yan; he was aged sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang killed him and sent his head to Xiao Yan. He was sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 子舍，字文若。

translations.literal: His son She, style Wenruo.
translations.idiomatic: His son She, courtesy name Wenruo.

sentences.zh: 員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Attendant Outside the Sequence at the Leisurely Riders.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Outside the Sequence at the Leisurely Riders.

sentences.zh: 粲弟衍，字文舒。

translations.literal: Can's younger brother Yan, style Wenshu.
translations.idiomatic: Can's younger brother Yan, courtesy name Wenshu.

sentences.zh: 學識優於諸兄，才行亦過之。

translations.literal: His learning surpassed his elder brothers, and his talent and conduct also exceeded theirs.
translations.idiomatic: He was more learned and capable than his brothers.

sentences.zh: 事親以孝聞，兼有將略。

translations.literal: He was known for filial service to parents and also possessed military stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: He was famed for filial piety and had military talent.

sentences.zh: 仕蕭寶卷，至陰平太守。

translations.literal: He served Xiao Baojuan, reaching Administrator of Yinping.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xiao Baojuan he rose to Administrator of Yinping.

sentences.zh: 景明二年，始得歸國，授通直郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingming he at last returned to Wei and was given Direct Communication Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingming year 2 he returned to Wei and was made Direct Communication Attendant.

sentences.zh: 衍欲辭朝命，請隱嵩高，乃上表曰：「臣幸乘昌運，得奉盛化，沐藉炎風，餐佩唐德，於生於運，已溢已榮。

translations.literal: Yan wished to decline the court order and request seclusion on Mount Song; he submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant has fortunately ridden a prosperous fortune and been able to serve a flourishing transformation, bathed in blazing wind and fed on Tang virtue—in life and in fortune already overflowing, already honored."
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire to Mount Song, writing that he had been blessed beyond measure to serve such a court.

sentences.zh: 但攝性乖和，恒苦虛弱。

translations.literal: But my received nature is at odds with harmony and I constantly suffer weakness.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his constitution was frail and constantly ailing.

sentences.zh: 比風露增加，精形侵耗。

translations.literal: Lately wind and dew have increased and essence and form are worn away.
translations.idiomatic: Lately his health had worsened.

sentences.zh: 小人愚懷，有願閑養。

translations.literal: The petty man's foolish thought has a wish for quiet nurture.
translations.idiomatic: He begged leave to recuperate.

sentences.zh: 伏見嵩岑極天，苞育名草，修生救疾，多遊此岫。

translations.literal: I see that Mount Song reaches the sky, nurturing famous herbs; those who cultivate life and cure illness mostly roam this peak.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Song, he wrote, was famed for healing herbs where sages had sought cure.

sentences.zh: 臣質無靈分，性乖山水，非敢追踵輕舉，髣髴高蹤，誠希藥此沉痾，全養禀氣耳。

translations.literal: Your servant's substance lacks spiritual allotment and my nature is at odds with mountains and waters; I do not dare follow in the footsteps of light ascent or imitate lofty traces—I truly hope to cure this lingering illness and fully nurture my received qi.
translations.idiomatic: He sought only to heal his illness in those heights, not to imitate immortals.

sentences.zh: 若所療微痊，庶偶影風雲，永歌至德。

translations.literal: If the treatment brings slight recovery, I may perchance share shadow with wind and clouds and forever sing of utmost virtue.
translations.idiomatic: If he recovered, he would return to serve.

sentences.zh: 荷衣葛屨，裁營已整；

translations.literal: Hemp clothes and straw sandals are already prepared;
translations.idiomatic: He had already prepared hermit's garb;

sentences.zh: 搖策納屣，便陟山途。

translations.literal: shaking the staff and putting on sandals, I will at once ascend the mountain path.
translations.idiomatic: and was ready to climb the mountain.

sentences.zh: 謹附陳聞，乞垂昭許。

translations.literal: I respectfully attach this report and beg your bright permission.
translations.idiomatic: He begged imperial consent.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「知欲養痾中岳，練石嵩嶺，栖素雲根，餌芝清壑，騰跡之操，深用嘉焉。

translations.literal: The edict said: "Knowing you wish to nurse illness on the central peak, refine stone on Song Ridge, dwell in plain roots of white clouds, and feed on fungus in clear ravines—your soaring-traces resolve is deeply to be commended. But governance lacks ancient wind, and I am ashamed before mountain guests. Since your will to go is hard to restrain, how can it be suppressed? Follow your former request."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his intent but noted that government lacked the ancients' purity, and granted his request.

sentences.zh: 但治缺古風，有愧山客耳。

translations.literal: But governance lacks ancient wind, and there is shame before mountain guests.
translations.idiomatic: Yet government lacked the ancients' purity, he admitted, and shamed a would-be hermit.

sentences.zh: 既志往難裁，豈容有抑，便從來請。」

translations.literal: Since your will to go is hard to restrain, how can it be suppressed? Follow your former request.
translations.idiomatic: His request was granted.

sentences.zh: 世宗之末，衍稍以出山，干祿執事。

translations.literal: At the end of Shizong's reign Yan gradually came out of the mountains and sought salary by handling affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Xuanwu's reign he emerged and sought office again.

sentences.zh: 肅宗除散騎侍郎，行河內郡事。

translations.literal: Suzong made him Regular Attendant at the Leisurely Riders and acting Administrator of Henei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong made him Regular Attendant and acting Administrator of Henei.

sentences.zh: 尋除建興太守，轉河內太守，加征虜將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Administrator of Jianxing, then transferred to Administrator of Henei, with the additional title General Who Captures Barbarians.
