translations.idiomatic: He became Administrator of Jianxing, then Henei, with the additional rank of General Who Captures Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂解任。

translations.literal: He met with mourning for his mother and left his post.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 衍歷二郡，廉貞寡欲，善撫百姓，民吏追思之。

translations.literal: Yan held two commanderies with integrity and few desires, good at comforting the hundred surnames; officials and people long remembered him.
translations.idiomatic: Over two commanderies he ruled with integrity and won lasting affection.

sentences.zh: 孝昌初，蕭衍遣將曹敬宗寇荊州，山蠻應之，大路斷絕。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiaochang, Xiao Yan's general Cao Jingzong invaded Jingzhou and the mountain barbarians responded; the great road was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaochang year 1 Cao Jingzong of Liang invaded Jingzhou with mountain tribes, cutting the main routes.

sentences.zh: 都督崔暹率數萬之眾，盤桓魯陽，不能前討。

translations.literal: Commander-in-Chief Cui Xuan led a host of tens of thousands, lingering at Luyang, unable to advance and attack.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Cui Xuan camped tens of thousands at Luyang but could not advance.

sentences.zh: 荊州危急，朝廷憂之。

translations.literal: Jingzhou was critically urgent and the court was worried.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhou was in peril and the court was alarmed.

sentences.zh: 詔衍為別將、假前將軍，與恒農太守王羆率軍一萬出武關以救荊州。

translations.literal: An edict made Yan a Separate General and acting Forward General; with Administrator of Hengnong Wang Pi he led ten thousand troops out of Wuguan to rescue Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was ordered out as Separate General with Wang Pi of Hengnong and ten thousand men through Wuguan to relieve Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 賊逆戰於浙陽，衍大破之，賊遂退走，荊州圍解。

translations.literal: The bandits met them in battle at Zheyang; Yan routed them greatly and the bandits then retreated; the siege of Jingzhou was relieved.
translations.idiomatic: At Zheyang he routed the enemy and lifted the siege.

sentences.zh: 除使持節、散騎常侍、平東將軍、假安東將軍、北道都督，鎮鄴西之武城，封安陽縣開國子，食邑三百戶。

translations.literal: He was made Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant at the Leisurely Riders, General Who Pacifies the East, acting General Who Pacifies the East, Commander of the Northern Route, garrisoning Wucheng west of Ye, enfeoffed Viscount of Anyang with an estate of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant, General Who Pacifies the East, northern-route commander at Wucheng, and Viscount of Anyang with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 時相州刺史、安樂王鑒潛圖叛逆，衍覺其有異，密表陳之。

translations.literal: At that time the Governor of Xiangzhou, Prince of Anle Jian, secretly plotted rebellion; Yan sensed his strangeness and memorialized it in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jian of Anle, Governor of Xiangzhou, plotted rebellion; Yan detected it and reported secretly.

sentences.zh: 尋而鑒所部別將嵇宗馳驛告變。

translations.literal: Soon Jian's Separate General Ji Zong galloped by post to report the change.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's Separate General Ji Zong soon reported by express.

sentences.zh: 乃詔衍與都督源子邕、李神軌等討鑒，平之。

translations.literal: Then an edict ordered Yan with Commander Yuan Ziyin, Li Shengui, and others to attack Jian and pacify him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan, Yuan Ziyin, and Li Shengui were ordered to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 除撫軍將軍、相州刺史，假鎮北將軍、北道大都督，進封臨汝縣開國公，增邑千二百戶，常侍如故。

translations.literal: He was made Pacifying Army General and Governor of Xiangzhou, acting General Who Pacifies the North and Grand Commander of the Northern Route, advanced to Duke of Linru with an estate increased by twelve hundred households; Regular Attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Pacifying Army General, Governor of Xiangzhou, acting General Who Pacifies the North, and Duke of Linru with twelve hundred added households.

sentences.zh: 仍詔衍與子邕北討葛榮。

translations.literal: Still an edict ordered Yan with Ziyin to campaign north against Ge Rong.
translations.idiomatic: He was then ordered north with Ziyin against Ge Rong.

sentences.zh: 軍次陽平之東北漳曲，賊來拒戰，衍軍敗見害。

translations.literal: The army halted northeast of Zhangqu in Yangping; the bandits came to resist in battle and Yan's army was defeated and he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhangqu northeast of Yangping Ge Rong's forces defeated and killed him.

sentences.zh: 朝野人情，莫不駭惋。

translations.literal: Court and countryside, human hearts—all were struck with shock and regret.
translations.idiomatic: All were shocked and grieved.

sentences.zh: 贈使持節、車騎大將軍、司空、相州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously given Bearer of the Staff, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Minister of Works, and Governor of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Bearer of the Staff, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Minister of Works, and Governor of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 子嵩，襲。

translations.literal: His son Song inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Song inherited.

sentences.zh: 武定中，河內太守。

translations.literal: In the Wuding era, Administrator of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: During Wuding he was Administrator of Henei.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，爵例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, his rank was reduced by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi took the throne his title was reduced according to custom.

sentences.zh: 又天水冀人尹挺，仕蕭鸞，以軍勳至陳郡太守。

translations.literal: Again Yin Ting of Jizhou in Tianshui served Xiao Luan and by military merit reached Administrator of Chen commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Another defector was Yin Ting of Jizhou in Tianshui, who served Xiao Luan and rose to Administrator of Chen by military merit.

sentences.zh: 遂與叔業參謀歸誠。

translations.literal: He then joined Shuye in plotting allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Shuye in planning submission to Wei.

sentences.zh: 景明初，除輔國將軍、南司州刺史，擬戍義陽，亦封宋縣開國伯，食邑八百戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingming he was made General Who Assists the State and Governor of Southern Sizhou, slated to garrison Yiyang, and also enfeoffed Baron of Song county with eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingming year 1 he was made General Who Assists the State and Governor of Southern Sizhou to garrison Yiyang and created Baron of Song with eight hundred households.

sentences.zh: 轉冠軍將軍、東郡太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General Who Establishes Valor and Administrator of Dong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to General Who Establishes Valor and Administrator of Dong.

sentences.zh: 未拜而卒。

translations.literal: Before he received appointment he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died before taking up the post.

sentences.zh: 賜布帛一百匹，贈本將軍、涇州刺史。

translations.literal: He was granted a hundred bolts of cloth and silk; posthumously given his former generalship and Governor of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a hundred bolts of cloth and posthumously made his former rank and Governor of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 子循，歷太原太守。

translations.literal: His son Xun passed through the post of Administrator of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xun served as Administrator of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 循弟彖，饒安令、遼西太守。

translations.literal: Xun's younger brother Tuan was Magistrate of Rao'an and Administrator of Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xun's brother Tuan was Magistrate of Rao'an and Administrator of Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 兄弟皆有政事才。

translations.literal: The brothers all had talent for government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Both brothers proved capable administrators.

sentences.zh: 時河東南解人柳玄達，頗涉經史。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Xuanda of Nanjie in Hedong was well versed in the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Liu Xuanda of Nanjie in Hedong was well read in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 仕蕭鸞，歷諸王參軍。

translations.literal: He served Xiao Luan, passing through staff posts for various princes.
translations.idiomatic: He served Xiao Luan on several princes' staffs.

sentences.zh: 與叔業姻婭周旋，叔業之鎮壽春，委以管記。

translations.literal: He had marriage ties with Shuye and moved in his circle; when Shuye garrisoned Shouchun he entrusted him with records.
translations.idiomatic: Related to Shuye by marriage, he managed Shuye's records at Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 及叔業之被猜疑，將謀獻款，玄達贊成其計，前後表啟皆玄達之詞。

translations.literal: When Shuye came under suspicion and was about to plot submission, Xuanda supported his plan; the memorials before and after were all Xuanda's words.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuye faced suspicion and planned to defect, Xuanda backed him and drafted the memorials.

sentences.zh: 景明初，除輔國將軍、司徒諮議參軍，封南頓縣開國子，邑二百戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingming he was made General Who Assists the State and Staff Adviser to the Minister of Education, enfeoffed Viscount of Nandun with two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingming year 1 he was made General Who Assists the State, staff adviser to the Minister of Education, and Viscount of Nandun with two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 二年秋卒，時年四十三。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the second year he died, aged forty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in autumn of year 2 at forty-three.

sentences.zh: 後改封夏陽縣，邑戶如先。

translations.literal: Later his enfeoffment was changed to Xiayang county; estate households as before.
translations.idiomatic: His fief was later moved to Xiayang with the same household quota.

sentences.zh: 玄達曾著大夫論，備陳叔業背逆歸順、契闊危難之旨，又著喪服論，約而易尋。

translations.literal: Xuanda once wrote Discourse of the Great Officer, fully setting forth Shuye's turning from rebellion to obedience and the meaning of trials in peril; he also wrote Discourse on Mourning Garments, concise and easy to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanda wrote Discourse of the Great Officer on Shuye's defection and a concise Discourse on Mourning Garments.

sentences.zh: 文多不錄。

translations.literal: Most of the text is not recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: Most of that writing is omitted here.

sentences.zh: 子絺，襲。

translations.literal: His son Chi inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chi inherited.

sentences.zh: 武定中，東太原太守。

translations.literal: In the Wuding era, Administrator of Eastern Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: During Wuding he was Administrator of Eastern Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，爵例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, his rank was reduced by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi took the throne his title was reduced according to custom.

sentences.zh: 絺弟遠，字季雲。

translations.literal: Chi's younger brother Yuan, style Jiyun.
translations.idiomatic: Chi's younger brother Yuan, courtesy name Jiyun.

sentences.zh: 性粗疏無拘撿，時人或謂之「柳癲」。

translations.literal: By nature coarse and careless without restraint, people of the time sometimes called him "Mad Liu."
translations.idiomatic: He was coarse and unrestrained—people called him "Mad Liu."

sentences.zh: 好彈琴，耽酒，時有文詠。

translations.literal: He loved playing the zither, was addicted to wine, and at times composed literary pieces.
translations.idiomatic: He loved the lute, wine, and occasional verse.

sentences.zh: 為肅宗挽郎。

translations.literal: He served as mourning officer for Suzong.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a mourning officer for Suzong.

sentences.zh: 出帝初，除儀同開府參軍事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Chu he was made Army Affairs Officer of the Equal-in-Rank Opening Office.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Chu he was made staff officer of an equal-rank opening office.

sentences.zh: 放情琴酒之間。

translations.literal: He gave free rein to zither and wine.
translations.idiomatic: He lived for music and drink.

sentences.zh: 每出返，家人或問有何消息，答云：「無所聞，縱聞亦不解。

translations.literal: Whenever he returned from going out, if his family asked what news there was, he answered: "I heard nothing; even if I heard, I would not understand."
translations.idiomatic: Asked for news when he came home, he said, "I heard nothing—and wouldn't understand it if I had."

sentences.zh: 」元象二年，客遊項城，遇患卒，時年四十。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanxiang, traveling as a guest in Xiangcheng, he met with illness and died, aged forty.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanxiang year 2 he died of illness while visiting Xiangcheng at forty.

sentences.zh: 玄達弟玄瑜，景明初，除正員郎，轉鎮南大將軍開府從事中郎，帶汝陰太守。

translations.literal: Xuanda's younger brother Xuanyu; in the first year of Jingming he was made Regular Master of Writing, then moved to Attendant of the Opening Office of the General Who Pacifies the South, concurrently Administrator of Ruyin.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanda's brother Xuanyu became Regular Master of Writing, then staff officer to the General Who Pacifies the South with concurrent Ruyin.

sentences.zh: 延昌二年卒，年五十五。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yanchang he died, aged fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yanchang year 2 at fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 子諧，頗有文學。

translations.literal: His son Xie had considerable literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xie was literate.

sentences.zh: 善鼓琴，以新聲手勢，京師士子翕然從學。

translations.literal: Skilled at playing the zither, with new sounds and hand gestures; gentlemen of the capital flocked to study with him.
translations.idiomatic: A gifted lutenist, he taught new techniques to eager students in the capital.

sentences.zh: 除著作佐郎。

translations.literal: He was made Assistant Editor in the Office of Composition.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Assistant Editor in the Office of Composition.

sentences.zh: 建義初，於河陰遇害，時年二十六。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyi he met with harm at Heyin, aged twenty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyi year 1 he was killed at Heyin at twenty-six.

sentences.zh: 又武都人楊令寶，有膂力，善射。

translations.literal: Again Yang Lingbao of Wudu had physical strength and was skilled at archery.
translations.idiomatic: Another ally was Yang Lingbao of Wudu, strong and a fine archer.

sentences.zh: 仕蕭鸞，數為小將，征戰著效，至譙郡太守，遂參叔業歸誠之謀。

translations.literal: He served Xiao Luan, several times as a minor commander; in campaigns he showed merit, reaching Administrator of Qiao commandery, and then joined Shuye's plot of allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: He served Xiao Luan as a field officer, rose to Administrator of Qiao, and joined Shuye's defection plot.

sentences.zh: 景明初，除輔國將軍、南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingming he was made General Who Assists the State and Governor of Southern Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingming year 1 he was made General Who Assists the State and Governor of Southern Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 擬戍淮陰，封寧陵縣開國子，食邑五百戶。

translations.literal: Slated to garrison Huaiyin, enfeoffed Viscount of Ningling with five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was to garrison Huaiyin and was created Viscount of Ningling with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 在淮南征戰，累著勞捷。

translations.literal: In campaigns on the Huai he repeatedly showed merit and swift success.
translations.idiomatic: On the Huai he won repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 徵拜冠軍將軍，試守京兆內史。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed General Who Establishes Valor and acting Interior Minister of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as General Who Establishes Valor and acting Interior Minister of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 卒，追封邵陵縣開國子，邑二百戶，賜帛三百匹，贈征虜將軍、華州刺史。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously enfeoffed Viscount of Shaoling with two hundred households, granted three hundred bolts of silk, posthumously made General Who Captures Barbarians and Governor of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made Viscount of Shaoling, granted silk, and honored as General Who Captures Barbarians and Governor of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 子彪，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Biao inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: His son Biao inherited.

sentences.zh: 永熙中，征虜將軍、中散大夫。

translations.literal: In the Yongxi era, General Who Captures Barbarians and Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongxi he was General Who Captures Barbarians and Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, his rank was reduced by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi took the throne his title was reduced according to custom.

sentences.zh: 令寶弟令仁，亦隨令寶立效。

translations.literal: Lingbao's younger brother Lingren also followed Lingbao in establishing merit.
translations.idiomatic: Lingbao's brother Lingren also earned merit with him.

sentences.zh: 前將軍、汝南內史。

translations.literal: Forward General and Interior Minister of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: He became Forward General and Interior Minister of Runan.

sentences.zh: 又京兆杜陵人韋伯昕，學尚，有壯氣。

translations.literal: Again Wei Boxin of Duling in Jingzhao valued learning and had bold spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Boxin of Duling in Jingzhao was learned and bold.

sentences.zh: 自以才智優於裴植，常輕之，植疾之如讎。

translations.literal: He considered his talent and wisdom superior to Pei Zhi and often looked down on him; Zhi hated him like a foe.
translations.idiomatic: He thought himself cleverer than Pei Zhi and despised him; Zhi hated him bitterly.

sentences.zh: 即彥先之妹壻也。

translations.literal: He was Yanxian's sister's husband.
translations.idiomatic: He was married to Yanxian's sister.

sentences.zh: 叔業以其有大志，故遣送子芬之為質。

translations.literal: Shuye, because he had great ambition, therefore sent his son Fenzhi as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye sent his son Fenzhi as hostage because Boxin was ambitious.

sentences.zh: 景明初，封雲陵縣開國男，食邑二百戶，拜南陽太守。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingming he was enfeoffed Baron of Yunling with two hundred households and made Administrator of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingming year 1 he was created Baron of Yunling with two hundred households and made Administrator of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 數歲，坐事免。

translations.literal: After several years he was dismissed because of an affair.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years he was dismissed for misconduct.

sentences.zh: 久之，拜員外散騎常侍，加中壘將軍。

translations.literal: After a long time he was made Attendant Outside the Sequence at the Leisurely Riders with the additional title General of the Central Rampart.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made Attendant Outside the Sequence with the additional rank General of the Central Rampart.

sentences.zh: 延昌末，告尚書裴植謀為廢黜，植坐死。

translations.literal: At the end of Yanchang he reported that Minister Pei Zhi plotted deposition; Zhi was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Yanchang he accused Pei Zhi of plotting deposition; Zhi was executed.

sentences.zh: 後百餘日，伯昕亦病卒。

translations.literal: More than a hundred days later Boxin also died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Boxin died of illness a hundred days later.

sentences.zh: 臨亡，見植為祟，口云：「裴尚書死，不獨見由，何以見怒也？」

translations.literal: At death he saw Zhi as a malign spirit and said with his mouth: "Minister Pei died—not only through me; why show anger at me?"
translations.idiomatic: Dying, he claimed Pei Zhi's ghost haunted him: "His death wasn't only my doing—why blame me?"

sentences.zh: 其叔業爪牙心膂所寄者：裴智淵，左中郎將，封浚儀縣；

translations.literal: Those in whom Shuye placed his claws and heart: Pei Zhiyuan, General of the Left Army, enfeoffed in Junyi county;
translations.idiomatic: Shuye's trusted lieutenants included Pei Zhiyuan, General of the Left Army, enfeoffed in Junyi;

sentences.zh: 王昊，左軍將軍，封南汝陰縣；

translations.literal: Wang Hao, General of the Left Army, enfeoffed in Southern Ruyin county;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hao, General of the Left Army, enfeoffed in Southern Ruyin;

sentences.zh: 趙革，右中郎將，封西宋縣。

translations.literal: Zhao Ge, General of the Right Army, enfeoffed in Western Song county.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ge, General of the Right Army, enfeoffed in Western Song.

sentences.zh: 並開國男，食邑各二百戶。

translations.literal: All were barons with estates of two hundred households each.
translations.idiomatic: Each was a baron with two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 李道真，右軍將軍，封睢陽縣開國子，食邑五百戶；

translations.literal: Li Daozhen, General of the Right Army, enfeoffed Viscount of Suiyang with five hundred households;
translations.idiomatic: Li Daozhen, General of the Right Army, Viscount of Suiyang with five hundred households;

sentences.zh: 胡文盛，右軍將軍，封剛陽縣；

translations.literal: Hu Wensheng, General of the Right Army, enfeoffed in Gangyang county;
translations.idiomatic: Hu Wensheng, General of the Right Army, enfeoffed in Gangyang;

sentences.zh: 魏承祖，右軍將軍，封平春縣。

translations.literal: Wei Chengzu, General of the Right Army, enfeoffed in Pingchun county.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Chengzu, General of the Right Army, enfeoffed in Pingchun.

sentences.zh: 並開國子，食邑各三百戶。

translations.literal: All were viscounts with estates of three hundred households each.
translations.idiomatic: Each was a viscount with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 承祖，廣陵寒人也。

translations.literal: Chengzu was a man of the cold ranks in Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzu was of humble origin in Guangling.

sentences.zh: 依隨叔業，為趨走左右。

translations.literal: He attached himself to Shuye and served as runner at his side.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Shuye as a personal attendant.

sentences.zh: 壯健，善事人，叔業待之甚厚。

translations.literal: Stalwart and good at serving people, Shuye treated him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Strong and obliging, he won Shuye's deep favor.

sentences.zh: 及出為州，以為防閤。

translations.literal: When Shuye went out to a province he was made garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuye took a provincial post Chengzu became his garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 善撫士卒，兼有將用，自景明以後，常為統軍，南北征伐，累有戰功。

translations.literal: Skilled at comforting soldiers and also possessing commander's use; from Jingming onward he was often overall commander, campaigning north and south with repeated battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: He was a capable commander; from Jingming on he led armies north and south with steady success.

sentences.zh: 歷太原太守，至光祿大夫、安南將軍。

translations.literal: He passed through Administrator of Taiyuan to Grand Master of the Palace and General Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through Administrator of Taiyuan to Grand Master of the Palace and General Who Pacifies the South.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍遣將圍義陽，士民應之。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan sent generals to besiege Yiyang; gentry and commoners responded.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan besieged Yiyang and the local elite sided with him.

sentences.zh: 三關既陷，州城時甚縣急。

translations.literal: The Three Passes having fallen, the provincial city was at that time very urgently pressed.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Passes had fallen and the city was desperate.

sentences.zh: 以承祖持節，行撫軍將軍，率師討之。

translations.literal: Chengzu was made Bearer of the Staff and acting Pacifying Army General to lead troops against them.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzu was sent as Bearer of the Staff and acting Pacifying Army General to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 大破賊眾，解義陽之圍，還復三關，遂為名將。

translations.literal: He routed the bandit host greatly, relieved the siege of Yiyang, recovered the Three Passes, and thus became a famed commander.
translations.idiomatic: He routed the enemy, lifted the siege, recovered the Three Passes, and became a famed general.

sentences.zh: 終於并州刺史。

translations.literal: He ended his career as Governor of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died as Governor of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 衣冠之士，預叔業勳者：安定皇甫光，北地梁祐，清河崔高客，天水閻慶胤，河東柳僧習等。

translations.literal: Gentlemen in caps and robes who shared in Shuye's merit: Huangfu Guang of Anding, Liang You of Beidi, Cui Gaoke of Qinghe, Yan Qingyin of Tianshui, Liu Sengxi of Hedong, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Other gentry who shared Shuye's rewards included Huangfu Guang, Liang You, Cui Gaoke, Yan Qingyin, and Liu Sengxi.

sentences.zh: 光，美鬚髯，善言笑。

translations.literal: Guang had a beautiful beard and was skilled in speech and laughter.
translations.idiomatic: Guang had a fine beard and a ready wit.

sentences.zh: 仕蕭鸞，以軍勳至右軍將軍。

translations.literal: He served Xiao Luan and by military merit reached General of the Right Army.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xiao Luan he rose to General of the Right Army.

sentences.zh: 入國，為輔國將軍，假南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Upon entering Wei he was made General Who Assists the State and acting Governor of Southern Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After defecting to Wei he was made General Who Assists the State and acting Governor of Southern Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 卒於勃海太守。

translations.literal: He died as Administrator of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: He died as Administrator of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 兄椿齡，薛安都壻也。

translations.literal: His elder brother Chunling was son-in-law to Xue Andu.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Chunling married Xue Andu's daughter.

sentences.zh: 隨安都於彭城內附，歷位司徒諮議、岐州刺史。

translations.literal: Following Andu in surrendering from Pengcheng, he passed through Staff Adviser to the Minister of Education and Governor of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chunling followed Xue Andu in surrendering from Pengcheng and rose to staff adviser and Governor of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 光未入朝而椿齡先卒。

translations.literal: Guang had not yet entered court when Chunling died first.
translations.idiomatic: Guang had not yet reached court when Chunling died.

sentences.zh: 椿齡子璋，鄉郡相。

translations.literal: Chunling's son Zhang was Chancellor of a district commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Chunling's son Zhang was a district chancellor.

sentences.zh: 璋弟瑒，為司徒胡國珍所拔，自太尉記室超遷吏部郎。

translations.literal: Zhang's younger brother Yang was pulled up by Minister of Education Hu Guozhen from the Grand Marshal's records office to Master of Writing in a leap.
translations.idiomatic: Yang, favored by Hu Guozhen, leapt from the Grand Marshal's staff to Master of Writing.

sentences.zh: 性貪婪，多所受納，鬻賣吏官，皆有定價。

translations.literal: By nature greedy, he took many bribes; selling official posts, each had a fixed price.
translations.idiomatic: He was corrupt and sold offices at fixed prices.

sentences.zh: 後以丞相、高陽王雍之壻，超拜持節、冠軍將軍、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Later because he was son-in-law to Chief Minister Prince Yong of Gaoyang, he was promoted in a leap to Bearer of the Staff, General Who Establishes Valor, and Governor of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: As son-in-law to Chief Minister Prince Yong of Gaoyang he was rushed to Bearer of the Staff, General Who Establishes Valor, and Governor of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 為政殘暴，百姓患之。

translations.literal: His government was cruel and violent; the hundred surnames suffered from him.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with cruelty and the people suffered.

sentences.zh: 罷州後，仍遇風病。

translations.literal: After leaving the province he still met with wind illness.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving office he suffered paralysis.

sentences.zh: 久之，除安南將軍、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: After a long time he was made General Who Pacifies the South and Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Long after he was made General Who Pacifies the South and Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 太昌初卒，年五十八。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taichang he died, aged fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Taichang year 1 at fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈衞大將軍、尚書左僕射、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Grand General of the Guard, Left Vice Minister, and Governor of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand General of the Guard, Left Vice Minister, and Governor of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 子長卿，司州主簿、祕書郎中、太尉司馬。

translations.literal: His son Changqing was Chief Clerk of Sizhou, Master of Writing in the Secretariat, and Marshal of the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: His son Changqing served as Chief Clerk of Sizhou, Secretariat Master of Writing, and Grand Marshal's marshal.

sentences.zh: 祐，叔業之從姑子也。

translations.literal: You was the son of Shuye's paternal aunt's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: You was Shuye's cousin.

sentences.zh: 好學，便弓馬。

translations.literal: He loved learning and was skilled with bow and horse.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and excelled at arms.

sentences.zh: 隨叔業征伐，身被五十餘創。

translations.literal: Following Shuye on campaigns, his body received more than fifty wounds.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning with Shuye, he took more than fifty wounds.

sentences.zh: 景明初，拜右軍將軍，賜爵山桑子。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingming he was made General of the Right Army and granted the rank of Viscount of Shansang.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingming year 1 he was made General of the Right Army and Viscount of Shansang.

sentences.zh: 出為北地太守，清身率下，甚有治稱。

translations.literal: He went out as Administrator of Beidi, personally pure and leading subordinates; he had a very good reputation for governance.
translations.idiomatic: As Administrator of Beidi he ruled with integrity and won praise.

sentences.zh: 歷驍騎將軍、太中大夫、右將軍。

translations.literal: He passed through General of Valiant Cavalry, Grand Master of the Palace, and General of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to General of Valiant Cavalry, Grand Master of the Palace, and General of the Right.

sentences.zh: 從容風雅，好為詩詠，常與朝廷名賢汎舟洛水，以詩酒自娛。

translations.literal: Easy in bearing, elegant in style, fond of composing poetry; he often with famed worthies of the court floated boats on the Luo and took poetry and wine for pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Graceful and literary, he often boated on the Luo with court luminaries, taking pleasure in verse and wine.

sentences.zh: 遷光祿大夫，加平北將軍。

translations.literal: He was moved to Grand Master of the Palace with the additional title General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Master of the Palace and General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 端然養志，不歷權門。

translations.literal: Composed and nurturing his will, he did not pass through powerful families' gates.
translations.idiomatic: He lived quietly and never courted the powerful.

sentences.zh: 出為平西將軍、京兆內史，當世歎其抑屈。

translations.literal: He went out as General Who Pacifies the West and Interior Minister of Jingzhao; men of the age sighed at his suppressed rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as General Who Pacifies the West and Interior Minister of Jingzhao—contemporaries thought him undervalued.

sentences.zh: 卒官，贈本將軍、涇州刺史。

translations.literal: He died in office; posthumously given his former generalship and Governor of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office and was posthumously made his former rank and Governor of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 高客，博學，善文札，美風流。

translations.literal: Gaoke was broadly learned, skilled in documents, and beautiful in bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoke was learned, skilled with documents, and striking in manner.

sentences.zh: 景明初，拜散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingming he was appointed Regular Attendant at the Leisurely Riders.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingming year 1 he was made Regular Attendant at the Leisurely Riders.

sentences.zh: 出為楊州開府掾，帶陳留太守。

translations.literal: He went out as staff member of Yangzhou's opening office, concurrently Administrator of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: He served on Yangzhou's opening staff as concurrent Administrator of Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 慶胤，父汪，參薛安都平北將軍事。

translations.literal: Qingyin—his father Wang had participated in Xue Andu's Pacifying the North staff affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Qingyin's father Wang had served on Xue Andu's Pacifying the North staff.

sentences.zh: 安都入國，聽汪還南。

translations.literal: When Andu entered Wei, Wang was permitted to return south.
translations.idiomatic: When Andu defected to Wei, Wang was allowed to return south.

sentences.zh: 慶胤博識洽聞，善於談論，聽其言說，不覺忘疲。

translations.literal: Qingyin was broadly informed and well versed; skilled in discourse—hearing him speak, one unawares forgot fatigue.
translations.idiomatic: Qingyin was encyclopedic and a brilliant talker—listeners forgot weariness.

sentences.zh: 景明初，為李元談輔國府司馬。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingming he was Marshal of Li Yuanhu's staff as General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingming year 1 he was marshal on Li Yuanhu's staff.

sentences.zh: 卒於敷城太守。

translations.literal: He died as Administrator of Fucheng.
translations.idiomatic: He died as Administrator of Fucheng.

sentences.zh: 僧習，善隸書，敏於當世。

translations.literal: Sengxi was skilled in clerical script and quick-witted for his age.
translations.idiomatic: Sengxi excelled in clerical script and was quick-witted.

sentences.zh: 景明初，為裴植征虜府司馬。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingming he was Marshal on Pei Zhi's staff as General Who Captures Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingming year 1 he was marshal on Pei Zhi's staff.

sentences.zh: 稍遷北地太守，為政寬平，氐羌悅愛。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to Administrator of Beidi; his government was lenient and fair, and the Di and Qiang loved him.
translations.idiomatic: He became Administrator of Beidi, ruling leniently so the Di and Qiang loved him.

sentences.zh: 肅宗時，至太中大夫，加前將軍，出為潁川太守。

translations.literal: In Suzong's time he reached Grand Master of the Palace with the additional Forward General, and went out as Administrator of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Suzong he rose to Grand Master of the Palace and Forward General and served as Administrator of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 夏侯道遷，譙國人。

translations.literal: Xiahou Daoqian was a man of Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Daoqian was from Qiao.

sentences.zh: 少有志操。

translations.literal: In youth he had aspiration and principle.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he had ambition and integrity.

sentences.zh: 年十七，父母為結婚韋氏，道遷云：「欲懷四方之志，不願取婦。

translations.literal: At seventeen his parents arranged marriage with the Wei clan; Daoqian said: "I wish to harbor the ambition of the four quarters and do not wish to take a wife."
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen his parents betrothed him to the Wei clan; he said, "I aim to roam the empire—I will not marry."

sentences.zh: 」家人咸謂戲言。

translations.literal: His family all considered it jest.
translations.idiomatic: His family thought he was joking.

sentences.zh: 及至婚日，求覓不知所在。

translations.literal: When the wedding day came, they sought him but did not know where he was.
translations.idiomatic: On the wedding day he had vanished.

sentences.zh: 於後訪問，乃云逃入益州。

translations.literal: Later on inquiry it was said he had fled into Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later they learned he had fled to Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 仕蕭鸞，以軍勳稍遷至前軍將軍、輔國將軍。

translations.literal: He served Xiao Luan and by military merit was gradually moved to Forward General and General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xiao Luan he rose by military merit to Forward General and General Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 隨裴叔業至壽春，為南譙太守。

translations.literal: Following Pei Shuye to Shouchun, he was Administrator of Southern Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Pei Shuye to Shouchun as Administrator of Southern Qiao.

sentences.zh: 兩家雖為姻好，而親情不協，遂單騎歸國。

translations.literal: Although the two families were marriage allies, their kin feelings did not harmonize; he then returned to Wei alone on a single horse.
translations.idiomatic: Though allied by marriage, he fell out with Shuye and rode alone to defect to Wei.

sentences.zh: 拜驍騎將軍，隨王肅至壽春，遣道遷守合肥。

translations.literal: He was appointed General of Valiant Cavalry; following Wang Suo to Shouchun, Suo sent Daoqian to guard Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: He was made General of Valiant Cavalry; Wang Suo sent him to guard Hefei.

sentences.zh: 肅薨，道遷棄戍南叛。

translations.literal: When Suo died, Daoqian abandoned his garrison and rebelled south.
translations.idiomatic: When Suo died Daoqian abandoned his post and rebelled to the south.

sentences.zh: 會蕭衍以莊丘黑為征虜將軍、梁秦二州刺史，鎮南鄭，黑請道遷為長史，帶漢中郡。

translations.literal: When Xiao Yan made Zhuang Qiu Hei General Who Captures Barbarians and Governor of Liang and Qin, garrisoning Nanzheng, Hei requested Daoqian as Chief Clerk with concurrent Hanzhong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan made Zhuang Qiu Hei governor of Liang and Qin at Nanzheng; Hei took Daoqian as chief clerk with Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 會黑死，衍以王鎮國為刺史，未至而道遷陰圖歸順。

translations.literal: When Hei died, Yan made Wang Zhenguo governor; before he arrived Daoqian secretly plotted to turn to allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: When Hei died and Wang Zhenguo was named to replace him, Daoqian secretly planned to defect to Wei.

sentences.zh: 先是，仇池鎮將楊靈珍阻兵反叛，戰敗南奔。

translations.literal: Earlier the garrison commander of Qiuchi Yang Lingzhen had raised troops in rebellion and, defeated in battle, fled south.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yang Lingzhen of Qiuchi had rebelled and fled south after defeat.

sentences.zh: 衍以靈珍為征虜將軍，假武都王，助戍漢中，有部曲六百餘人，道遷憚之。

translations.literal: Yan made Lingzhen General Who Captures Barbarians and acting Prince of Wudu to help garrison Hanzhong, with more than six hundred followers; Daoqian feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan sent Lingzhen back as acting Prince of Wudu with six hundred men; Daoqian feared him.

sentences.zh: 衍時又遣其左右吳公之等十餘人使南鄭。

translations.literal: At that time Yan also sent more than ten of his attendants including Wu Gongzhi to Nanzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yan also sent Wu Gongzhi and a dozen envoys to Nanzheng.

sentences.zh: 道遷乃偽會使者，請靈珍父子，靈珍疑而不赴。

translations.literal: Daoqian then falsely summoned the envoys and invited Lingzhen and his sons; Lingzhen suspected and did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Daoqian feigned a meeting and summoned Lingzhen, who stayed away in suspicion.

sentences.zh: 道遷乃殺使者五人，馳擊靈珍，斬其父子，并送使者五首於京師。

translations.literal: Daoqian then killed five envoys, galloped to strike Lingzhen, beheaded him and his sons, and together sent the five envoys' heads to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He killed five Liang envoys, struck Lingzhen, beheaded him and his sons, and sent five heads to the capital.

sentences.zh: 江悅之等推道遷為持節、冠軍將軍、梁秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: Jiang Yuezhi and others raised Daoqian to Bearer of the Staff, General Who Establishes Valor, and Governor of Liang and Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yuezhi and others proclaimed him Bearer of the Staff, General Who Establishes Valor, and Governor of Liang and Qin.

sentences.zh: 道遷表曰：「臣聞知機其神，趨利如響，臣雖不武，敢忘機利。

translations.literal: Daoqian memorialized: "Your servant has heard that knowing the moment is divine and rushing for profit is like an echo; though your servant is not martial, how dare I forget opportune profit?"
translations.idiomatic: Daoqian wrote: "To seize the moment is wisdom; though no warrior, I dare not miss my chance."

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下澤被區宇，德濟蒼生，八表同忻，品物咸賴。

translations.literal: "Your Majesty's grace covers the realm, virtue aids the black-haired people; the eight directions rejoice together, all things rely on you."
translations.idiomatic: "Your grace covers the realm and all creatures rely on you."

sentences.zh: 臣頃亡蟻賊，匹馬歸闕，自斯搏噬，罄竭丹款。

translations.literal: "Your servant lately escaped petty bandits and returned to court alone on a single horse; since then in struggle I have exhausted my red sincerity."
translations.idiomatic: "I fled the south and returned alone, offering all my loyalty since."

sentences.zh: 但中於壽陽，橫為韋纘所謗。

translations.literal: "But at Shouyang I was slandered by Wei Zuan."
translations.idiomatic: "But at Shouyang Wei Zuan slandered me."

sentences.zh: 理之曲直，並是楊集朗、王秉所悉。

translations.literal: "The rights and wrongs of the case are both known to Yang Jilang and Wang Bing."
translations.idiomatic: "Yang Jilang and Wang Bing know the truth."

sentences.zh: 臣實愚短，豈能自安，便逃竄江吳，苟存視息。

translations.literal: "Your servant is truly foolish and short; how could I be at ease? I fled to Jiang and Wu to barely preserve breath."
translations.idiomatic: "Fearing for my life I fled to the lower Yangzi."

sentences.zh: 蕭衍梁州刺史莊丘黑與臣早舊，申臣為長史。

translations.literal: "Xiao Yan's Governor of Liangzhou Zhuang Qiu Hei was old friends with your servant and recommended your servant as Chief Clerk."
translations.idiomatic: "Zhuang Qiu Hei of Liangzhou, an old friend, made me his chief clerk."

sentences.zh: 值黑亡歿專任，天時素願，機會在茲。

translations.literal: "When Hei died and I held sole charge, the heavenly season of my long wish and the opportunity were here."
translations.idiomatic: "When Hei died I held power—the moment I had long awaited had come."

sentences.zh: 遇武興私署侍郎鄭洛生來此，臣即披露誠款，與其共契機要，報武興王楊紹先并其中叔集起等，請其遣軍以為腹背。

translations.literal: "Meeting Wuxing's privately appointed Attendant Zheng Luosheng here, your servant at once disclosed sincere intent and with him joined in crucial plans, reporting to Prince of Wuxing Yang Shaoxian and his uncle Jiaqi and others, asking them to send troops as belly and back."
translations.idiomatic: "With Zheng Luosheng of Wuxing I plotted and asked Prince Yang Shaoxian of Wuxing for troops in support."

sentences.zh: 即遣左天長由寒山路馳啟，復會通直散騎常侍臣集朗還至武興。

translations.literal: "At once I sent Zuo Tianchang by the Han Mountain road in urgent report, and again met Regular Attendant Yang Jilang returning to Wuxing."
translations.idiomatic: "I sent Zuo Tianchang by the Han Mountain road and met Yang Jilang returning from Wuxing."

sentences.zh: 臣聞其至，知事必克。

translations.literal: "When your servant heard he had arrived, I knew the affair would succeed."
translations.idiomatic: "When Jilang arrived I knew we would succeed."

sentences.zh: 集朗果遣鄭右留使至臣間，密參機舉。

translations.literal: Jilang indeed sent Zheng Youliu as envoy to your servant's place to consult secretly on the military action.
translations.idiomatic: Jilang sent Zheng Youliu to coordinate the coup in secret.

sentences.zh: 會有蕭衍使人吳公之至，知臣懷誠，將歸大化，遂與府司馬嚴思、臧恭，典籤吳宗肅、王勝等共楊靈珍父子密相構結，期當取臣。

translations.literal: When Xiao Yan's envoy Wu Gongzhi arrived, knowing your servant harbored sincerity and would return to great transformation, he with Staff Adviser Yan Si, Zang Gong, Record Keeper Wu Zongsu, Wang Sheng, and others together with Yang Lingzhen and his sons secretly joined in plot, fixing a time to seize your servant.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Gongzhi of Liang, learning of the plot, conspired with Yan Si, Zang Gong, and Yang Lingzhen's faction to seize Daoqian.

sentences.zh: 臣幸先覺，悉得戮思、恭等。

translations.literal: Your servant was fortunate to perceive first and killed Si, Gong, and the others entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Daoqian struck first and killed Si, Gong, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 臣即遣鄭猥馳告集朗，急求軍援。

translations.literal: Your servant at once sent Zheng Wei in urgent report to Jilang, urgently seeking military aid.
translations.idiomatic: He urgently asked Jilang for troops through Zheng Wei.

sentences.zh: 而武興軍未到之間，蕭衍白馬戍主尹天寶不識天命，固執愚迷，乃率部曲驅掠民丁，敢為不逞。

translations.literal: But before Wuxing's army arrived, Xiao Yan's garrison commander of Baima Yi Tianbao, not knowing Heaven's mandate, stubbornly clung to folly, and led his followers to drive and plunder the people, daring to act lawlessly.
translations.idiomatic: Before Wuxing's troops arrived, Liang's Baima garrison commander Yi Tianbao raided the populace.

sentences.zh: 臣即遣軍主江悅之率諸軍主席靈坦、龐樹等領義勇應時討撲。

translations.literal: Your servant at once sent Army Commander Jiang Yuezhi leading the army masters Xi Lingtan, Pang Shu, and others with righteous courage to suppress in timely fashion.
translations.idiomatic: Daoqian sent Jiang Yuezhi with Xi Lingtan and Pang Shu to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 而樹銳氣難裁，違悅之節度，輕進失脫，天寶因此直到南鄭，重圍州城。

translations.literal: But Shu's sharp spirit was hard to restrain; he violated Yuezhi's command, advanced lightly and missed capture, and Tianbao therefore reached Nanzheng straight through and heavily besieged the walled city.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Shu disobeyed orders; Tianbao reached Nanzheng and besieged the city.

sentences.zh: 梁秦士庶，僉云危棘，以義逼臣，勸為刺史，須藉此威，鎮靖內外。

translations.literal: The gentry and commoners of Liang and Qin all said peril was extreme; by righteousness pressing your servant they urged him to be governor, needing to borrow this authority to pacify inside and outside.
translations.idiomatic: The people pressed him to act as governor to save the province.

sentences.zh: 臣赤誠奉國，苟取濟事，輒捐小跡，且從權宜，假當州位。

translations.literal: Your servant's red sincerity served the state; if it could help the affair, I would cast aside small traces and for the moment follow expedience, falsely taking the provincial post.
translations.idiomatic: For the state's sake he accepted the post provisionally.

sentences.zh: 重遣皇甫選由斜谷道以事啟聞。

translations.literal: Again he sent Huangfu Xuan by the Xiegu road to report the affair.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Huangfu Xuan through Xiegu to report to court.

sentences.zh: 臣即親率士卒，四日三夜，交鋒苦戰。

translations.literal: Your servant then personally led soldiers for four days and three nights of bitter battle in crossing blades.
translations.idiomatic: He fought in person for four days and three nights.

sentences.zh: 武興之軍，乘虛躡後。

translations.literal: Wuxing's army took advantage of the void to follow in the rear.
translations.idiomatic: Wuxing's troops struck from behind.

sentences.zh: 天寶兇徒，因宵鳥散，進既摧破，退失巢穴，潛捨軍眾，依山傍險，突入白馬。

translations.literal: Tianbao's vicious followers because of night scattered like birds; advancing they were broken, retreating they lost nest and lair, secretly abandoning the army host and relying on mountains and passes for danger, bursting into Baima.
translations.idiomatic: Tianbao's men fled by night; he abandoned his army and fled into Baima.

sentences.zh: 集朗與二弟躬擐甲冑，率其所領，登即擒斬。

translations.literal: Jilang and his two younger brothers personally donned armor and led those they commanded, ascending at once to seize and behead.
translations.idiomatic: Jilang and his brothers captured and beheaded Tianbao in armor.

sentences.zh: 戍內戶口，即放還民。

translations.literal: The households within the garrison were at once released back to the people.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison population was restored to civilian life.

sentences.zh: 斯由皇威遐振，罪人授首，凶狡時殄，公私慶快，非但梁秦竭力，實關集朗赴接之機。

translations.literal: This was because imperial might reached far and criminals offered their heads; the fierce and cunning were timely exterminated—public and private rejoiced with joy, not only Liang and Qin exerting strength but truly tied to Jilang's timely reinforcement.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial might prevailed; the victory owed much to Jilang's timely aid.

sentences.zh: 臣前已遣軍主杜法先還洵陽，構合徒黨，誘結鄉落；

translations.literal: Your servant earlier had sent Army Commander Du Faxian back to Xunyang to assemble followers and entice joined villages;
translations.idiomatic: He had sent Du Faxian to Xunyang to raise local allies;

sentences.zh: 令晉壽土豪王僧承、王文粲等還至西關，共興大義。

translations.literal: ordered Jinshou local magnates Wang Chengcheng, Wang Wencai, and others to return to Xiguan and together raise great righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: and ordered Wang Chengcheng and Wang Wencai to stir rebellion west of the passes.

sentences.zh: 當今庸蜀虛弱，楚鄧懸危，開拓九區，掃清六合，形要之利，在於此時，進趣之略，願速處分。

translations.literal: Today Yong and Shu are weak, Chu and Deng hang in peril; to open the nine regions and sweep the six harmonies—the advantage of strategic form lies in this time; the plan of advance—may it be quickly disposed.
translations.idiomatic: "Shu is weak and this is the moment to unify the realm—send orders quickly."

sentences.zh: 臣以愚陋，猥當推舉，事定之後，便即束身馳歸天闕。

translations.literal: Your servant, foolish and lowly, was improperly raised to recommendation; when the affair is settled I will at once bind myself and gallop back to the heavenly gate.
translations.idiomatic: "When done I will return to court at once."

sentences.zh: 但物情草創，猶有參差。

translations.literal: But popular feeling was newly founded and still had unevenness.
translations.idiomatic: But local opinion was still unsettled.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍魏興太守范珣、安康太守范泌共前巴西太守姜脩，屯聚川東，尚規舉斧，登遣討襲，具於別啟。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan's Administrator of Weixing Fan Xun, Administrator of Ankang Fan Bi, together with former Administrator of Baxi Jiang Xiu, gathered in eastern Chuan, still plotting to raise axes; I have sent to attack—details in a separate report.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Xun, Fan Bi, and Jiang Xiu still held eastern Chuan; he reported attacks separately.

sentences.zh: 集朗兄弟並議留臣權相綏奬，[2]須得撲滅珣等，便即首路。

translations.literal: Jilang's brothers all discussed retaining your servant to comfort and encourage by authority, [2] needing to destroy Xun and the others, then at once take the road to court.
translations.idiomatic: Jilang's kin asked him to stay until Fan Xun was crushed, [2] then go to court.

sentences.zh: 伏願聖慈特垂鑒照。

translations.literal: I bow and wish the sacred compassion especially to cast down bright regard.
translations.idiomatic: "I beg your luminous regard."

sentences.zh: 謹遣兼長史臣張天亮奉表略聞。」

translations.literal: I respectfully send Concurrent Chief Clerk Zhang Tianliang to present this memorial in brief report."
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zhang Tianliang with the memorial."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「得表，聞之。

translations.literal: The edict said: "Received the memorial; I have heard it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "Your memorial is received."

sentences.zh: 將軍前識機運，已投誠款，而中逢猜間，致有播越，復翻然風返，建茲殊效，忠貫古烈，義動遐邇。

translations.literal: "General, you earlier knew the moment and machine and already offered sincere intent, but midway met suspicion and intervals, causing wandering exile; again you turned with the wind and returned, establishing this special achievement—loyalty penetrating ancient heroism, righteousness moving the distant and near."
translations.idiomatic: "You saw the moment early and defected; though slandered, you returned with splendid merit."

sentences.zh: 漢鄭既開，勢翦庸蜀，混同之略，方自斯始。

translations.literal: Han and Zheng being opened, power shears Yong and Shu—the plan of unification begins from this.
translations.idiomatic: "With Hanzhong opened, Shu can be taken—unification begins here."

sentences.zh: 擒凶掃惡，何快如之。

translations.literal: To capture the fierce and sweep the wicked—what could be more joyful?
translations.idiomatic: "What joy to sweep away the wicked!"

sentences.zh: 想餘黨悉平，西南清盪，經算淹朔，當有劬勞。

translations.literal: I think the remaining parties will all be pacified and the southwest cleared; the plan has delayed months—you must have toil and labor.
translations.idiomatic: "Finish the southwest pacification—you have labored long."

sentences.zh: 所請軍宜，別敕一二。

translations.literal: "The requested troops and provisions will be separately ordered one or two items."
translations.idiomatic: "Your requests for troops will be granted separately."

sentences.zh: 」又賜道遷璽書曰：「得表，具誠節之懷。

translations.literal: Again he bestowed on Daoqian an imperial letter saying: "Received the memorial; fully your sincere intent."
translations.idiomatic: He also sent a sealed letter praising Daoqian's loyalty.

sentences.zh: 卿忠義夙挺，期委自昔。

translations.literal: "Your loyalty and righteousness have long stood forth; trust and commission from of old."
translations.idiomatic: "Your loyalty was always known to us."

sentences.zh: 中有事因，以致乖舛。

translations.literal: "In the midst there was a matter's cause, leading to error and breach."
translations.idiomatic: "Misfortune caused your wandering."

sentences.zh: 知能乘機豹變，翻然改圖，奬率同心，萬里投順，遠舉漢中，為開蜀之始。

translations.literal: "Knowing you could seize the moment like a leopard's change and turn your map over, encouraging and leading those of one heart, casting yourself in loyalty from ten thousand li, raising Hanzhong from afar as the beginning of opening Shu."
translations.idiomatic: "You turned at the right moment, rallied allies, and opened Hanzhong—the start of conquering Shu."

sentences.zh: 洪規茂略，深有嘉焉。

translations.literal: "Grand plan and lush stratagem—I deeply commend them."
translations.idiomatic: "Your strategy merits high praise."

sentences.zh: 今授卿持節、散騎常侍、平南將軍、豫州刺史、豐縣開國侯，食邑一千戶。

translations.literal: "Now I appoint you Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant at the Leisurely Riders, General Who Pacifies the South, Governor of Yuzhou, Marquis of Feng county with an estate of a thousand households."
translations.idiomatic: "He was made Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant, General Who Paciles the South, Governor of Yuzhou, and Marquis of Feng with a thousand households."

sentences.zh: 并同義諸人，尋有別授。

translations.literal: "Those of shared righteousness will soon receive separate appointments."
translations.idiomatic: "Your comrades will be rewarded separately."

sentences.zh: 王師數道，絡繹電邁，遣使持節、散騎常侍、都督征梁漢諸軍事、鎮西將軍、尚書邢巒，指授節度。

translations.literal: "The royal army on several routes follows in continuous streams like lightning; I send Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of campaigns against Liang and Han, General Who Pacifies the West, Minister Xing Luan to point and grant command."
translations.idiomatic: "Xing Luan was sent to command the armies against Liang and Han."

sentences.zh: 卿其善建殊效，稱朕意焉。

translations.literal: "Build special achievement well and match my intent."
translations.idiomatic: "Serve me well."

sentences.zh: 」道遷表受平南、常侍，而辭豫州、豐縣侯，引裴叔業公爵為例。

translations.literal: Daoqian on the memorial accepted Pacifying the South and Regular Attendant, but declined Yuzhou and Marquis of Feng, citing Duke Pei Shuye's precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Daoqian accepted Pacifying the South but declined Yuzhou and the marquisate, citing Pei Shuye's precedent.

sentences.zh: 世宗不許。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu refused.

sentences.zh: 道遷自南鄭來朝京師，引見於太極東堂，免冠徒跣謝曰：「臣往日歸誠，誓盡心力，超蒙榮奬，灰殞匪報。

translations.literal: Daoqian from Nanzheng came to court in the capital and was received in audience at the east hall of Taiji; bareheaded and barefoot he apologized: "Your servant in former days turned to allegiance, vowing to exhaust heart and strength; exceeding I received glory and reward—reduced to ashes I could not repay."
translations.idiomatic: At court he went barefoot to apologize: "I pledged my all when I defected—your rewards overwhelm me."

sentences.zh: 但比在壽春，遭韋纘之酷，申控無所，致此猖狂。

translations.literal: "But compared with at Shouyang, meeting Wei Zuan's cruelty, I had nowhere to appeal and control, leading to this madness."
translations.idiomatic: "At Shouyang Wei Zuan drove me to desperation."

sentences.zh: 是段之來，希酬昔遇。

translations.literal: "This period's coming hopes to repay the former encounter."
translations.idiomatic: "I hope now to repay your trust."

sentences.zh: 勳微恩重，有靦心顏。

translations.literal: Merit slight and grace heavy—I have a ashamed face.
translations.idiomatic: "Your grace shames my small deeds."

sentences.zh: 」世宗曰：「卿建為山之功，一簣之玷，何足謝也。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong said: "You built the achievement of a mountain; a basketful's stain—what is there to apologize for?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "A mountain needs no apology for a pebble's flaw."

sentences.zh: 」道遷以賞報為微，逡巡不拜。

translations.literal: Daoqian considered the reward slight and hesitated, not bowing.
translations.idiomatic: Daoqian thought the reward too small and hesitated to bow.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「道遷至止既淹，未恭州封，可敕吏部速令召拜。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Daoqian's arrival and stop having been long, he has not respectfully received the provincial enfeoffment; the Ministry of Personnel may be ordered to summon and appoint him quickly."
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Ministry to appoint him at once.

sentences.zh: 」道遷拜日，詔給百五十人供。

translations.literal: On the day Daoqian bowed in appointment, an edict granted supplies for a hundred fifty men.
translations.idiomatic: On his appointment day he was granted supplies for a hundred fifty men.

sentences.zh: 尋改封濮陽縣開國侯，邑戶如先。

translations.literal: Soon his enfeoffment was changed to Marquis of Puyang; estate households as before.
translations.idiomatic: His fief was soon changed to Marquis of Puyang with the same household quota.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，頻表解州，世宗許之。

translations.literal: After more than a year he repeatedly memorialized to resign the province; Emperor Shizong permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he repeatedly asked to leave office and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 除南兗州大中正，不拜。

translations.literal: He was made Chief Arbiter of Southern Yanzhou but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was offered Chief Arbiter of Southern Yanzhou but declined.

sentences.zh: 道遷雖學不淵洽，而歷覽書史，閑習尺牘，札翰往還，甚有意理。

translations.literal: Although Daoqian's learning was not deep and comprehensive, he had surveyed books and histories and was practiced in documents; correspondence back and forth had very good reasoning.
translations.idiomatic: Though not deeply learned, he read widely and wrote lucid correspondence.

sentences.zh: 好言宴，務口實，京師珍羞，罔不畢有。

translations.literal: He loved banquets and pursued the substance of talk; delicacies of the capital he had without exception.
translations.idiomatic: He loved feasts and collected every delicacy of the capital.

sentences.zh: 於京城之西，水次之地，大起園池，殖列蔬果，延致秀彥，時往遊適，妓妾十餘，常自娛興。

translations.literal: At the west of the capital, on waterside land, he greatly raised gardens and ponds, planted fruits and vegetables, invited outstanding talents, and at times went to roam and enjoy—more than ten singing girls and concubines, regularly amusing himself.
translations.idiomatic: West of the capital he built gardens, entertained scholars, and kept a dozen concubines for amusement.

sentences.zh: 國秩歲入三千餘匹，專供酒饌，不營家產。

translations.literal: The state stipend's annual income of more than three thousand bolts he devoted entirely to wine and food, not managing household property.
translations.idiomatic: He spent his three-thousand-bolt stipend on wine and feasting, not on property.

sentences.zh: 每誦孔融詩曰：「『坐上客恒滿，樽中酒不空』，餘非吾事也。

translations.literal: He often recited Kong Rong's poem: "'Guests always fill the seat, wine never empties in the cup'—the rest is not my affair."
translations.idiomatic: He quoted Kong Rong: "A full table and a full cup—that is all I need."

sentences.zh: 」識者多之。

translations.literal: Those who knew him praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Connoisseurs approved.

sentences.zh: 出為散騎常侍、平西將軍、華州刺史，轉安東將軍、瀛州刺史，常侍如故。

translations.literal: He went out as Regular Attendant at the Leisurely Riders, General Who Pacifies the West, and Governor of Huazhou; was moved to General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Yingzhou; Regular Attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Regular Attendant, General Who Pacifies the West, and Governor of Huazhou, then General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 為政清嚴，善禁盜賊。

translations.literal: His government was clear and strict; he was good at prohibiting bandits and thieves.
translations.idiomatic: He governed strictly and suppressed banditry.

sentences.zh: 熙平年，病卒，年六十九。

translations.literal: In the Xiping era he died of illness, aged sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Xiping at sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 贈撫軍將軍、雍州刺史，贈帛五百匹，諡曰明侯。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Pacifying Army General and Governor of Yongzhou; granted five hundred bolts of silk; posthumous name Marquis Ming.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Pacifying Army General and Governor of Yongzhou, with the posthumous title Marquis Ming.

sentences.zh: 初，道遷以拔漢中歸誠，本由王潁興之計，求分邑戶五百封之，世宗不許。

translations.literal: Earlier, because Daoqian's seizing Hanzhong and turning to allegiance originally came from Wang Yingxing's plan, he asked to divide five hundred estate households to enfeoff him; Emperor Shizong did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He had wanted to reward Wang Yingxing with five hundred households for the Hanzhong plan, but Xuanwu refused.

sentences.zh: 靈太后臨朝，道遷重求分封。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling held court, Daoqian again requested the divided enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Ling he asked again.

sentences.zh: 太后大奇其意，議欲更以三百戶封潁興，會卒，遂寢。

translations.literal: The empress dowager greatly marveled at his intent and discussed enfeoffing Yingxing with three hundred households more; when he died the matter was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The empress considered it but Yingxing died before it was done.

sentences.zh: 道遷不娉正室，唯有庶子數人。

translations.literal: Daoqian did not marry a principal wife; he had only several illegitimate sons.
translations.idiomatic: He never took a principal wife and had only bastard sons.

sentences.zh: 長子夬，字元廷。

translations.literal: His eldest son Gui, style Yuanting.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Gui, courtesy name Yuanting.

sentences.zh: 歷位前軍將軍、鎮遠將軍、南兗州大中正。

translations.literal: He passed through Forward General, General Who Pacifies the Distant, and Chief Arbiter of Southern Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Forward General, General Who Pacifies the Distant, and Chief Arbiter of Southern Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 夬性好酒，居喪不戚，醇醪肥鮮，不離於口。

translations.literal: Gui by nature loved wine; in mourning he was not sorrowful—rich brew and fat delicacies never left his mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was a drunkard who feasted even during mourning.

sentences.zh: 沽買飲噉，多所費用。

translations.literal: Buying and drinking consumed much expense.
translations.idiomatic: He drank away his wealth.

sentences.zh: 父時田園，貨賣略盡，人間債負數猶千餘匹，穀食至常不足，弟妹不免飢寒。

translations.literal: The fields and gardens of his father's time were sold off almost entirely; private debts still numbered more than a thousand bolts, grain food often insufficient, and younger siblings could not escape cold and hunger.
translations.idiomatic: He sold the family estates and left debts; his siblings went hungry.

sentences.zh: 初，道遷知夬好酒，不欲傳授國封。

translations.literal: Earlier Daoqian, knowing Gui loved wine, did not wish to transmit the state enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Daoqian had refused to pass the title to him because of his drinking.

sentences.zh: 夬未亡前，忽夢見征虜將軍房世寶來至其家，直上廳事，與其父坐，屏人密言。

translations.literal: Before Gui died he suddenly dreamed that General Who Captures Barbarians Fang Shibao came to his house, went straight up to the hall, and sat with his father; people were screened for secret talk.
translations.idiomatic: Gui dreamed Fang Shibao came to his house and met his father in secret.

sentences.zh: 夬心驚懼，謂人曰：「世寶至官間，必擊我也。

translations.literal: Gui was startled and afraid and told people: "When Shibao reaches office he will surely strike me."
translations.idiomatic: He feared Shibao would punish him when in office.

sentences.zh: 」尋有人至，云「官呼郎」。

translations.literal: Soon someone came saying "The office summons the gentleman."
translations.idiomatic: Soon messengers came to summon him.

sentences.zh: 隨召即去，遣左右杖之二百，不勝楚痛，大叫良久乃寤，流汗徹於寢具。

translations.literal: When summoned he went at once; they sent attendants to cane him two hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: He was caned two hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 至明，前涼城太守趙卓詣之，見其衣濕，謂夬曰：「卿昨夕當大飲，溺衣如此。

translations.literal: Unable to bear the pain, he cried out long before waking, sweat soaking through bedding.
translations.idiomatic: He woke screaming, soaked in sweat.

sentences.zh: 」夬乃具陳所夢。

translations.literal: At dawn former Administrator of Qianliangcheng Zhao Zhuo visited and, seeing his clothes wet, said to Gui: "You must have drunk heavily last night and wet your clothes thus."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhuo found him drenched and teased him about drunkenness.

sentences.zh: 先是旬餘，祕書監鄭道昭暴病卒。

translations.literal: Gui then fully related the dream.
translations.idiomatic: Gui told the dream.

sentences.zh: 夬聞，謂卓曰：「人生何常，唯當縱飲耳。

translations.literal: Earlier, more than ten days before, Chief Minister of Writing Zheng Daozhao had died suddenly of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Director Zheng Daozhao had died days before.

sentences.zh: 」於是昏酣遂甚。

translations.literal: When Gui heard, he told Zhuo: "Human life—how constant? One should only drink freely."
translations.idiomatic: Gui said life was short and one should drink.

sentences.zh: 夢後二日，不能言，針之，乃得語，而猶虛劣。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sank into deep intoxication.
translations.idiomatic: He drank himself into a stupor.

sentences.zh: 其從兄㚟等並營視之，皆言危而獲振。

translations.literal: Two days after the dream he could not speak; after acupuncture he could speak but was still weak.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later he lost speech; needles restored it weakly.

sentences.zh: 俄而心悶，旋轉而死。

translations.literal: His cousins and others all attended him, all saying he was critical yet rallied.
translations.idiomatic: His kin thought he would recover.

sentences.zh: 為洗浴者視其尸體，大有杖處，青赤隱起二百下許。

translations.literal: Soon chest distress; turning he died.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly he died.

sentences.zh: 贈鉅鹿太守。

translations.literal: Those who washed the corpse saw on the body many cane marks, blue and red swelling in hidden rise of about two hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: The washers found two hundred cane welts on his body.

sentences.zh: 初夬與南人辛諶、庾道、江文遙等終日遊聚，酣飲之際，恒相謂曰：「人生局促，何殊朝露，坐上相看，先後之間耳。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Administrator of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Administrator of Julu.

sentences.zh: 脫有先亡者，當於良辰美景，靈前飲宴。

translations.literal: Earlier Gui with southerners Xin Chen, Yu Dao, Jiang Wenyao, and others gathered all day in drink; in intoxication they often told each other: "Life is cramped, no different from morning dew; sitting and looking at each other on the seat is only a matter of before and after."
translations.idiomatic: He and his drinking companions vowed to feast at one another's funerals.

sentences.zh: 儻或有知，庶共歆饗。

translations.literal: "If one dies first, at a fine day and beautiful scene we should drink before the spirit."
translations.idiomatic: "If one dies first, the rest should drink at his bier on a fine day."

sentences.zh: 」及夬亡後，三月上巳，諸人相率至夬靈前酌飲。

translations.literal: "Perhaps if there is awareness, we may together enjoy the offering."
translations.idiomatic: "Perhaps the dead can still share the cup."

sentences.zh: 時日晚天陰，室中微闇，咸見夬在坐，衣服形容不異平昔，時執杯酒，似若獻酬，但無語耳。

translations.literal: Three months after Gui's death, on the third-month upper si day, the men together came to Gui's spirit to pour and drink.
translations.idiomatic: Three months later they drank before Gui's spirit on the upper si of the third month.

sentences.zh: 時夬家客雍僧明心有畏恐，披簾欲出，便即僵仆，狀若被毆。

translations.literal: The day was late and the sky overcast; in the room it was slightly dark—all saw Gui seated, clothes and appearance no different from usual, holding a wine cup as if offering toast, but without words.
translations.idiomatic: In dim light they saw Gui seated among them, cup in hand, silent.

sentences.zh: 夬從兄欣宗云：「今是節日，諸人憶弟疇昔之言，故來共飲，僧明何罪而被瞋責？

translations.literal: At that time Gui's household guest Yong Sengming was afraid in heart and pulled the curtain to go out; at once he fell stiff as if beaten.
translations.idiomatic: The guest Yong Sengming tried to flee and collapsed as if beaten.

sentences.zh: 」僧明便寤。

translations.literal: Gui's cousin Xinzong said: "Today is a festival; the gentlemen recall my younger brother's former words and came to drink together—what crime has Sengming that he was angrily rebuked?"
translations.idiomatic: Xinzong said they had come to drink as Gui wished and asked why Sengming was punished.

sentences.zh: 而欣宗鬼語如夬平生，并怒家人皆得其罪，又發摘陰私竊盜，咸有次緒。

translations.literal: And Xinzong spoke in ghost language like Gui in life, rebuking the household for all their crimes, exposing private theft—everything in order.
translations.idiomatic: Then Xinzong spoke as Gui's ghost, denouncing the household's thefts one by one until Sengming awoke.

sentences.zh: 夬妻，裴植女也，與道遷諸妾不穆，訟䦧徹于公庭。

translations.literal: And Xinzong spoke in ghost language like Gui in life, rebuking the household for all their crimes, exposing private theft—everything in order.
translations.idiomatic: Xinzong then spoke as Gui's ghost, exposing the household's thefts.

sentences.zh: 子籍，年十餘歲，襲祖封。

translations.literal: Gui's wife was Pei Zhi's daughter; with Daoqian's various concubines she was not harmonious, lawsuits reaching the public court.
translations.idiomatic: Gui's wife, Pei Zhi's daughter, feuded with Daoqian's concubines in court.

sentences.zh: 已數年，而夬弟眘等言其眇目癎疾，不任承繼，自以與夬同庶，己應紹襲。

translations.literal: His son Ji, aged more than ten, inherited the grandfather's enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ji, barely ten, inherited the grandfather's title.

sentences.zh: 尚書奏籍承封。

translations.literal: Already several years, yet Gui's younger brothers Shen and others said he had small eyes and epilepsy and could not bear succession; they themselves, same illegitimate as Gui, should inherit.
translations.idiomatic: His uncles claimed Ji was unfit and sought the title themselves.

sentences.zh: 元象中，平東將軍、太中大夫。

translations.literal: The Ministry memorialized that Ji should inherit the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry upheld Ji's succession.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，例降。

translations.literal: In the Yuanxiang era, General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanxiang he was General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 㚟，道遷兄子也。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, his rank was reduced by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi took the throne his title was reduced.

sentences.zh: 位至咸陽太守。

translations.literal: Shen was Daoqian's elder brother's son.
translations.idiomatic: Shen was Daoqian's nephew.

sentences.zh: 李元護，遼東襄平人。

translations.literal: He reached Administrator of Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: He became Administrator of Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 八世祖胤，晉司徒、廣陸侯。

translations.literal: Li Yuanhu was a man of Xiangping in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuanhu was from Xiangping in Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 胤子順、璠及孫沉、志，皆有名宦。

translations.literal: His eighth-generation ancestor Yin was Jin Minister of Education and Marquis of Guanglu.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestor Yin of the eighth generation was Jin Minister of Education and Marquis of Guanglu.

sentences.zh: 沉孫根，慕容寶中書監。

translations.literal: Yin's sons Shun and Fan and grandsons Shen and Zhi all had famous offices.
translations.idiomatic: Yin's descendants held famous offices for generations.

sentences.zh: 根子後智等隨慕容德南渡河，居青州，數世無名位，三齊豪門多輕之。

translations.literal: Shen's grandson Gen was Secretariat Director under Murong Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Gen was Secretariat Director under Murong Bao.

sentences.zh: 元護以國家平齊後，隨父懷慶南奔。

translations.literal: Gen's son Houzhi and others followed Murong De south across the river and lived in Qingzhou; for generations without name and rank, the great families of the Three Qi mostly looked down on them.
translations.idiomatic: His line settled in Qingzhou and was scorned by local magnates.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺，美鬚髯，少有武力。

translations.literal: After the state pacified Qi, Yuanhu followed his father Huaiqing in fleeing south.
translations.idiomatic: After Wei conquered Qi he fled south with his father.

sentences.zh: 仕蕭道成，歷官馬頭太守、後軍將軍、龍驤將軍。

translations.literal: He was eight chi tall, with a beautiful beard; in youth he had martial strength.
translations.idiomatic: He was tall, bearded, and strong in youth.

sentences.zh: 雖以將用自達，然亦頗覽文史，習於簡牘。

translations.literal: He served Xiao Daocheng, passing through the posts of Administrator of Matou, Rear General, and Dragon Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: He served Xiao Daocheng as a field commander.

sentences.zh: 高祖至鍾離，元護時在城中，為蕭鸞徐州刺史蕭惠休奉使詣軍，高祖見而善之。

translations.literal: Although he reached office through military use, he also read literature and history and was practiced in documents.
translations.idiomatic: He was a soldier who also read history and handled documents.

sentences.zh: 後為裴叔業司馬，帶汝陰太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu reached Zhongli, Yuanhu was then in the city; as Xiao Luan's Governor of Xuzhou Xiao Huixiu he was sent as envoy to the army; Gaozu saw him and favored him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen reached Zhongli, Yuanhu was envoy from Xuzhou and impressed him.

sentences.zh: 叔業歸順，元護贊同其謀。

translations.literal: Later he was Pei Shuye's marshal with concurrent Administrator of Ruyin.
translations.idiomatic: He became Shuye's marshal at Ruyin.

sentences.zh: 及叔業疾病，外內阻貳，元護督率上下，以俟援軍。

translations.literal: When Shuye turned to allegiance, Yuanhu supported his plan.
translations.idiomatic: He backed Shuye's defection.

sentences.zh: 壽春克定，元護頗有力焉。

translations.literal: When Shuye fell ill, inside and outside were divided in loyalty; Yuanhu supervised and led those above and below to await relief troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuye fell ill Yuanhu held the garrison together until relief came.

sentences.zh: 景明初，以元護為輔國將軍、齊州刺史、廣饒縣開國伯，食邑一千戶，便道述職。

translations.literal: When Shouchun was pacified, Yuanhu had considerable strength in it.
translations.idiomatic: He played a major part in taking Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 其年入朝。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingming he was made General Who Assists the State, Governor of Qizhou, and Baron of Guangrao with a thousand households, proceeding directly to his post.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingming year 1 he was made General Who Assists the State, Governor of Qizhou, and Baron of Guangrao.

sentences.zh: 尋以州民柳世明圖為不軌，元護馳還歷城，至即擒殄，誅戮所加，微為濫酷。

translations.literal: That year he entered court.
translations.idiomatic: He visited court that year.

sentences.zh: 值州內飢儉，民人困弊，志存隱恤，表請賑貸，蠲其賦役。

translations.literal: Soon because the provincial people Liu Shiming plotted unrest, Yuanhu galloped back to Licheng; on arrival he seized and destroyed them; those he punished were slightly excessive in slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: He crushed Liu Shiming's plot in Qizhou, though harshly.

sentences.zh: 但多有部曲，時為侵擾，城邑苦之，故不得為良刺史也。

translations.literal: When famine struck the province and the people were distressed, his will was to give hidden relief; he memorialized requesting relief loans and remitting their taxes and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: He sought tax relief during famine.

sentences.zh: 三年夏卒，年五十一。

translations.literal: But he had many retainers who at times encroached and harassed; the walled cities suffered—therefore he could not be a good governor.
translations.idiomatic: His retainers oppressed the people, spoiling his good intentions.

sentences.zh: 病前月餘，京師無故傳其凶問。

translations.literal: In the third year of summer he died, aged fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in summer of year 3 at fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 又城外送客亭柱，有人書曰「李齊州死」。

translations.literal: More than a month before his illness, in the capital his death was rumored without cause.
translations.idiomatic: A month before his death rumors spread in the capital.

sentences.zh: 綱佐餞別者見而拭之，後復如此。

translations.literal: Also on a guest pavilion pillar outside the city someone wrote "Li of Qizhou is dead."
translations.idiomatic: Someone wrote "Li of Qizhou is dead" on a pavilion post.

sentences.zh: 元護妾妓十餘，聲色自縱。

translations.literal: Staff who saw it wiped it away; later it appeared again.
translations.idiomatic: Officials erased it; it reappeared.

sentences.zh: 情慾既甚，支骨消削，鬚長二尺，一時落盡。

translations.literal: Yuanhu had more than ten concubines and singing girls and indulged sound and color.
translations.idiomatic: He kept many concubines.

sentences.zh: 贈平東將軍、青州刺史。

translations.literal: Desire being extreme, his limbs wasted; his beard, two chi long, fell out all at once.
translations.idiomatic: Lust wasted him; his two-chi beard fell out.

sentences.zh: 元護為齊州，經拜舊墓，巡省故宅，饗賜村老，莫不欣暢。

translations.literal: Posthumously made General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 及將亡，謂左右曰：「吾嘗以方伯簿伍至青州，士女屬目。

translations.literal: As governor of Qizhou he once visited old tombs and inspected his former house, feasting and bestowing on village elders—all were pleased.
translations.idiomatic: As governor he visited his old home and feasted the village elders.

sentences.zh: 若喪過東陽，不可不好設儀衞，哭泣盡哀，令觀者改容也。

translations.literal: When about to die he told attendants: "I once came to Qingzhou as a registrar—men and women looked at me."
translations.idiomatic: Dying, he ordered a grand funeral procession through Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 」家人遵其誡。

translations.literal: "If the coffin passes Dongyang, you must set out rites and guards well, weep with full grief, and make onlookers change expression."
translations.idiomatic: He wanted mourners to impress the crowds.

sentences.zh: 子會，襲。

translations.literal: His family followed his instruction.
translations.idiomatic: His family obeyed.

sentences.zh: 正始中，降爵為子，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: His son Hui inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hui inherited.

sentences.zh: 延昌中，除宣威將軍、給事中。

translations.literal: In Zhengshi, his rank was reduced to viscount with five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengshi his title was reduced to viscount.

sentences.zh: 會頑騃好酒，其妻，南陽太守清河房伯玉女也，甚有姿色，會不答之。

translations.literal: In Yanchang he was made General Who Establishes Might and Attendant Within.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanchang he was made General Who Establishes Might and Attendant Within.

sentences.zh: 房乃通於其弟機，因會飲醉，殺之。

translations.literal: Hui was stupid and fond of wine; his wife was the daughter of Administrator of Nanyang Fang Boyu of Qinghe, very beautiful in appearance; Hui did not respond to her.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was a drunk who neglected his beautiful wife.

sentences.zh: 子景宣襲。

translations.literal: Fang then had relations with his younger brother Ji and, taking advantage of Hui's drunkenness, killed him.
translations.idiomatic: His father-in-law Fang seduced his brother Ji and murdered Hui while drunk.

sentences.zh: 天平中，除給事中。

translations.literal: His son Jingxuan inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingxuan inherited.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，例降。

translations.literal: In the Tianping era he was made Attendant Within.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianping he was Attendant Within.

sentences.zh: 機與房遂如夫婦。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, his rank was reduced by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi took the throne his title was reduced.

sentences.zh: 積十餘年，房氏色衰，乃更婚娶。

translations.literal: Ji and Fang then lived as husband and wife.
translations.idiomatic: Ji lived with Fang as man and wife.

sentences.zh: 元護弟靜，景明初，以歸誠勳拜前將軍。

translations.literal: After more than ten years Fang's beauty faded and he again married.
translations.idiomatic: After ten years Fang remarried.

sentences.zh: 性甚貪忍，兄亡未斂，便剝脫諸妓服玩及餘財物。

translations.literal: Yuanhu's younger brother Jing; in the first year of Jingming, by merit of turning to allegiance he was made Forward General.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was made Forward General for the family's defection.

sentences.zh: 歷齊州內史、天水太守。

translations.literal: By nature very greedy and cruel; before his elder brother's corpse was encoffined he stripped the singing girls' dress and trinkets and remaining property.
translations.idiomatic: Before his brother was buried Jing stole the household goods.

sentences.zh: 靜子鉉，羽林監。
