translations.literal: He passed through Interior Minister of Qizhou and Administrator of Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Interior Minister of Qizhou and Administrator of Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 元護從叔恤，卒於東代郡太守。

translations.literal: Jing's son Xuan was Supervisor of the Feathered Forest.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xuan was Supervisor of the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 子曠之。

translations.literal: Yuanhu's paternal uncle Xu died as Administrator of Eastern Dai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Xu died as Administrator of Eastern Dai.

sentences.zh: 席法友，安定人也。

translations.literal: His son Kuangzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Kuangzhi.

sentences.zh: 祖父南奔。

translations.literal: His grandfather fled south.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather fled south to the Liang.

sentences.zh: 法友仕蕭鸞，以膂力自效軍勳，稍遷至安豐、新蔡二郡太守，建安戍主。

translations.literal: Fayou served Xiao Luan; by physical strength he showed merit in military achievement and was gradually moved to Administrator of Anfeng and New Cai and garrison commander of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: Fayou served Xiao Luan and rose by strength to govern Anfeng and New Cai.

sentences.zh: [3]蕭寶卷遣胡景略代之。

translations.literal: [3] Xiao Baojuan sent Hu Jinglue to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: [3] Xiao Baojuan sent Hu Jinglue to replace him.

sentences.zh: 法友遂留壽春，與叔業同謀歸國。

translations.literal: Fayou then remained at Shouchun and with Shuye jointly plotted to enter Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Fayou stayed at Shouchun and plotted defection with Shuye.

sentences.zh: 景明初，拜冠軍將軍、豫州刺史、苞信縣開國伯，食邑千戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingming he was made General Who Establishes Valor, Governor of Yuzhou, and Baron of Baoxin with a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingming year 1 he was made General Who Establishes Valor, Governor of Yuzhou, and Baron of Baoxin.

sentences.zh: 始叔業卒後，法友與裴植追成叔業志，淮南克定，法友有力焉。

translations.literal: When Shuye first died, Fayou with Pei Zhi pursued completion of Shuye's intent; the Huai was pacified—Fayou had strength in it.
translations.idiomatic: After Shuye's death Fayou and Pei Zhi secured the Huai, with Fayou playing a major role.

sentences.zh: 尋轉冠軍將軍、華州刺史，未拜，改授并州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to General Who Establishes Valor and Governor of Huazhou; before appointment he was changed to Governor of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon moved to Huazhou, then Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 歲餘代還。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was replaced and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He returned after a year.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍遣將楊公則寇揚州，假法友征虜將軍以討之。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan sent General Yang Gongze to invade Yangzhou; Fayou was made acting General Who Captures Barbarians to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan sent Yang Gongze against Yangzhou; Fayou was sent to repel him.

sentences.zh: 法友未至而公則敗走。

translations.literal: Before Fayou arrived Gongze was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Gongze fled before Fayou arrived.

sentences.zh: 後假法友前將軍、持節，為別將出淮南，欲解朐山之圍。

translations.literal: Later Fayou was made acting Forward General with the Staff as Separate General into the Huai, wishing to relieve the siege of Qushan.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was sent as Separate General to relieve Qushan.

sentences.zh: 法友始渡淮而朐山敗沒，遂停散十年。

translations.literal: Fayou had just crossed the Huai when Qushan fell; he then stopped and was idle ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Qushan fell as he crossed the Huai; he was idle ten years.

sentences.zh: 恬靜自處，不競勢利。

translations.literal: Quiet and self-contained, he did not compete for power and profit.
translations.idiomatic: He lived quietly, shunning power.

sentences.zh: 世宗末，以本將軍除濟州刺史。

translations.literal: At the end of Shizong's reign he was made his former generalship and Governor of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Xuanwu's reign he governed Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 在州廉和著稱。

translations.literal: In the province he was known for leniency and harmony.
translations.idiomatic: He was praised for mild rule in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 又徙封乘氏。

translations.literal: His enfeoffment was again moved to Chengsi.
translations.idiomatic: His fief was moved to Chengsi.

sentences.zh: 肅宗初，拜光祿大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Suzong he was made Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Under Suzong he was Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 熙平二年卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiping he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Xiping year 2.

sentences.zh: 贈平西將軍、秦州刺史，贈帛三百匹，諡襄侯。

translations.literal: Posthumously made General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Qinzhou; granted three hundred bolts of silk; posthumous name Marquis Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Qinzhou, with the posthumous title Marquis Xiang.

sentences.zh: 子景通，襲。

translations.literal: His son Jingtong inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingtong inherited.

sentences.zh: 善事元叉，兼以貨賂叉父繼，繼為司空，引景通為掾。

translations.literal: Skilled at serving Yuan Cha, and also with bribes to Cha's father Ji—when Ji was Minister of Works he drew Jingtong as staff.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtong curried favor with Yuan Cha and his father.

sentences.zh: 後加右軍將軍、鎮軍將軍，卒官。

translations.literal: Later he was made General of the Right Army and Pacifying Army General and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to General of the Right Army and died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈輔國將軍、衞尉少卿。

translations.literal: Posthumously made General Who Assists the State and Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General Who Assists the State and Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 子鶠，襲。

translations.literal: His son Yan inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yan inherited.

sentences.zh: 永安末，尚書郎。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongtai he was Master of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yongtai he was Master of Writing.

sentences.zh: 走關西。

translations.literal: He fled west of the passes.
translations.idiomatic: He fled west of the passes.

sentences.zh: 王世弼，京兆霸城人也。

translations.literal: Wang Shibi was a man of Bacheng in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shibi was from Bacheng in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 劉裕滅姚泓，其祖父從裕南遷。

translations.literal: When Liu Yu destroyed Yao Hong, his grandfather followed Yu south in migration.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather followed Liu Yu south when Yao Hong fell.

sentences.zh: 世弼身長七尺八寸，魁岸有壯氣。

translations.literal: Shibi was seven chi eight inches tall, imposing with stalwart spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Shibi was tall and imposing.

sentences.zh: 善草隸書，好愛墳典。

translations.literal: Skilled in cursive and clerical script, he loved and treasured the classics.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled in calligraphy and loved the classics.

sentences.zh: 仕蕭鸞，以軍勳至游擊將軍，為軍主，助戍壽春，遂與叔業同謀歸誠。

translations.literal: He served Xiao Luan and by military merit reached General of Mobile Attack, as army commander helping garrison Shouchun; he then joined Shuye in plotting allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: He served Xiao Luan, garrisoned Shouchun, and joined Shuye's defection.

sentences.zh: 景明初，除冠軍將軍、南徐州刺史，擬戍鍾離，懸封慎縣開國伯，食邑七百戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingming he was made General Who Establishes Valor and Governor of Southern Xuzhou, slated to garrison Zhongli, enfeoffed Baron of Shen county with seven hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingming year 1 he was to garrison Zhongli as Baron of Shen.

sentences.zh: 後以本將軍除東徐州刺史，治任於刑，為民所怨，有受納之響。

translations.literal: Later by his former generalship he was made Governor of Eastern Xuzhou; his government relied on punishments and the people resented him—there was a reputation for taking bribes.
translations.idiomatic: As Governor of Eastern Xuzhou he ruled harshly and was accused of bribery.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，為御史中尉李平所彈，會赦免。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was impeached by Imperial Inquisitor Li Ping; he was pardoned by amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ping impeached him; an amnesty saved him.

sentences.zh: 久之，拜太中大夫，加征虜將軍。

translations.literal: After a long time he was made Grand Master of the Palace with the additional General Who Captures Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was Grand Master of the Palace and General Who Captures Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 尋以本將軍出為河北太守，治有清稱。

translations.literal: Soon by his former generalship he went out as Administrator of Hebei, with a clear reputation in government.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Hebei with a clean reputation.

sentences.zh: 轉勃海相，尋遷中山內史，加平北將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chancellor of Bohai, then moved to Interior Minister of Zhongshan with the additional General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: He became Chancellor of Bohai and Interior Minister of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 直閤元羅，領軍叉弟也，曾行過中山，謂世弼曰：「二州刺史，翻復為郡，亦當恨恨耳。

translations.literal: Direct Attendant Yuan Luo, younger brother of Commander-in-Chief Cha, once passed through Zhongshan and said to Shibi: "Two provincial governors, turned back to be commandery administrators—you must resent it too."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Luo taunted him for demotion from governor to commandery administrator.

sentences.zh: 」世弼曰：「儀同之號，起自鄧隲；

translations.literal: Shibi said: "The title Equal-in-Rank began with Deng Zhi; Pacifying the North as commandery began with your servant."
translations.idiomatic: Shibi replied that Pacifying the North as a commandery post began with him.

sentences.zh: 平北為郡，始在下官。

translations.literal: Pacifying the North as commandery began with your servant.
translations.idiomatic: Pacifying the North as a commandery post began with me.

sentences.zh: 」正光元年卒官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengguang he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in Zhengguang year 1.

sentences.zh: 贈本將軍、豫州刺史，諡曰康。

translations.literal: Posthumously given his former generalship and Governor of Yuzhou; posthumous name Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made his former rank and Governor of Yuzhou, with the posthumous name Kang.

sentences.zh: 長子會，汝陽太守。

translations.literal: His eldest son Hui was Administrator of Ruyang.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Hui was Administrator of Ruyang.

sentences.zh: 次子由，字茂道。

translations.literal: His second son You, style Maodao.
translations.idiomatic: His second son You, courtesy name Maodao.

sentences.zh: 好學，有文才，尤善草隸。

translations.literal: He loved learning and had literary talent, especially skilled in cursive and clerical.
translations.idiomatic: You was learned and skilled in calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 性方厚，有名士之風。

translations.literal: By nature square and generous, he had the air of a famed gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He had the bearing of a gentleman.

sentences.zh: 又工摹畫，為時人所服。

translations.literal: Also skilled at tracing paintings, he was admired by men of the time.
translations.idiomatic: He was also admired as a painter.

sentences.zh: 歷給事中、尚書郎、東萊太守。

translations.literal: He passed through Attendant Within, Master of Writing, and Administrator of Donglai.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Attendant, Master of Writing, and Administrator of Donglai.

sentences.zh: 罷郡後寓居潁川。

translations.literal: After leaving the commandery he lodged in Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving office he lived in Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 天平初，元洪威構逆，大軍攻討，為亂兵所害，時年四十三。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianping, Yuan Hongwei plotted rebellion; the great army attacked; he was killed by disorderly troops, aged forty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianping year 1 he was killed in Yuan Hongwei's rebellion at forty-three.

sentences.zh: 名流悼惜之。

translations.literal: Famed gentlemen mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: Men of note mourned him.

sentences.zh: 江悅之，字彥和，濟陽考城人也。

translations.literal: Jiang Yuezhi, style Yanhe, was a man of Kaocheng in Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yuezhi, courtesy name Yanhe, was from Kaocheng in Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 七世祖統，晉散騎常侍。

translations.literal: His seventh-generation ancestor Tong was Jin Regular Attendant at the Leisurely Riders.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestor Tong of the seventh generation was Jin Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 劉淵、石勒之亂，南徙渡江。

translations.literal: In the disorders of Liu Yuan and Shi Le they migrated south across the river.
translations.idiomatic: His line fled south in the Jin disorders.

sentences.zh: 祖興之，父範之，並為劉裕所誅。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xingzhi and father Fanzhi were both executed by Liu Yu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather and father were executed by Liu Yu.

sentences.zh: 悅之少孤。

translations.literal: Yuezhi was orphaned in youth.
translations.idiomatic: Yuezhi was orphaned young.

sentences.zh: 仕劉駿，歷諸王參軍。

translations.literal: He served Liu Jun, passing through staff posts for various princes.
translations.idiomatic: He served Liu Jun on princes' staffs.

sentences.zh: 好兵書，有將略，善待士，有部曲數百人。

translations.literal: He loved military books, had military stratagem, was good at treating gentlemen, and had several hundred retainers.
translations.idiomatic: He read military texts, commanded men, and kept hundreds of retainers.

sentences.zh: 蕭道成初，以悅之為荊州征西府中兵參軍，領臺軍主。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiao Daocheng he was made Army Staff Adviser of the Western Expedition Office of Jingzhou and Commander of the Capital Army.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xiao Daocheng he was staff officer at Jingzhou and capital army commander.

sentences.zh: 遷屯騎校尉，轉後軍將軍。

translations.literal: He was moved to Colonel of the Garrison Cavalry and transferred to Rear General.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Colonel of the Garrison Cavalry and Rear General.

sentences.zh: 部曲稍眾，千有餘人。

translations.literal: His retainers gradually grew numerous—more than a thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: His retinue grew to over a thousand.

sentences.zh: 蕭賾遣戍漢中，就遷輔國將軍。

translations.literal: Xiao Ze sent him to garrison Hanzhong and he was then moved to General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Ze garrisoned him in Hanzhong as General Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍初，劉季連據蜀反叛，悅之率部曲及梁秦之眾討滅之，以功進號冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiao Yan, Liu Jilian held Shu in rebellion; Yuezhi led retainers and Liang-Qin troops to destroy him and by merit was advanced to General Who Establishes Valor.
translations.idiomatic: He crushed Liu Jilian's rebellion in Shu and was promoted to General Who Establishes Valor.

sentences.zh: 武興氐破白馬，進圖南鄭，悅之率軍拒戰，大破氐眾，還復白馬。

translations.literal: The Di of Wuxing broke Baima and advanced toward Nanzheng; Yuezhi led troops to resist, routed the Di host greatly, and recovered Baima.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated the Di at Baima and recovered the post.

sentences.zh: 衍秦梁二州刺史莊丘黑死，夏侯道遷與悅之及龐樹、軍主李忻榮、張元亮、士孫天與等，謀以梁州內附。

translations.literal: When Yan's Governor of Qin and Liang Zhuang Qiu Hei died, Xiahou Daoqian with Yuezhi and Pang Shu, Army Commander Li Xinxing, Zhang Yuanliang, and Shi Sun Tianyu plotted to submit Liangzhou to inner allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuang Qiu Hei died, Yuezhi joined Daoqian's plot to defect Liangzhou to Wei.

sentences.zh: 既殺蕭衍使者及楊靈珍，衍華陽太守尹天寶率眾向州城。

translations.literal: After killing Yan's envoys and Yang Lingzhen, Yan's Administrator of Huayang Yin Tianbao led a host toward the provincial city.
translations.idiomatic: After killing Liang envoys, Yin Tianbao marched on Nanzheng.

sentences.zh: 悅之與樹、忻榮勒眾逆戰，為天寶所敗，遂圍南鄭。

translations.literal: Yuezhi with Shu and Xinxing led troops to meet in battle and was defeated by Tianbao, who then besieged Nanzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yuezhi was defeated and Nanzheng besieged.

sentences.zh: 戰經四日，眾心危沮，咸懷離貳。

translations.literal: After four days of battle popular hearts were perilous and fearful; all harbored division in loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: After four days morale cracked.

sentences.zh: 悅之盡以家財散賞士卒，身當矢刃，晝夜督戰。

translations.literal: Yuezhi distributed all family wealth to reward soldiers and personally met blades and arrows, supervising battle day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Yuezhi spent his fortune on the troops and fought day and night.

sentences.zh: 會武興軍至，天寶敗走。

translations.literal: When Wuxing's army arrived Tianbao was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Wuxing reinforcements routed Tianbao.

sentences.zh: 道遷之克全勳款，悅之實有力焉。

translations.literal: In Daoqian's complete achievement of merit and sincerity, Yuezhi truly had strength in it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuezhi was vital to Daoqian's success.

sentences.zh: 正始二年夏，與道遷俱至洛陽。

translations.literal: In the second year of summer of Zhengshi he arrived at Luoyang with Daoqian.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengshi year 2 he reached Luoyang with Daoqian.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: Soon he died, aged sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 贈輔國將軍、梁州刺史，追封安平縣開國子，食邑三百戶，諡曰莊。

translations.literal: Posthumously made General Who Assists the State and Governor of Liangzhou; posthumously enfeoffed Viscount of Anping with three hundred households; posthumous name Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General Who Assists the State and Governor of Liangzhou, Viscount of Anping, with the posthumous name Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 悅之二子，文遙、文遠。

translations.literal: Yuezhi had two sons, Wenyao and Wenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Wenyao and Wenyuan.

sentences.zh: 文遙，少有大度，輕財好士，士多歸之。

translations.literal: Wenyao in youth had great magnanimity, lightly valued wealth and loved gentlemen—many gentlemen followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyao was generous and gathered followers.

sentences.zh: 道遷之圖楊靈珍也，文遙奮劍請行，遂手斬靈珍。

translations.literal: In Daoqian's plot against Yang Lingzhen, Wenyao drew sword and requested to go and with his own hand beheaded Lingzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyao personally beheaded Yang Lingzhen in Daoqian's coup.

sentences.zh: 正始二年，除步兵校尉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengshi he was made Colonel of the Foot Soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengshi year 2 he was Colonel of the Foot Soldiers.

sentences.zh: 遭父憂解官。

translations.literal: He met with mourning for his father and left office.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 永平初，襲封，拜前軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongping he inherited the enfeoffment and was appointed Forward General.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongping year 1 he inherited and was made Forward General.

sentences.zh: 出為咸陽太守。

translations.literal: He went out as Administrator of Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was Administrator of Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 勤於禮接，終日坐廳事，至者見之，假以恩顏，屏人密問。

translations.literal: Diligent in ritual reception, he sat in the hall all day; when visitors came he lent them a gracious face and in private asked closely.
translations.idiomatic: He received petitioners all day and learned every grievance and thief's name.

sentences.zh: 於是民所疾苦、大盜姓名、姦猾吏長，無不知悉，郡中震肅，姦劫息止，治為雍州諸郡之最。

translations.literal: Thus the people's hardships, great robbers' names, and crafty officials were all known without exception; the commandery was shaken into severity, wicked robbery ceased, and his government was the best of Yongzhou's commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: His district became the best-governed in Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 徵拜驍騎將軍、輔國將軍，進號征虜將軍。

translations.literal: He was summoned as General of Valiant Cavalry and General Who Assists the State, advanced to General Who Captures Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as General of Valiant Cavalry and General Who Captures Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 肅宗初，拜平原太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Suzong he was made Administrator of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Suzong he was Administrator of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 在郡六年，政理如在咸陽。

translations.literal: In the commandery six years, his government was as in Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: For six years he governed Pingyuan as he had Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 長史許思祖等以文遙遺愛在民，復推其子果行州事。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Xu Sinu and others, because Wenyao's legacy of love remained with the people, again pushed his son Guo to act in provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The people pushed his son Guo to govern.

sentences.zh: 既攝州任，乃遣使奉表。

translations.literal: Having taken provincial charge, he then sent envoys with a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Guo memorialized the throne.

sentences.zh: 莊帝嘉之，除果通直散騎侍郎、假節、龍驤將軍、行安州事、當州都督。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuang praised this and made Guo Regular Attendant Direct Communication, acting Bearer of the Staff, Dragon Cavalry General, acting in Anzhou affairs and Commander-in-Chief of the province.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang made Guo Regular Attendant and acting commander of Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 既而賊勢轉盛，臺援不接，果以阻隔強寇，內徙無由，乃攜諸弟并率城民東奔高麗。

translations.literal: Soon bandit power turned stronger; capital relief did not connect; because he was blocked by strong bandits and could not migrate inward, he then took his younger brothers and led the city populace east to flee to Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Cut off by rebels, Guo fled east to Goguryeo with his kin.

sentences.zh: 天平中，[4]詔高麗送果等。

translations.literal: In the Tianping era, [4] an edict ordered Goguryeo to send Guo and others back.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianping year [4] Goguryeo was ordered to return them.

sentences.zh: 元象中，乃得還朝。

translations.literal: In the Yuanxiang era they were able to return to court.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanxiang they returned to court.

sentences.zh: 果弟昴，武定三年襲爵。

translations.literal: Guo's younger brother Mao in the third year of Wuding inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Mao inherited in Wuding year 3.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, his rank was reduced by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi took the throne his title was reduced.

sentences.zh: 文遠，善騎射，勇於攻戰。

translations.literal: Wenyuan was skilled at mounted archery and brave in attack and battle.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyuan was a bold cavalryman.

sentences.zh: 以軍勳致效，自給事中稍遷中散大夫、龍驤將軍。

translations.literal: By military merit he showed effect; from Attendant Within he was gradually moved to Grand Master of the Palace and Dragon Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: He rose by merit to Grand Master and Dragon Cavalry General.

sentences.zh: 龐樹，南安人。

translations.literal: Pang Shu was a man of Nan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Shu was from Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 世宗追錄謀勳，封其子景亮襄邑縣開國男，食邑二百戶。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong posthumously recorded plotting merit and enfeoffed his son Jingliang as Baron of Xiangyi with two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanwu enfeoffed Shu's son Jingliang as Baron of Xiangyi.

sentences.zh: 李忻榮，漢中人。

translations.literal: Li Xinxing was a man of Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xinxing was from Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 與樹俱擊天寶，同時戰歿。

translations.literal: With Shu he together struck Tianbao and at the same time died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He fell fighting Tianbao with Pang Shu.

sentences.zh: 封其子建為清水縣開國子，食邑二百戶。

translations.literal: Posthumously his son Jian was enfeoffed Viscount of Qingshui with two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jian was enfeoffed Viscount of Qingshui.

sentences.zh: 張元亮，漢中人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yuanliang was a man of Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yuanliang was from Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 便弓馬，善戰鬬。

translations.literal: Skilled with bow and horse, good at fighting.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in archery and combat.

sentences.zh: 以勳封撫夷縣開國子，食邑二百戶。

translations.literal: By merit enfeoffed Viscount of Fuyi with two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed Viscount of Fuyi.

sentences.zh: 拜東萊太守，入為平遠將軍、左中郎將。

translations.literal: He was made Administrator of Donglai and entered court as General Who Pacifies the Distant and Left General of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He became Administrator of Donglai and Left General of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 遷中散大夫，加龍驤將軍。

translations.literal: He was moved to Grand Master of the Palace with the additional Dragon Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: He was Grand Master with Dragon Cavalry General.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈左將軍、巴州刺史。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made General of the Left and Governor of Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General of the Left and Governor of Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 士孫天與，扶風人。

translations.literal: Shi Sun Tianyu was a man of Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Sun Tianyu was from Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 以勳封莫西縣開國男，食邑二百戶。

translations.literal: By merit enfeoffed Baron of Moxi with two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed Baron of Moxi.

sentences.zh: 拜武功太守。

translations.literal: He was made Administrator of Wugong.
translations.idiomatic: He was Administrator of Wugong.

sentences.zh: 又襄陽羅道珍、北海王安世、潁川辛諶、漢中姜永等，皆參其勳末。

translations.literal: Also Xiangyang's Luo Daozhen, Beihai's Wang Anshi, Yingchuan's Xin Chen, and Hanzhong's Jiang Yong—all shared in the tail of the merit.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Daozhen, Wang Anshi, Xin Chen, and Jiang Yong shared in the rewards.

sentences.zh: 道珍，除齊州東平原相，有治稱。

translations.literal: Daozhen was made Chancellor of Eastern Pingyuan in Qizhou and had a reputation for good government.
translations.idiomatic: Daozhen governed Eastern Pingyuan well.

sentences.zh: 卒於鎮遠將軍、屯騎校尉。

translations.literal: He died as General Who Pacifies the Distant and Colonel of the Garrison Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He died as General Who Pacifies the Distant.

sentences.zh: 安世，苻堅丞相王猛之玄孫也。

translations.literal: Anshi was the great-great-grandson of Former Qin Chief Minister Wang Meng.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi descended from Wang Meng of Former Qin.

sentences.zh: 歷涉書傳，敏於人間。

translations.literal: He ranged through books and records and was quick-witted among men.
translations.idiomatic: He was widely read and quick-witted.

sentences.zh: 自羽林監稍遷安西將軍、北華州刺史。

translations.literal: From Supervisor of the Feathered Forest he was gradually moved to General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Northern Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to General Who Pacifies the West.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈本將軍、梁州刺史。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously given his former generalship and Governor of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Governor of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 諶，魏衞尉辛毗之後。

translations.literal: Chen was a descendant of Wei Minister of the Guard Xin Pi.
translations.idiomatic: Chen descended from Xin Pi.

sentences.zh: 有文學。

translations.literal: He had literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: He was literate.

sentences.zh: 歷步兵校尉，濮陽、上黨二郡太守。

translations.literal: He passed through Colonel of the Foot Soldiers and the two Administrators of Puyang and Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: He served as colonel and administrator of Puyang and Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈征虜將軍、梁州刺史。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made General Who Captures Barbarians and Governor of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General Who Captures Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 子儒之，濟州司馬。

translations.literal: His son Ruzhi was Marshal of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ruzhi was Marshal of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 永，善彈琴，有文學。

translations.literal: Yong was skilled at playing the zither and had literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: Yong played the zither and wrote well.

sentences.zh: 員外郎、梁州別駕、漢中太守。

translations.literal: Attendant Outside the Sequence, Vice Administrator of Liangzhou, and Administrator of Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He was Attendant, Vice Administrator of Liangzhou, and Administrator of Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 永弟漾，亦善士。

translations.literal: Yong's younger brother Yang was also a good gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Yang was also esteemed.

sentences.zh: 性亦至孝，為漢中所歎服。

translations.literal: By nature also utmost filial, he was admired in Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Yang was famed for filial piety in Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 元羅之陷也，永入於建鄴，遂死焉。

translations.literal: When Yuan Luo fell, Yong entered Jiankang and died there.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Luo fell Yong went to Jiankang and died there.

sentences.zh: 時有潁川庾道者，[5]亦與道遷俱入國，雖不參謀，亦為奇士。

translations.literal: At that time Yingchuan's Yu Daozhe, [5] also entered Wei with Daoqian; though he did not join in counsel, he was also an extraordinary man.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Daozhe of Yingchuan also defected with Daoqian as an eccentric scholar.

sentences.zh: 歷覽史傳，善草隸書，輕財重義。

translations.literal: He ranged through historical records, was skilled in cursive and clerical script, lightly valued wealth and heavily valued righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He read history, wrote well, and valued honor over money.

sentences.zh: 仕蕭衍，右中郎將，助戍漢中。

translations.literal: He served Xiao Yan as Right General of the Guard and helped garrison Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He had served Liang at Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 及至洛陽，環堵弊廬。

translations.literal: When he reached Luoyang he lived in a ring of walls and a shabby hut.
translations.idiomatic: In Luoyang he lived in poverty.

sentences.zh: 多與儁秀交舊，積二十餘歲，殊無宦情。

translations.literal: He associated much with outstanding old friends; for more than twenty years he had no desire for office.
translations.idiomatic: For twenty years he refused office and kept scholarly company.

sentences.zh: 正光中，乃除幽州左將軍府主簿，饒安令。

translations.literal: In Zhengguang he was at last made Staff Master of the Left General's office of Youzhou and Magistrate of Rao'an.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengguang he briefly served as staff master and magistrate.

sentences.zh: 罷縣後，仍客遊齊魯之間。

translations.literal: After leaving the county he still wandered as guest between Qi and Lu.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving office he wandered Qi and Lu.

sentences.zh: 天平中，卒於青州。

translations.literal: In the Tianping era he died in Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Qingzhou during Tianping.

sentences.zh: 時有皇甫徽，字子玄，安定朝那人。

translations.literal: At that time Huangfu Hui, style Zixuan, was a man of Zhaoge in Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Hui, courtesy name Zixuan, was from Zhaoge in Anding.

sentences.zh: 仕蕭衍，歷諸王參軍、郡守。

translations.literal: He served Xiao Yan, passing through staff for princes and commandery administrators.
translations.idiomatic: He had served Liang as staff and administrator.

sentences.zh: 及道遷之入國也，徽亦因地內屬。

translations.literal: When Daoqian entered Wei, Hui also followed the territory in inner submission.
translations.idiomatic: When Daoqian defected Hui came over too.

sentences.zh: 徽妻即道遷之兄女，道遷列上勳書，欲以徽為元謀。

translations.literal: Hui's wife was Daoqian's elder brother's daughter; Daoqian listed merit and wished to make Hui the primary plotter.
translations.idiomatic: Daoqian wanted to credit his nephew-in-law Hui as chief plotter.

sentences.zh: 徽曰：「創謀之始，本不關預，雖貪榮賞，實內愧於心。

translations.literal: Hui said: "At the beginning of founding the plot I was not involved; though I covet glory and reward, in truth I feel shame within."
translations.idiomatic: Hui refused: "I did not start the plot and would be ashamed to take chief credit."

sentences.zh: 」遂拒而不許。

translations.literal: He then refused and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He refused the honor.

sentences.zh: 後刺史羊祉表授征虜府司馬，卒官。

translations.literal: Later Governor Yang Zuo memorialized appointing him as staff marshal of the office of General Who Captures Barbarians; he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Yang Zuo appointed him staff marshal; he died in office.

sentences.zh: 子和，武定末，司空司馬。

translations.literal: His son He, at the end of Wuding, was Marshal of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His son He was Marshal of the Minister of Works at the end of Wuding.

sentences.zh: 和弟亮，儀曹郎中。

translations.literal: He's younger brother Liang was Master of Writing in the Ceremonial Office.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Liang was in the Ceremonial Office.

sentences.zh: 淳于誕，字靈遠。

translations.literal: Chunyu Yan, style Lingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Chunyu Yan, courtesy name Lingyuan.

sentences.zh: 其先太山博人，後世居於蜀漢，或家安固之桓陵縣。

translations.literal: His ancestors were men of Bowen in Taishan; later generations lived in Shu-Han, or the family was in Huanling county of Anguo in Anding.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors were from Taishan; later the family lived in Shu and Anding.

sentences.zh: [6]父興宗，蕭賾南安太守。

translations.literal: [6] His father Xingzong was Administrator of Nan'an under Xiao Ze.
translations.idiomatic: [6] His father Xingzong was Administrator of Nan'an under Xiao Ze.

sentences.zh: 誕年十二，隨父向揚州。

translations.literal: Yan was twelve when he followed his father toward Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he accompanied his father to Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 父於路為羣盜所害。

translations.literal: His father on the road was killed by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: His father was killed by bandits on the road.

sentences.zh: 誕雖童稚，而哀感奮發，傾資結客，旬朔之內，遂得復讎，由是州里歎異之。

translations.literal: Although Yan was still a child, grief and indignation flared; he spent his assets to gather guests, and within ten days and a month he had avenged it—the district sighed in wonder.
translations.idiomatic: Though a boy, he hired men and avenged his father within weeks, astonishing the district.

sentences.zh: 賾益州刺史劉悛召為主簿。

translations.literal: Ze's Governor of Yizhou Liu Jun summoned him as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jun of Yizhou made him chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍除步兵校尉。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan made him Colonel of the Foot Soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan made him Colonel of the Foot Soldiers.

sentences.zh: 景明中，自漢中歸國。

translations.literal: In the Jingming era he returned to Wei from Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingming he defected from Hanzhong to Wei.

sentences.zh: 既達京師，陳伐蜀之計，世宗嘉納之。

translations.literal: Having reached the capital he presented a plan to campaign against Shu; Emperor Shizong praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: At court he proposed conquering Shu and Xuanwu approved.

sentences.zh: 延昌末，王師大舉，除驍騎將軍，假冠軍將軍，都督別部司馬，領鄉導統軍。

translations.literal: At the end of Yanchang the royal army marched greatly; he was made General of Valiant Cavalry and acting General Who Establishes Valor, Commander Separate Division Staff, leading native-guide overall army.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanchang a great campaign began; he was made guide-general for the Shu expedition.

sentences.zh: 誕不願先受榮爵，乃固讓實官，止參戎號。

translations.literal: Yan was unwilling to receive honorary rank first and firmly declined substantive office, only participating under military title.
translations.idiomatic: He refused honorary rank until merit was earned.

sentences.zh: 及奉辭之日，詔遣主書趙桃弓宣旨勞勉，若克成都，即以益州許之。

translations.literal: On the day of taking leave an edict sent Master of Writing Zhao Taogong to proclaim intent and encourage him: if Chengdu were taken, Yizhou would be granted him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor promised him Yizhou if Chengdu fell.

sentences.zh: 師次晉壽，蜀人大震。

translations.literal: The army halted at Jinshou; the people of Shu were greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: The army reached Jinshou and Shu trembled.

sentences.zh: 屬世宗晏駕，不果而還。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong died suddenly the campaign did not succeed and they returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanwu died the campaign was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 後以客例，起家除羽林監。

translations.literal: Later by guest precedent he began his career as Supervisor of the Feathered Forest.
translations.idiomatic: He later entered service as Supervisor of the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍遣將張齊攻圍益州，詔誕為統軍，與刺史傅豎眼赴援。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan sent General Zhang Qi to besiege Yizhou; an edict made Yan overall commander with Governor Fu Shuyan to relieve.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Qi besieged Yizhou Yan was sent to relieve with Fu Shuyan.

sentences.zh: 事寧還朝。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: After relief he returned to court.

sentences.zh: 正光中，秦隴反叛，詔誕為西南道軍司、假冠軍將軍、別將，從子午南出斜谷趣建安，與行臺魏子建共參經略。

translations.literal: In Zhengguang Qin and Long rebelled; an edict made Yan army staff of the Southwest Route, acting General Who Establishes Valor, Separate General, south from Ziwu through Xiegu toward Jian'an with Mobile Commandant Wei Zijian jointly planning.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengguang he campaigned in the southwest with Wei Zijian.

sentences.zh: 時衍益州刺史蕭淵猷遣將樊文熾、蕭世澄等率眾數萬圍小劍戍，益州刺史邴虬令子達拒之。

translations.literal: At that time Yan's Governor of Yizhou Xiao Yuanyou sent Generals Fan Wench Chi and Xiao Shicheng with tens of thousands to besiege Xiaojian garrison; Governor of Yizhou Bing Qiu ordered his son Da to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyou's generals besieged Xiaojian; Bing Qiu's son resisted.

sentences.zh: [7]因轉營，為文熾所掩，統軍胡小虎、崔珍寶並見俘執。

translations.literal: [7] He then shifted camp and was ambushed by Wench Chi; Overall Commander Hu Xiaohu and Cui Zhenbao were both captured.
translations.idiomatic: [7] Shifting camp, he was ambushed and commanders were captured.

sentences.zh: 子建遣誕助討之。

translations.literal: Zijian sent Yan to help attack.
translations.idiomatic: Zijian sent Yan to relieve.

sentences.zh: 誕勒兵馳赴，相對月餘，未能摧殄。

translations.literal: Yan led troops in gallop; facing each other more than a month, he could not destroy them.
translations.idiomatic: Yan fought a month without victory.

sentences.zh: 文熾軍行之谷，東峯名龍鬚山，置柵其上以防歸路。

translations.literal: Wench Chi's army's marching valley—on the eastern peak was a place called Dragon-Mustache Mountain, with a palisade above to guard the return road.
translations.idiomatic: Wench Chi fortified Dragon-Mustache Mountain above his line of retreat.

sentences.zh: 誕以賊眾難可角力，乃密募壯士二百餘人，令夜登山攻其柵。

translations.literal: Yan judged the bandit host hard to match in force; he then secretly recruited more than two hundred stalwart men and ordered them to climb the mountain by night and attack the palisade.
translations.idiomatic: Yan sent two hundred men to storm the palisade by night.

sentences.zh: 及時火起，[8]煙焰漲天。

translations.literal: When fire rose in time, [8] smoke and flame filled the sky.
translations.idiomatic: [8] Fire lit the sky.

sentences.zh: 賊以還途不守，連營震怖。

translations.literal: The bandits, because the return road was not held, connected camps were shaken in terror.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy panicked, cut off from retreat.

sentences.zh: 誕率諸軍鳴鼓攻擊，文熾大敗，俘斬萬計，擒世澄等十一人。

translations.literal: Yan led the various armies with drumming attack; Wench Chi was routed greatly, capturing and beheading tens of thousands, seizing Shicheng and eleven others.
translations.idiomatic: Yan routed Wench Chi, taking tens of thousands of heads.

sentences.zh: 文熾為元帥，先走獲免。

translations.literal: Wench Chi as commander-in-chief fled first and escaped capture.
translations.idiomatic: Wench Chi fled.

sentences.zh: 孝昌初，子建以誕行華陽郡，帶白馬戍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiaochang, Zijian had Yan act in Huayang commandery with Baima garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaochang year 1 Yan held Huayang and Baima.

sentences.zh: 二年，復以誕行巴州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year he again had Yan act in Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he acted in Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，朝議以梁州安康郡阻帶江山，要害之所，分置東梁州，仍以誕為鎮遠將軍、梁州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year court discussion held that Ankang commandery of Liangzhou, blocked by rivers and mountains, was a strategic place; Eastern Liangzhou was separately established, and Yan was made General Who Pacifies the Distant and Governor of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 Eastern Liangzhou was split off and Yan was made its governor.

sentences.zh: 永安二年四月卒，時年六十。

translations.literal: In the second year of the fourth month of Yongan he died, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yongan year 2, fourth month, at sixty.

sentences.zh: 贈安西將軍、益州刺史，諡曰莊。

translations.literal: Posthumously made General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Yizhou; posthumous name Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Yizhou, with the posthumous name Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 長子亢。

translations.literal: His eldest son Kang.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son was Kang.

sentences.zh: 亢弟胤，字□館。

translations.literal: Kang's younger brother Yin, style □Guan.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yin, courtesy name [illegible].

sentences.zh: 武定末，梁州驃騎府司馬。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuding he was Marshal of the Agile Cavalry staff of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Wuding he was staff marshal in Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 李苗，字子宣，梓潼涪人。

translations.literal: Li Miao, style Zixuan, was a man of Fu in Zitong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Miao, courtesy name Zixuan, was from Fu in Zitong.

sentences.zh: 父膺，蕭衍尚書郎、太僕卿。

translations.literal: His father Ying was Xiao Yan's Master of Writing and Minister of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ying was Liang Master of Writing and Minister of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 苗出後叔父略。

translations.literal: Miao was adopted by his paternal uncle Lue.
translations.idiomatic: Miao was adopted by his uncle Lue.

sentences.zh: [9]略為蕭衍寧州刺史，大著威名。

translations.literal: [9] Lue was Xiao Yan's Governor of Ningzhou and had great martial fame.
translations.idiomatic: [9] Lue was famed as Governor of Ningzhou under Liang.

sentences.zh: 王足伐蜀也，衍命略拒足於涪，許其益州。

translations.literal: When Wang Zu campaigned against Shu, Yan ordered Lue to resist Zu at Fu and promised him Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zu attacked Shu; Yan promised Lue Yizhou if he stopped Zu at Fu.

sentences.zh: 及足還退，衍遂改授。

translations.literal: When Zu returned in retreat, Yan then changed the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When Zu withdrew Yan broke his promise.

sentences.zh: 略怒，將有異圖，衍使人害之。

translations.literal: Lue was angry and was about to plot differently; Yan sent men to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Lue plotted revenge and Yan had him killed.

sentences.zh: 苗年十五，有報雪之心，延昌中遂歸闕。

translations.literal: Miao at fifteen had the heart to avenge blood; in Yanchang he then returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen Miao vowed revenge; in Yanchang he defected to Wei.

sentences.zh: 仍陳圖蜀之計。

translations.literal: He again presented a plan against Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He again proposed conquering Shu.

sentences.zh: 於是大將軍高肇西伐，詔假苗龍驤將軍、鄉導統軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon Grand General Gao Zhao campaigned west; an edict made Miao acting Dragon Cavalry General and native-guide overall army.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhao marched west; Miao was guide-general.

sentences.zh: 師次晉壽，世宗晏駕，班師。

translations.literal: The army halted at Jinshou; Emperor Shizong died suddenly; the army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Jinshou; when Xuanwu died it withdrew.

sentences.zh: 後以客例，除員外散騎侍郎，加襄威將軍。

translations.literal: Later by guest precedent he was made Attendant Outside the Sequence at the Leisurely Riders with the additional General Who Establishes Might.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Attendant Outside the Sequence and General Who Establishes Might.

sentences.zh: 苗有文武才幹，以大功不就，家耻未雪，常懷慷慨。

translations.literal: Miao had civil and military talent and capacity; because great achievement was not realized and family shame was not avenged, he constantly harbored indignation.
translations.idiomatic: Brilliant yet denied vengeance for his uncle, he burned with frustration.

sentences.zh: 乃上書曰：「昔晉室數否，華戎鼎沸，三燕兩秦，咆勃中夏，九服分崩，五方圮裂。

translations.literal: He then submitted a memorial saying: "Formerly the Jin house met repeated misfortune; barbarians and Chinese seethed; three Yan and two Qin roared in the central lands; the nine domains split, the five directions crumbled."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that Jin's fall showed how empires fracture and reunify.

sentences.zh: 皇祚承歷，自北而南，誅滅姦雄，定鼎河洛，唯獨荊揚，尚阻聲教。

translations.literal: "The imperial fortune succeeded the sequence from north to south, executing and destroying traitors and villains, fixing the tripod in He-Luo—only Jing and Yang still blocked sound and teaching."
translations.idiomatic: Wei had reunified the north; only the south remained.

sentences.zh: 今令德廣被於江漢，威風遠振於吳楚，國富兵強，家給人足。

translations.literal: "Now virtue and grace widely cover Jiang and Han, prestige and wind far shake Wu and Chu; the state is rich and soldiers strong, households provided and people sufficient."
translations.idiomatic: Wei was strong and the south weak.

sentences.zh: 以九居八之形，有兼弱攻昧之勢，而欲逸豫，遺疾子孫，違高祖之本圖，非社稷之深慮。

translations.literal: "With the form of nine holding eight, there is the momentum of attacking the weak while they are dim; yet to seek ease and leave illness to descendants violates Gaozu's original plan—not the deep concern of the altars of soil and grain."
translations.idiomatic: To delay conquest was to betray the founding vision.

sentences.zh: 誠宜商度東西戍防輕重之要，計量疆埸險易安危之理，探測南人攻守窺覦之情，籌算卒乘器械征討之備，然後去我所短，避彼所長，釋其至難，攻其甚易，奪其險要，割其膏壤，數年之內，荊揚可并。

translations.literal: "Truly one should weigh east and west garrison light and heavy needs, calculate border strategic easy and dangerous safety, probe southern men's attack-defend and peering intent, plan soldiers chariots weapons and expedition preparation—then discard our shortcomings, avoid their strengths, release their utmost difficulty, attack their very ease, seize their strategic passes, cut their fertile lands; within several years Jing and Yang can be merged."
translations.idiomatic: He urged a calculated southern campaign within years.

sentences.zh: 若捨舟檝，即平原，斂後疏前，則江淮之所短；

translations.literal: If one abandons boats and planks and goes to the plain, gathering rear and scattering front, then the shortness of Jiang and Huai applies.
translations.idiomatic: To fight on plain ground would expose Wei's weakness on the rivers.

sentences.zh: 棄車馬，游飛浪，乘流馳逐，非中國之所長。

translations.literal: abandoning carriage and horses, roaming flying waves, riding currents in chase, is not what China excels at.
translations.idiomatic: Naval war is not Wei's strength.

sentences.zh: 彼不敢入平陸而爭衡，猶我不能越巨川而趣利。

translations.literal: They dare not enter the level land and contend in balance—just as we cannot cross great rivers for profit.
translations.idiomatic: They cannot fight on land; we cannot fight on water.

sentences.zh: 若俱去其短，各恃其長，則東南未見可滅之機，而淮沔方有相持之勢。

translations.literal: If both discard their shortness and each rely on their length, then in the southeast no occasion of extinction is seen, while in Huai and Mian there is a momentum of mutual standoff.
translations.idiomatic: Each side's advantage yields stalemate, not quick conquest.

sentences.zh: 且夫滿昃相傾，陰陽恒理；

translations.literal: And fullness and waning tilt against each other—yin and yang are constant principle;
translations.idiomatic: Fullness and decline obey constant law;

sentences.zh: 盛衰遞襲，五德常運。

translations.literal: success and decline succeed in turn—the five virtues constantly move.
translations.idiomatic: as dynasties rise and fall in turn.

sentences.zh: 今以至強攻至弱，必見吞并之理；

translations.literal: Now to use the utmost strong to attack the utmost weak must see the principle of swallowing and merging;
translations.idiomatic: To crush the weak seems inevitable;

sentences.zh: 如以至弱禦至強，焉有全濟之術？

translations.literal: like using the utmost weak to defend against the utmost strong—how could there be a method of full preservation?
translations.idiomatic: yet the weak defending the strong cannot endure.

sentences.zh: 故明王聖主，皆欲及時立功，為萬世之業。

translations.literal: Therefore enlightened kings and sage lords all wish timely to establish achievement as enterprise for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Sage rulers strike while fortune favors them.

sentences.zh: 去高而就下，百川以之常流；

translations.literal: Going from high to low—the hundred streams flow thus by constant current;
translations.idiomatic: Armies descend from high ground as rivers flow down;

sentences.zh: 取易而避難，兵家以之恒勝。

translations.literal: taking the easy and avoiding the difficult—the military family by this constantly wins.
translations.idiomatic: and take easy ground, as strategists always have.

sentences.zh: 今巴蜀孤懸，去建鄴遼遠，偏兵獨戍，泝流十千，牧守無良，專行劫剝，官由財進，獄以貨成，士民思化，十室而九，延頸北望，日覬王師。

translations.literal: Now Bashu hangs isolated, far from Jiankang; a separate army alone garrisons, upstream ten thousand li; governors are not good, exclusively practicing plunder; office comes by wealth, prisons by goods; gentry and people desire transformation—nine houses in ten; craning necks northward, daily beholding the royal army.
translations.idiomatic: Shu is isolated, corrupt, and longing for Wei.

sentences.zh: 若命一偏將弔民伐罪，風塵不接，可傳檄而定。

translations.literal: If one orders a separate general to console the people and punish crime, without wind and dust of battle, it can be settled by proclamation.
translations.idiomatic: A single column could take it by proclamation.

sentences.zh: 守白帝之阨，據上流之險，循士治之迹，蕩建鄴之逋，然後偃武修文，制禮作樂，天下幸甚，豈不盛哉！

translations.literal: Holding the pass of Baidi and the strategic height of the upper flow, following the traces of scholar governance, sweeping the fugitives of Jiankang, then resting arms and cultivating culture, making rites and music—the world would be greatly fortunate; would it not be splendid!
translations.idiomatic: Then culture could follow conquest.

sentences.zh: 」於時肅宗幼沖，無遠略之意，竟不能納。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Suzong was young and had no far-reaching intent; in the end he could not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Young Emperor Suzong ignored the plan.

sentences.zh: 正光末，二秦反叛，侵及三輔。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhengguang the two Qins rebelled, invading and reaching the three assists.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Zhengguang Qin rebels threatened the capital region.

sentences.zh: 時承平既久，民不習戰。

translations.literal: The time having been long at peace, the people did not practice war.
translations.idiomatic: Peace had left the people unwarlike.

sentences.zh: 苗以隴兵強悍，且羣聚無資，乃上書曰：「臣聞食少兵精，利於速戰；

translations.literal: Miao judged Long troops fierce and strong and that as a gathered host they had no supplies; he submitted a memorial: "Your servant has heard that little food and refined soldiers favor swift battle;
translations.idiomatic: He advised swift attack on the Long rebels, who lacked supplies.

sentences.zh: 糧多卒眾，事宜持久。

translations.literal: much grain and many soldiers—affairs suit endurance."
translations.idiomatic: Many troops need a long campaign.

sentences.zh: 今隴賊猖狂，非有素蓄，雖據兩城，本無德義。

translations.literal: "Now the Long bandits are rampant, not having plain accumulation; though they hold two cities, they fundamentally lack virtue and righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: The rebels held cities but had no legitimacy.

sentences.zh: 其勢在於疾攻，日有降納，遲則人情離阻，坐受崩遺。

translations.literal: "Their momentum lies in swift attack; daily there are surrenders; delay then popular feeling separates and obstructs, sitting to receive collapse and dispersal."
translations.idiomatic: Speed would bring surrenders; delay would dissolve them.

sentences.zh: 夫飈至風起，逆者求萬一之功；

translations.literal: "When the whirlwind arrives and wind rises, the contrary seek merit of one in ten thousand;
translations.idiomatic: Opportunists rush in when fortune turns;

sentences.zh: 高壁深壘，王師有全制之策。

translations.literal: high walls and deep ramparts—the royal army has the policy of full control."
translations.idiomatic: walls and discipline win for the court.

sentences.zh: 但天下久泰，人不曉兵，奔利不相待，逃難不相顧，將無法令，士非教習。

translations.literal: "But the world has long been at peace; men do not understand war; rushing profit they do not wait for each other, fleeing disaster they do not look back at each other; generals have no laws and orders, soldiers lack teaching and practice."
translations.idiomatic: Peacetime officers lacked discipline.

sentences.zh: 以驕將御惰卒，不思長久之計，務奇正之通，必有莫敖輕敵之志，恐無充國持重之規。

translations.literal: "With proud generals commanding lazy soldiers, not thinking of long-term plan, pursuing odd and orthodox communication—there must be the will of Mo Ao to slight the enemy; I fear there is not the measured rule of Chong Guo."
translations.idiomatic: Rash generals risked Mo Ao's arrogance, not Chong Guo's patience.

sentences.zh: 如令隴東不守，汧軍敗散，則二秦遂強，三輔危弱，國之右臂，於斯廢矣。

translations.literal: "If now Long east is not held and Qian army is defeated and scattered, then the two Qins will grow strong, the three assists weak and perilous—the state's right arm is abandoned here."
translations.idiomatic: If Qin fell, the capital's flank would collapse.

sentences.zh: 今且宜勒大將，深溝高壘，堅守勿戰。

translations.literal: "Now for the moment one should order the great general to dig deep moats and raise high ramparts, firmly defend and not battle."
translations.idiomatic: He urged deep defense, not rash attack.

sentences.zh: 別命偏師精兵數千，出麥積崖以襲其後，則汧岐之下，羣妖自散。

translations.literal: "Separately order a separate army of picked soldiers in several thousands out Maiji cliff to strike their rear—then below Qian and Qi the demon host will scatter of itself."
translations.idiomatic: A flanking force through Maiji would break them.

sentences.zh: 」於是詔苗為統軍，與別將淳于誕俱出梁益，隸行臺魏子建。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict made Miao overall commander; with Separate General Chunyu Yan he together went out Liang and Yi, subordinate to Mobile Commandant Wei Zijian.
translations.idiomatic: Miao was made overall commander with Chunyu Yan under Wei Zijian.

sentences.zh: 子建以苗為郎中，仍領軍，深見知待。

translations.literal: Zijian made Miao a Master of Writing and still had him lead the army—he was deeply known and favored.
translations.idiomatic: Zijian trusted him with command.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，還朝，除鎮遠將軍、步兵校尉。

translations.literal: In Xiaochang he returned to court and was made General Who Pacifies the Distant and Colonel of the Foot Soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaochang he returned as General Who Pacifies the Distant.

sentences.zh: 俄兼尚書右丞，為西北道行臺，與大都督宗正珍孫討汾、絳蜀賊，平之。

translations.literal: Soon he was concurrently Right Assistant Minister as Northwest Route Mobile Commandant; with Grand Commander-in-Chief Zongzheng Zhensun he attacked Fen and Jiang Shu bandits and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: He helped crush northwestern rebels.

sentences.zh: 還除司徒司馬，轉太府少卿，加龍驤將軍。

translations.literal: Returning he was made Marshal of the Minister of Education, moved to Vice Minister of the Grand Treasury with the additional Dragon Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Minister of the Grand Treasury.

sentences.zh: 於時蕭衍巴西民何難尉等豪姓，相率請討巴蜀之間，詔苗為通直散騎常侍、冠軍將軍、西南道慰勞大使。

translations.literal: At that time Xiao Yan's Brazilian magnates He Nanwei and others by clans led a request to campaign in the Bashu region; an edict made Miao Regular Attendant Direct Communication, General Who Establishes Valor, and Southwest Route Comforting and Soothing Grand Ambassador.
translations.idiomatic: Liang magnates invited Wei into Bashu; Miao was sent to soothe the southwest.

sentences.zh: 未發，會殺尒朱榮，榮從弟世隆擁榮部曲屯據河橋，還逼都邑。

translations.literal: Before departure the killing of Erzhu Rong occurred; Rong's younger cousin Shilong gathered Rong's followers and garrisoned Heqiao, returning to press the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Before he left, Erzhu Rong was killed and Shilong seized the capital.

sentences.zh: 孝莊親幸大夏門，集羣臣博議。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozhuang personally visited the Great Xia Gate and gathered ministers for wide deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozhuang held council at the Great Xia Gate.

sentences.zh: 百僚恇懼，計無所出。

translations.literal: The hundred officials were terrified and fearful, plans nowhere to be found.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were terrified and helpless.

sentences.zh: 苗獨奮衣而起曰：「今小賊唐突如此，朝廷有不測之危，正是忠臣烈士效節之日。

translations.literal: Miao alone flung his robes and rose, saying: "Now petty bandits intrude thus; the court has unforeseen peril—this is exactly the day for loyal ministers and heroic martyrs to offer their nodes."
translations.idiomatic: Only Miao stood and offered to strike.

sentences.zh: 臣雖不武，竊所庶幾。

translations.literal: "Your servant, though not martial, secretly aspires to it."
translations.idiomatic: "I am no warrior, but I will try."

sentences.zh: 請以一旅之眾，為陛下徑斷河梁。

translations.literal: "Please with one brigade's host, for Your Majesty directly cut Heqiao."
translations.idiomatic: "Give me a brigade to break Heqiao."

sentences.zh: 」城陽王徽、中尉高道穆讚成其計。

translations.literal: Prince of Chengyang Hui and Commandant of the Prohibitory Offices Gao Daomu praised and completed his plan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Hui and Gao Daomu backed him.

sentences.zh: 莊帝壯而許焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuang was stirred and permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 苗乃募人於馬渚上流以舟師夜下，去橋數里便放火船，河流既駛，倏忽而至。

translations.literal: Miao then recruited men at Mashu upstream with a river force to descend by night; several li from the bridge he at once set fire boats; the river current being swift, in an instant they arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Miao sent fire-ships downriver by night.

sentences.zh: 賊於南岸望見火下，相蹙爭橋，俄然橋絕，沒水死者甚眾。

translations.literal: The bandits on the south bank saw fire descending and crowded to contend for the bridge; soon the bridge broke and many drowned in the water.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels panicked on the bridge; it broke and many drowned.

sentences.zh: 苗身率士卒百許人泊於小渚以待南援。

translations.literal: Miao personally led more than a hundred soldiers to moor at a small islet awaiting southern relief.
translations.idiomatic: Miao waited on a shoal with a hundred men for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 既而官軍不至，賊乃涉水，與苗死鬬。

translations.literal: When official troops did not arrive, the bandits then waded the water and fought Miao to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Reinforcements never came; the rebels waded over and killed him fighting.

sentences.zh: 眾寡不敵，左右死盡，苗浮河而歿，時年四十六。

translations.literal: The crowd was few and could not match; attendants died completely; Miao floated the river and perished, aged forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: Outnumbered, he died in the river at forty-six.

sentences.zh: 帝聞苗死，哀傷久之，曰：「苗若不死，當應更立奇功。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard Miao had died he mourned long and said: "If Miao had not died, he should have again established special achievement."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned: "Had he lived, he would have done more."

sentences.zh: 」贈使持節、都督梁益巴東梁四州諸軍事、車騎大將軍、儀同三司、梁州刺史，河陽縣開國侯、邑一千戶，賵帛五百匹、粟五百石。

translations.literal: Posthumously given Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of military affairs of Liang, Yi, Ba, Eastern Liang, and Liang provinces, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Equal-in-Rank with the Three Excellencies, Governor of Liangzhou, Marquis of Heyang with a thousand households; condolence of five hundred bolts of silk and five hundred shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: He was richly honored posthumously as Marquis of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 諡忠烈侯。

translations.literal: Posthumous name Marquis Zhonglie.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Marquis Zhonglie (Loyal and Ardent).

sentences.zh: 苗少有節操，志尚功名。

translations.literal: Miao in youth had moral discipline and aspiration set on fame and achievement.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he sought honor.

sentences.zh: 每讀蜀書，見魏延請出長安，諸葛不許，常歎息謂亮無奇計。

translations.literal: Whenever he read the Shu chronicle and saw Wei Yan request to march out of Chang'an and Zhuge not permit it, he constantly sighed and said Liang had no wondrous plan.
translations.idiomatic: Reading of Zhuge Liang refusing Wei Yan's march, he sighed at missed chances.

sentences.zh: 及覽周瑜傳，未曾不咨嗟絕倒。

translations.literal: And whenever he read Zhou Yu's biography he never failed to sigh in admiration and fall back in wonder.
translations.idiomatic: He adored Zhou Yu's biography.

sentences.zh: 太保、城陽王徽，司徒、臨淮王彧重之，二王頗或不穆，苗每諫之。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Prince of Chengyang Hui and Minister of Education Prince of Huaihai Yu both valued him; the two princes at times were not harmonious—Miao often admonished them.
translations.idiomatic: He mediated between feuding princes Hui and Yu.

sentences.zh: 及徽寵勢隆極，猜忌彌甚。

translations.literal: When Hui's favor and power reached the extreme, suspicion grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Hui grew too powerful, Miao warned others:

sentences.zh: 苗謂人曰：「城陽蜂目先見，豺聲今轉彰矣。

translations.literal: Miao told people: "Prince of Chengyang has bee eyes that see first; jackal voice now turns more manifest."
translations.idiomatic: "Chengyang's bee eyes and jackal voice grow ominous."

sentences.zh: 」解鼓琴，好文詠，尺牘之敏，當世罕及。

translations.literal: He unstrung the zither, loved literary chant, and quickness in documents—rare in his age.
translations.idiomatic: He loved music, verse, and swift writing.

sentences.zh: 死之日，朝野悲壯之。

translations.literal: On the day of death court and countryside mourned his heroism.
translations.idiomatic: All mourned his death.

sentences.zh: 及莊帝幽崩，世隆入洛，主者追苗贈封，以白世隆。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang was secretly murdered Shilong entered Luoyang; the chief official pursued Miao's posthumous enfeoffment to report to Shilong.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor was murdered, officials sought to honor Miao before Shilong.

sentences.zh: 世隆曰：「吾爾時羣議，更一二日便欲大縱兵士焚燒都邑，任其採掠。

translations.literal: Shilong said: "At that time in group deliberation, in another day or two I was about to greatly release soldiers to burn the capital and let them plunder at will."
translations.idiomatic: Shilong said Miao had saved the capital from his planned sack.

sentences.zh: 賴苗京師獲全。

translations.literal: Thanks to Miao the capital was preserved whole.
translations.idiomatic: "Thanks to Miao the capital was saved."

sentences.zh: 天下之善一也。

translations.literal: One good deed under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: "That was a great good."

sentences.zh: 不宜追之。」

translations.literal: It is not fitting to pursue posthumous honor."
translations.idiomatic: "He needs no posthumous title."

sentences.zh: 子曇，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Tan inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tan inherited.

sentences.zh: 武定末，冀州儀同府刑獄參軍。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuding he was Punishments Staff Adviser of Yizhou's Equal-in-Rank Office.
translations.idiomatic: Tan served in Yizhou at the end of Wuding.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，爵例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, his rank was reduced by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi took the throne his title was reduced.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：壽春形勝，南鄭要險，乃建鄴之肩髀，成都之喉嗌。

translations.literal: The historian says: Shouchun's strategic advantage, Nanzheng's strategic peril—are the shoulder and arm of Jiankang, the throat of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Shouchun and Nanzheng were keys to Jiankang and Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 裴叔業、夏侯道遷，體運知機，翻然鵲起，舉地而來，功誠兩茂。

translations.literal: Pei Shuye and Xiahou Daoqian, embodying fortune and knowing the moment, loftily rose like magpies, raising land as they came—merit and sincerity both lush.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Shuye and Xiahou Daoqian seized their moment and defected with splendid merit.

sentences.zh: 其所以大啟茅賦，兼列旐旟，固其宜矣。

translations.literal: Therefore greatly to open enfeoffments of thatch and rank together with banners—indeed it was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Grand rewards suited their service.

sentences.zh: 植不恒其德，器小志大，斯所以顛覆也。

translations.literal: Zhi did not keep his virtue; vessel small, ambition large—this is why he was overthrown.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zhi's small character brought his fall.

sentences.zh: 衍才行將略，不遂其終，惜哉！

translations.literal: Yan's talent, conduct, stratagem, and overview did not reach their end—pity!
translations.idiomatic: Yan died before his promise was fulfilled—pity!

sentences.zh: 李、席、王、江雖復因人成事，亦為果決之士。

translations.literal: Li, Xi, Wang, and Jiang though again accomplished affairs through others were also men of resolute decision.
translations.idiomatic: Li, Xi, Wang, and Jiang were decisive even when riding others' success.

sentences.zh: 淳于誕好立功名，有志者竟能遂也。

translations.literal: Chunyu Yan loved to establish fame and achievement—men of will can after all succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Chunyu Yan's ambition was fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 李苗以文武幹局，沉斷過人，臨難慨然，奮其大節，蹈忠履義，歿而後已。

translations.literal: Li Miao with civil and military capacity and overview, calm judgment surpassing others—in facing difficulty he was impassioned, exerting his great node; treading loyalty and fulfilling righteousness, he died and then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Li Miao died loyal at Heqiao—courage matched his gifts.

sentences.zh: 仁必有勇，其斯人之謂乎！

translations.literal: Benevolence surely has courage—is it not men like these!
translations.idiomatic: Truly, benevolence and courage met in such men.

translations.literal: Although called Zhongda's urgent rebuke: According to "名" it should be the error for "召"; below impeaching Pei Zhi "summoned Zhongda to question and he would not inform" can verify.

translations.idiomatic: Dian and Ju editions follow the flawed Bei text.

translations.literal: The nineteen characters wrongly inserted in the north edition are in fact not language from the memorial table, but belong below "bareheaded and barefoot he apologized" and above the sentence "when at Shouyang."
translations.idiomatic: Those nineteen characters belong to the court apology scene, not to the memorial.

sentences.zh: 由於錯簡，「謝曰」的「曰」字錯到上文去了，故北本又於「謝」下增一「曰」字。

translations.literal: Because of misplaced text "曰" of "謝曰" went upward; Bei edition also added "曰" under "謝".
translations.idiomatic: Because of the displaced passage, the yue character of "apologized saying" was moved upward; the north edition therefore added another yue under "apologized."

sentences.zh: 今據冊府乙正北、殿、局三本十九字的錯簡，並刪所增「曰」字。

translations.literal: Now according to Cefu correct Bei, Dian, Ju three editions' nineteen-character error and delete added "曰".
translations.idiomatic: Editions corrected accordingly.

sentences.zh: 稍遷至安豐新蔡二郡太守建安戍主 按下云「蕭寶卷遣胡景略代之」，則景略之官即同法友。

translations.literal: Soon moved to Anfeng and New Cai two commanderies Administrator Jian'an garrison commander: Below says "Baojuan sent Hu Jinglue to replace him"—Jinglue's office same as Fayou.
translations.idiomatic: On Fayou's posts: Jinglue held the same posts.

sentences.zh: 南齊書卷五七魏虜傳稱「席法友攻北新蔡、安豐二郡太守胡景略於建安城」。

translations.literal: Southern Qi Book 57 Wei captives says "Xi Fayou attacked Beixin Cai and Anfeng Administrator Hu Jinglue at Jian'an city."
translations.idiomatic: Southern Qi confirms Beixin Cai.

sentences.zh: 「新蔡」上有「北」字。

translations.literal: On "New Cai" there should be the character "North."
translations.idiomatic: "North" is missing before New Cai.

sentences.zh: 南齊書卷一四州郡志豫州有北新蔡、安豐二郡。

translations.literal: Southern Qi Book 14 Province and Commandery Annals of Yuzhou has Northern New Cai and Anfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Qi annals list Northern New Cai and Anfeng.

sentences.zh: 這裏「新蔡」上當脫「北」字。

translations.literal: Here above "New Cai" the character "North" should be missing.
translations.idiomatic: The text should read Northern New Cai.

sentences.zh: 天平中 諸本「天」作「太」，北史卷四五江悅之傳作「天」。

translations.literal: Tianping era: All editions "天" as "太"; Beishi Jiang Yuezhi biography has "天."
translations.idiomatic: On "in the Tianping era": editions wrongly read tai for tian; the Beishi biography of Jiang Yuezhi has tian.

sentences.zh: 按魏無「太平」年號，下稱「元象中」，顯為「天平」之訛，今據改。

translations.literal: Wei has no "Taiping" era title; below says "Yuanxiang"—clearly error for Tianping—now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Wei has no Taiping era title; below says Yuanxiang, clearly an error for Tianping—now corrected.

sentences.zh: 時有潁川庾道者 諸本「道」作「導」，北史卷四五江悅之傳作「道」。

translations.literal: At that time Yingchuan Yu Daozhe: All editions "道" as "導"; Beishi Jiang Yuezhi has "道."
translations.idiomatic: On "Yu Daozhe of Yingchuan": all editions read dao as the alternate graph dao-with-hand; Beishi Jiang Yuezhi biography has dao.

sentences.zh: 按上夏侯夬傳內也作「道」。

translations.literal: Above in Xiahou Gui biography also has "道."
translations.idiomatic: Consistent with Gui biography.

sentences.zh: 北史夬傳作「遵」，當是「導」之訛。

translations.literal: Beishi Gui biography has "遵"—should be error for "導."
translations.idiomatic: The Beishi Gui biography reads zun, which should be an error for dao-with-hand.

sentences.zh: 「道」「導」本一字，今統一作「道」。

translations.literal: "道" and "導" originally one character—now unified as "道."
translations.idiomatic: Dao and dao-with-hand were originally one character—now unified as dao.

sentences.zh: 或家安固之桓陵縣 諸本及北史卷四五淳于誕傳「固」都作「國」。

translations.literal: Or family in Anguo's Huanling county: All editions and Beishi Chunyu Yan "固" all as "國."
translations.idiomatic: On "or the family was in Huanling county of Anguo": all editions and Beishi Chunyu Yan read guo for gu (solid).

translations.idiomatic: Hongshi Kaoyi notes the place-name issue.

translations.idiomatic: 〈Volume 15〉

translations.literal: Yizhou Anguo commandery had Huanling county; "Anguo" is the error for "Anguo"—"國" character erroneous, now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo commandery had Huanling county; Anguo is the error for Anguo—the character guo is erroneous, now corrected.

translations.idiomatic: Song Shu confirms Anguo and Huanling.

sentences.zh: 「國」字訛，今改正。

translations.literal: The character "國" is erroneous; now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: The character guo is erroneous; now corrected to gu.

translations.literal: And when fire rose: All editions "起" as "赴"; only Ju edition has "起."
translations.idiomatic: On "when fire rose in time": all editions read fu for qi; only the Ju edition has qi.

translations.idiomatic: Correctly has qi; now follow the Ju edition.

translations.literal: Miao adopted by paternal uncle Lue: Beishi Li Miao biography "略" as "畎."
translations.idiomatic: On "Miao was adopted by paternal uncle Lue": Beishi Li Miao biography reads quan for lue.

sentences.zh: 按卷六五邢巒傳也作「畎」，疑「略」乃「畎」之訛。

translations.literal: According to vol. 65 Xing Luan biography also has "畎"—suspect "略" is error for "畎."
translations.idiomatic: According to vol. 65 Xing Luan biography it also reads quan; suspect lue is an error for quan.
